myths.name: 中国神话
myths.subtitle: 在山海与星河之间，重绘天地初形
myths.description: 中国神话并非一部统一经典，而是先秦典籍、地方祭祀与历代讲述交织成的广阔谱系。从女娲补天到昆仑仙境，人、神与山川彼此感应，天地秩序也在灾变后重新建立。不同年代的记载常有分歧，民间信仰与文学改写又不断赋予古老形象新的生命。
myths.era: 先秦已有文字记载，后世持续传承与重述
myths.quote: 天有裂隙，仍有人拾起五色的光。

gods.name: 女娲
gods.title: 造人与补天的神圣者
gods.desc: 在不同文献中承担造人、补天与维系秩序的角色。她的蛇身形象及与伏羲的关系，随时代与地域而变化。

gods.name: 伏羲
gods.title: 文明技艺的开创者
gods.desc: 常与八卦、结网和婚姻制度的起源相联系。汉代图像中多与女娲相对，呈现人首蛇身的神圣形态。

gods.name: 西王母
gods.title: 昆仑与不死之境的主宰
gods.desc: 早期记载带有威严而异质的形貌，后来逐渐成为仙界尊神。她与不死药、昆仑及群仙会聚密切相连。

stories.title: 女娲补天
stories.summary: 天柱倾折，洪水与烈火侵扰人间。女娲炼五色石补天、断鳌足立四极，以一连串修复行动，使濒于崩坏的天地重新容纳生命。
paragraphs: 《淮南子》描绘过一个秩序破碎的世界：四极废坏，九州裂开，火焰不熄，洪水不止，猛兽威胁生民。这里的灾难不只是一次暴雨，而是支撑生活的天地结构同时失灵，连日常赖以存在的边界也变得不再可靠。
女娲于是炼五色石修补苍天，又断巨鳌之足支立四极，止息洪水，清除危害。故事没有把创造限定为开天辟地的一瞬；在世界受损以后，重新支撑它、让众生得以安居，同样是一种艰难而重要的创造。
后世常把这段叙事与共工触山等故事连接，形成更完整的灾变起因，但古代文献并不总按同一顺序讲述。五色石由此成为修复与承担的意象：天地未必天然完满，秩序也需要神圣者以行动重新缝合。

stories.title: 羿射九日
stories.summary: 十日并出使草木枯焦，羿持弓射落多余的太阳，留下日光照耀人间。不同版本为这场行动安排了各异的背景与后续命运。
paragraphs: 在与扶桑、羲和相关的太阳叙事中，十个太阳本有轮流运行的秩序。当它们一齐升上天空，过量的光便成为灾祸：田禾枯槁，草木焦灼，人们失去生存所需的阴凉与水分，世界被迫面对失去节律的力量。
羿以善射回应这场危机。流传甚广的讲法让他射落九个太阳，只留一个维持白昼；较早文献对射日数量与情节的表达并不完全相同。弓箭在这里并非只为征服，而是为过度炽烈的天象重新划定尺度。
羿的故事还与除害、求取不死药和嫦娥奔月相连，但这些情节来自多层累积，不能当作一份毫无差异的古代定本。后世亦常混用羿与夏代后羿的名称，阅读时须留意神话射手与历史传说人物的区别。

stories.title: 盘古开天
stories.summary: 混沌如鸡卵，盘古在其中孕育，醒来后使天地分开，又以成长的身躯撑住天地。后世记载把他的身体化作山川日月，讲述世界从混沌走向秩序。
paragraphs: 在三国时期徐整《三五历纪》的佚文中，天地尚未分开，整个世界混沌得如同一枚鸡卵，盘古就在其中孕育。经过一万八千年，天地开始开辟：轻清的阳气上升成为天空，重浊的阴气下沉成为大地。盘古居于两者之间，新的世界还在不断变化。
天地分开以后，并没有立刻成为今天的模样。记载说，天每天升高一丈，地每天增厚一丈，盘古也每天长高一丈。这样的变化又持续了一万八千年，天终于极高，地也极深。盘古的身体随着天地一同成长，构成了这段开天叙事的主要过程。
另一部题为《五运历年纪》的佚文接着描绘盘古死后的变化：气息成为风云，声音成为雷霆，双眼成为日月，血液成为江河，毛发成为草木。这些古籍残文由后书保存，细节不尽相同；流行图画里的巨斧劈天，并不是上述早期记载的核心情节。

en.title: Pangu Separates Heaven and Earth
en.summary: Within a universe resembling an egg, Pangu grows as heaven and earth separate. Early surviving quotations describe his immense growth; another account transforms his body into the natural world. The familiar axe belongs to later popular retellings rather than these early passages.
paragraphs: In surviving quotations from Xu Zheng’s third-century account, the universe begins in a confused state resembling a chicken’s egg. Pangu develops within it for eighteen thousand years. When heaven and earth begin to separate, the clear, light principle rises to become heaven, while the heavy, turbid principle settles as earth. Pangu remains between them as the newly divided cosmos continues to change.

The separation is not immediately complete. Each day heaven rises one measure, earth thickens by another, and Pangu grows by the same amount. This extraordinary process continues for another eighteen thousand years, until heaven stands immensely high and earth extends immensely deep. Rather than describing a single stroke with a weapon, this early passage presents creation as a sustained process of cosmic growth.

A separate surviving passage, attributed to the Record of the Five Cycles, describes transformations at Pangu’s death. His breath becomes wind and clouds, his voice thunder, his eyes the sun and moon, and his blood rivers. These texts survive through later quotations and differ in detail. The giant axe familiar from modern illustrations is not central to the early passages summarized here.

stories.title: 女娲造人
stories.summary: 天地已有万物，却还没有人。女娲抟黄土塑成人形，又把绳子拖过泥浆，创造出更多的人。古代记载还借两种造人方法解释社会身份差异，留下时代印记。
paragraphs: 东汉应劭《风俗通义》的佚文说，天地开辟以后，还没有人类。女娲于是取来黄土，亲手揉捏，做出了人的形状。一个个泥人由她的手中诞生，原本没有人烟的世界开始有了人群。这不是补天故事的接续，而是一则独立解释人类从何而来的传说。
然而，天下如此广大，只靠逐个捏塑，女娲忙碌许久仍觉力不从心。她改用绳子，把它放进泥浆，再提起挥动，让泥点落下成为人。这样，细细抟土与绳引泥浆两种做法共同出现在记载中，故事也由缓慢的手工创造转入迅速繁衍人群的过程。
佚文最后把手抟黄土的人说成富贵者，把绳上泥点化成的人说成贫贱者。这反映古人借神话解释等级的观念，并不是现代人的价值判断。原文没有给泥人安排姓名，也没有写入后世常见的吹气细节；女娲完成造人，空寂的天地从此有了人类。

en.title: Nüwa Makes Human Beings
en.summary: Finding a world without people, Nüwa shapes human figures from yellow earth. When the work becomes exhausting, she uses a cord dipped in mud to make more. The ancient account also attaches a historically revealing explanation of social rank to her methods.
paragraphs: A passage preserved from Ying Shao’s Eastern Han work, Comprehensive Discussions of Customs, begins after heaven and earth have opened. There are still no human beings. Nüwa takes yellow earth and kneads it into human forms with her own hands. People begin to inhabit the previously empty world. This is an independent account of human origins, not a continuation of her repair of heaven.

The world is vast, however, and shaping every person individually proves too demanding. Nüwa changes her method. She draws a cord through mud and lifts it, producing further people from the scattered material. The account contrasts careful molding with this quicker technique. Its action turns on a practical difficulty within creation: how one maker can populate an entire world without endlessly repeating the same labor.

The surviving passage then associates hand-molded people with the wealthy and noble, and people made from the cord’s mud with the poor. That explanation reflects an ancient hierarchical worldview, not a judgment readers must accept. The text supplies neither individual names nor the breath animation common in some later retellings. Its conclusion is simpler: the once unpeopled world now contains humanity.

stories.title: 嫦娥奔月
stories.summary: 羿从西王母那里求得不死药，嫦娥却取药独自升入月中。早期记载留下了分离与长生的代价，后世又发展出月宫、玉兔和中秋相望等不同故事。
paragraphs: 西汉《淮南子》记载，羿向西王母求得了不死之药。药能带来超越凡人的生命，却也成了夫妻之间命运的转折。文本中的嫦娥取走了这份药，故事随即由人间转向遥远的月亮。早期原文十分简短，并没有交代羿如何求药，也没有描写盛大的赠药仪式。
嫦娥服药之后奔向月亮，离开了羿所在的人间。《淮南子》用这场突变说明，得到长生之物，并不等于能够始终拥有它。她并非在这部书中迎战追兵，也没有被写成替众人守护仙药；后世流传的逢蒙逼药等情节，属于另外发展的叙事版本。
汉代其他材料还说嫦娥在月中化为蟾蜍，后来的文学则更常把她想象成独居月宫的仙子。两种形象不宜当成同一篇古文里的连续经历。共同的结局是她留在月中，与人间隔开；圆月因而既令人向往，也让读故事的人想到团聚、孤独与离别。

en.title: Chang’e Flies to the Moon
en.summary: Yi obtains an immortality drug from the Queen Mother of the West, but Chang’e takes it and departs for the moon. Early accounts emphasize an irreversible separation; later traditions develop different lunar identities and motives for her departure.
paragraphs: The second-century BCE Huainanzi says that Yi obtained a drug of immortality from the Queen Mother of the West. Its extraordinary promise becomes the turning point in his household. Chang’e takes the medicine, and the narrative moves from the human world toward the moon. The early passage is very brief: it does not describe Yi’s journey to obtain the drug or an elaborate presentation ceremony.

After taking the medicine, Chang’e flees to the moon, leaving the world in which Yi remains. The Huainanzi uses this reversal to suggest that acquiring something precious does not guarantee keeping it. This account does not portray her resisting an attacker or protecting the medicine for others. The familiar episode involving Peng Meng’s attempted theft belongs to a different, later development of the story.

Other Han sources describe Chang’e becoming a toad in the moon, while later literature more often imagines a beautiful immortal dwelling in a lunar palace. These are alternative developments, not necessarily consecutive events in one ancient text. Across the traditions, her departure creates a lasting distance from earthly life. The moon consequently becomes an image of longing as well as immortality and separation.

stories.title: 大禹治水
stories.summary: 洪水久困大地，鲧治水未成，禹继承重任，奔走山川开通水道。他让河流入海，使百姓重新耕种生活，三过家门而不入的记述也传扬着他的劳苦。
paragraphs: 上古洪水漫过田野，百姓难以安居，鲧受命治理，却多年没有成功。禹继承这项重任时，面对的不只是一处决口，而是山川之间失去秩序的水患。《史记》写他与益、后稷等人一同奔走，察看土地与水势，为恢复人们的生活寻找可以实行的办法。
禹在陆地乘车，涉水乘船，翻山则使用适合山行的工具，沿途疏通河流、引导积水。他让阻塞的水道彼此连通，使大水有路流向江海；又随土地高下安排贡赋与物产。治水并非一挥神力便告完成，而是长久勘察、劳作与组织众人共同承担的过程。
水患渐平，低地重新可以耕种，人们得以回到可以生活的土地。《孟子》特别说禹在外八年，三次经过家门都没有进去；其他古书对年数另有说法。故事把治水的成果与他的克己联系起来，最终禹因功德受到推举，成为夏代开国叙事中的关键人物。

en.title: Yu Brings the Floodwaters Under Control
en.summary: After Gun fails to control devastating floods, Yu surveys mountains and waterways, opening channels that carry water toward the sea. Farming and settlement become possible again. Different ancient texts describe his labor and the personal sacrifices associated with it.
paragraphs: Floodwaters cover the fields, leaving people unable to settle securely. Gun is assigned to control them, but his efforts fail over many years. Yu inherits a problem extending across mountains, plains, and rivers rather than a single broken bank. In Sima Qian’s Records of the Grand Historian, he works alongside figures including Yi and Houji, examining the land and seeking ways to restore ordinary life.

Yu travels by carriage on dry ground, by boat over water, and with special equipment through the mountains. He opens obstructed waterways and guides accumulated water into connected channels leading toward the seas. His work also involves understanding soils, resources, and regional obligations. The achievement is not an instantaneous magical gesture, but an extended undertaking of travel, observation, physical effort, and coordinated human labor.

As the waters subside, land becomes available for farming and communities can recover. Mencius singles out Yu’s self-denial: during eight years away, he passes his own doorway three times without entering. Other ancient accounts give different durations, so their chronologies should not be merged uncritically. The tradition links practical success with service, leading eventually to Yu’s elevation within accounts of the founding of Xia.

cosmos.name: 昆仑
cosmos.desc: 古代神话中的神山与通天之所，常关联西王母；各典籍对其方位、层级与景观描述不尽相同。

cosmos.name: 扶桑
cosmos.desc: 与东方日出相关的神木，太阳栖息或起行于此；它让天体运行呈现可被想象的空间路径。

cosmos.name: 四极
cosmos.desc: 支撑并界定天地秩序的边缘结构，常在灾变叙事中显现，不宜直接等同现代地理坐标。

myths.note: 本条兼及古代文献与后世传播，不代表中国各民族神话的总和。女娲、西王母等也属于部分地区的活态祭祀传统；文学形象、道教神谱与地方信仰须分别理解。

myths.name: 日本神话
myths.subtitle: 神岛浮起，日光重返林间与人世
myths.description: 日本神话以《古事记》《日本书纪》等文本中的国土生成与诸神故事广为人知，也与神社祭祀、地方风土记和口传传统相互交织。天照大神、须佐之男与伊邪那岐的行动连接天上、海原和黄泉。诸神并非全然一致的家谱，异文与地方传统始终并存。
myths.era: 八世纪文献集中编录，更早祭祀与口传延续至今
myths.quote: 当岩门微启，晨光便有了归途。

gods.name: 天照大神
gods.title: 照临高天原的太阳神
gods.desc: 在主要编纂神话中居于核心，与神镜及王权叙事相连。各地神社的祭祀理解不能完全归于单一故事。

gods.name: 须佐之男
gods.title: 越界而又除害的神
gods.desc: 兼有猛烈、失序与保护者的不同面向。他在高天原造成危机，也在出云斩蛇救人，呈现复杂性格。

gods.name: 伊邪那岐
gods.title: 生成国土与行禊的神
gods.desc: 与伊邪那美共同参与国土与诸神的生成。离开黄泉后的净化，成为理解神圣洁净的重要叙事背景。

stories.title: 天岩户前的笑声
stories.summary: 天照因须佐之男的暴行藏入岩户，世界陷入昏暗。诸神以镜、仪式与笑声引她探看，终于使太阳重新照临天上与人间。
paragraphs: 须佐之男在高天原的破坏引起严重混乱，天照大神遂退入天岩户。日光隐没后，天上与人间一同陷入黑暗，灾异随之而来。神话将太阳的缺席写成社会与自然秩序的同时受损，而不只是天空颜色的一次改变。
众神聚集商议，在岩户前安排神镜、玉饰与祭仪。天宇受卖的舞动引得诸神大笑，岩内的天照因好奇而开门。她看见镜中的光辉，又被引向门外，众神随即以界绳阻止她再次退入，世界由此恢复明亮。
这一故事呈现协作、表演与神圣器物共同恢复秩序的力量，也为若干仪式传统提供解释资源。不过，后世的神乐、神镜信仰和地方祭典有各自发展，不能把今日所有仪式都说成对这段神话的直接复制。

stories.title: 八岐大蛇与稻田姬
stories.summary: 被逐离高天原的须佐之男来到出云，得知少女将遭八岐大蛇吞食。他设下烈酒之计斩杀大蛇，并在蛇尾发现一柄宝剑。
paragraphs: 须佐之男来到出云，遇见为女儿哭泣的老夫妇。他们说，八岐大蛇每年吞食一个女儿，如今只剩栉名田比卖，也常译作奇稻田姬。大蛇拥有八头八尾，身躯绵延山谷，其巨大形象让威胁超出了普通野兽的尺度。
须佐之男安排酿造浓烈的酒，并设置让大蛇各头饮酒的容器。待它沉醉，他挥剑斩杀，在尾部发现异样的宝剑，后来与草薙剑的传承相联系。曾经造成破坏的神，在此显现保护婚姻、土地与生活的另一面。
故事常被联系到河流、洪患或冶铁文化，但这些解释属于研究视角，并非文本明确说明的唯一原义。《古事记》与《日本书纪》的细节也有差异；将它放回出云的地景与神社传统，才能看见更丰富的地方意义。

stories.title: 伊邪那岐访黄泉
stories.summary: 伊邪那美死后，伊邪那岐追到黄泉求她归来，却违背约定点火窥看。他逃过追逐，以巨石封住两界通道，夫妻的争执成为解释生死消长的一段神话。
paragraphs: 《古事记》中，伊邪那美因生下火神而死，伊邪那岐不愿失去妻子，追到黄泉国请求她回来。她说自己已经吃过黄泉的食物，仍愿去同黄泉诸神商量，却叮嘱他不可窥看。伊邪那岐在外等候许久，终于失去耐心，折下发梳的一枚齿，点燃照明。
火光照出了伊邪那美腐败的身体，以及依附其上的雷神。伊邪那岐惊恐逃跑，受辱的伊邪那美派黄泉丑女追赶。他先抛出发饰，再掷下梳齿，分别化作葡萄与竹笋，使追者停下取食。后来面对更多追兵，他又在黄泉坂用桃子将他们击退，争得逃离的机会。
最后伊邪那美亲自追来，伊邪那岐搬来巨石堵住黄泉坂，两人在石头两边诀别。她宣告每天夺去人间一千人的生命，他回应每天建立一千五百间产屋。故事由寻妻转为生死分界；伊邪那岐随后洗去黄泉污秽，那又开启了诞生新神的另一段叙事。

en.title: Izanagi Visits the Land of the Dead
en.summary: Seeking his dead wife, Izanagi enters Yomi and promises not to look at her. His broken promise brings horror and pursuit. A boulder finally separates the couple, whose exchange explains the continuing balance of human deaths and births.
paragraphs: In the Kojiki, Izanami dies after bearing the fire deity. Unwilling to lose her, Izanagi travels to Yomi and asks her to return. She explains that she has already eaten its food, but agrees to consult the deities there. He must not look at her while she does so. After waiting impatiently, he breaks a tooth from his comb and lights it.

The flame reveals Izanami’s decaying body and the thunder deities attached to it. Izanagi flees in terror. Humiliated, she sends pursuers after him. He throws down his headdress and then his comb, which become grapes and bamboo shoots that delay the pursuing women as they eat. At the slope leading out of Yomi, he also uses peaches to repel a further supernatural force.

Izanami herself finally pursues him, but Izanagi blocks the passage with an enormous boulder. Speaking from opposite sides, they end their marriage. She declares that she will kill a thousand people each day; he answers that he will establish fifteen hundred birth houses. The rescue has become a permanent boundary. His subsequent purification from Yomi’s pollution begins a separate sequence of divine births.

stories.title: 因幡白兔与大国主
stories.summary: 白兔欺骗海兽搭桥，受伤后又被众神兄弟误导。背负行李的大穴牟迟教它用清水和蒲黄疗伤，白兔遂预言八上姬会选择这位后来称作大国主的神。
paragraphs: 《古事记》说，一只兔子想从淤岐渡到因幡，便哄海中的ワニ排成一列，说要替双方数一数谁的族类更多。它踩着它们的背过海，接近岸边时却得意泄露了骗局。最后一只海兽扯掉它的皮，兔子受伤伏在岬角；这种海兽究竟指鲨还是鳄，解释并不一致。
前去向八上姬求婚的众兄弟经过，看见受伤的兔子，竟教它用海水洗身，再躺到高处迎风吹干。兔子照做，盐水与风使伤口更加疼痛。替兄长们背负行李、落在后面的大穴牟迟随后来到，没有取笑它，而是停下来询问经过，听完了它渡海受伤的事情。
大穴牟迟让兔子用河口的清水洗净身体，铺开蒲草的花粉，再在上面翻滚。兔子依言而行，恢复了原来的模样，便告诉他：八上姬不会选择那些兄弟，而会选择你。预言随后应验；这位当时地位卑微的行李背负者，正是后来广为人知的大国主神。

en.title: The Hare of Inaba and Ōkuninushi
en.summary: A hare tricks sea creatures into forming a bridge and suffers a terrible injury. Cruel advice worsens its condition, but a burdened younger brother offers an effective remedy. The grateful hare predicts that Princess Yagami will choose him.
paragraphs: The Kojiki tells of a hare seeking passage from Oki to Inaba. Claiming it wants to count their numbers, it persuades sea creatures called wani to form a line. It crosses on their backs, then boasts about its trick before reaching safety. The last creature strips off its skin. Scholars differ over whether wani here should be understood as crocodiles, sharks, or other creatures.

A group of divine brothers passes on the way to court Princess Yagami. They advise the injured hare to bathe in seawater and dry itself in the wind. Following their instructions only increases its pain. Their younger brother, Ōnamuchi, arrives later because he carries their luggage. Instead of mocking the animal, he stops and listens to how the crossing and injury occurred.

Ōnamuchi tells the hare to wash in fresh water at the river mouth, spread cattail pollen on the ground, and roll in it. The hare follows this treatment and recovers its former appearance. It then predicts that Princess Yagami will reject the brothers and choose their mistreated luggage carrier. The prediction comes true; this younger deity is later widely known as Ōkuninushi.

stories.title: 天孙降临
stories.summary: 苇原中国平定后，天照大神派孙子邇邇艺命降临。天宇受卖与猿田彦在岔路相遇，众神携镜、剑、玉同行，最终抵达日向高千穗，建立地上的居所。
paragraphs: 《古事记》的叙事中，天上诸神先遣使者平定苇原中国，随后准备让天照大神的后裔前往治理。受命的天忍穗耳命报告，自己在准备期间已有儿子出生，建议改派这名孩子。于是，邇邇艺命领受使命，带着随行诸神，准备从高天原走向地上的国土。
出发之际，天上与地上相接的岔路出现一位光耀的神，挡在前方。天宇受卖命奉命上前问话，得知他是猿田彦神，专来迎接并引导天孙。队伍还带着镜、剑与勾玉；天照特别嘱咐，要如同敬奉自己一般敬奉那面镜子，让降临同时承载祭祀的职责。
邇邇艺命拨开重叠的云层，降到日向的高千穗，随后寻找适合居住的地方，在笠沙一带建立宫室。天孙终于由天界进入地上，随行诸神也各有职司。《日本书纪》另存多个降临版本，地点与细节有所差异；这里依《古事记》的线索讲述，不把诸本拼成一路。

en.title: The Heavenly Grandchild Descends
en.summary: After the earthly realm is pacified, Amaterasu sends her grandson Ninigi to govern it. Divine companions bear sacred objects, and Sarutahiko offers guidance. The party descends to Takachiho in Himuka before establishing a dwelling in the earthly land.
paragraphs: In the Kojiki, heavenly envoys first secure the submission of the Central Land of Reed Plains. Amaterasu’s descendant is then to govern it. Ame-no-Oshihomimi reports that a son has been born while preparations were underway and proposes that the child go instead. Ninigi receives the commission and prepares to leave the heavenly plain, accompanied by deities assigned to assist the new undertaking.

At the crossroads between heaven and earth, a radiant deity appears before the travelers. Ame-no-Uzume goes forward to question him. He identifies himself as Sarutahiko and explains that he has come to guide the heavenly grandchild. The company carries a mirror, sword, and curved jewels. Amaterasu particularly commands that the mirror be honored as her own presence, linking the journey with ritual responsibility.

Ninigi pushes through the layers of cloud and descends to Takachiho in Himuka. He subsequently seeks a suitable dwelling place and establishes a palace in the region of Kasasa. The transition from heaven to an earthly residence is complete. The Nihon Shoki preserves several alternative descent accounts with differing locations and details; this telling follows the Kojiki rather than combining all their routes.

stories.title: 海幸山幸
stories.summary: 山幸借用兄长海幸的鱼钩，却不慎将它遗失。他沿海寻钩，进入海神宫廷并迎娶丰玉姬；寻回鱼钩后，借潮水宝珠化解兄长的攻击，使争执终于平息。
paragraphs: 海幸善捕鱼，弟弟山幸善打猎，兄弟交换用具试试彼此的本领。山幸却弄丢了借来的鱼钩，纵然把佩剑打成许多新钩赔偿，兄长仍坚持要回原物。山幸在海边哭泣，遇到盐椎神指路，乘编成的小舟前往海神宫殿，坐到井边树上，等待新的转机。
海神之女丰玉姬发现了这位来客，海神接待他，并把女儿嫁给他。山幸在海宫住了三年，想起失钩才叹息说明原委。海神召集鱼群询问，得知一条鲷鱼喉中有异物，取出后果然是鱼钩。临别时，海神又交给山幸能够使潮水涨落的两颗宝珠。
山幸回到陆地，把鱼钩还给兄长，兄长后来仍向他发难。他依海神所教，举起涨潮珠，潮水涌来，逼得海幸求饶；再以退潮珠令水消去。兄长终于承诺臣服，兄弟争端得到收束。此处依《古事记》主线讲述，海神女儿分娩等后续另属故事的下一段。

en.title: The Sea Luck and the Mountain Luck
en.summary: A hunter loses the fishing hook borrowed from his elder brother and journeys to the sea god’s palace to recover it. Marriage, a gathering of fish, and two tide controlling jewels transform his desperate search into a reversal of power.
paragraphs: The elder brother prospers through fishing, the younger through hunting. They exchange equipment, but the younger loses his brother’s hook. He offers many replacements made from his own sword, yet the elder insists on the original. Weeping beside the sea, the younger meets Shiotsuchi, who provides directions and a small woven vessel. It carries him toward the sea god’s palace and a tree beside its well.

Toyotama-hime, the sea god’s daughter, discovers the visitor. Her father welcomes him and gives them in marriage. After three years, the younger brother remembers the missing hook and explains his sorrow. The sea god assembles the fish, and a hook is recovered from a sea bream’s throat. Before the visitor returns home, he also receives jewels that control the rising and falling tide.

The recovered hook is returned, but the elder brother subsequently attacks. Following the sea god’s instructions, the younger raises the tide jewel, and water threatens to engulf his opponent. When the elder begs for mercy, he lowers the water with its companion jewel. The elder finally promises submission. This follows the Kojiki narrative; Toyotama-hime’s later childbirth belongs to the subsequent episode rather than this resolution.

cosmos.name: 高天原
cosmos.desc: 诸天津神活动的天上领域，与地上世界发生往来；它的性质并非现代天文学意义的太空。

cosmos.name: 苇原中国
cosmos.desc: 神话中人间国土的称谓之一，常与国土生成和让国故事相连；此处的中国并非现代国名。

cosmos.name: 黄泉
cosmos.desc: 伊邪那美所在的死亡领域，与生者世界存在危险边界，不宜简单套用善恶报应式的地狱观。

myths.note: 本条以古代编纂神话为主；神道是活态宗教实践，地方神社传统远比此处广泛。阿伊努、琉球等传统具有独立脉络，不应自动并入这套诸神叙事。

myths.name: 希腊神话
myths.subtitle: 群山之上，神与命运彼此凝望
myths.description: 希腊神话经由史诗、赞歌、戏剧和城邦祭祀保存下来，并没有唯一权威的定本。奥林匹斯诸神拥有鲜明欲望，英雄则在荣耀、亲缘与限度之间行走。神谱解释宇宙与权力的更替，地方传说连接具体山川，也让同一位神在不同城邦呈现不同面貌。
myths.era: 古风至古典时期文本丰富，更早传统可追溯至青铜时代
myths.quote: 海风吹过神殿，凡人的名字仍在回响。

gods.name: 宙斯
gods.title: 天空、雷霆与王权之神
gods.desc: 奥林匹斯秩序的主要统治者，也与誓言、宾客和正义相关。他的权力始终置于复杂亲缘与命运之中。

gods.name: 雅典娜
gods.title: 智慧、技艺与城邦守护神
gods.desc: 关联审慎的战争策略、织造和多种技艺。她与雅典关系尤深，却并非只在一座城邦受到敬奉。

gods.name: 德墨忒尔
gods.title: 谷物与土地丰饶之神
gods.desc: 掌管农作物生长，与女儿珀耳塞福涅的离合构成重要神话，也与厄琉西斯的宗教仪式密切相关。

stories.title: 普罗米修斯取火
stories.summary: 普罗米修斯为人类取得被宙斯扣留的火种，因而承受长期惩罚。不同诗人与剧作家让这次越界呈现出欺计、慈悲或反抗的意味。
paragraphs: 在赫西俄德的叙事中，普罗米修斯曾以分配祭肉的计谋欺骗宙斯，神与人的关系因此趋于紧张。宙斯扣下火，不让凡人轻易获得它。火于是既是烹饪、温暖与技艺的条件，也是双方权力关系的一处关键界线。
普罗米修斯把火藏在中空的茴香茎中带回人间，越过了这条界线。惩罚随之降下：他被束缚，遭鹰反复啄食肝脏。在不同作品里，人类得到的礼物和由此承受的苦难相互牵连，文明的开端并不显得轻松。
后来的悲剧传统让普罗米修斯更鲜明地成为人类技艺与希望的援助者，但这不等于所有古希腊作者都把他写成同一种英雄。阅读不同版本，可以看见同一束火如何同时照出神权、计谋、责任与抗争的面孔。

stories.title: 珀耳塞福涅的归期
stories.summary: 珀耳塞福涅被哈得斯带往冥界，德墨忒尔在寻女中停止赐予丰收。诸神达成安排，女儿在两个领域之间往返，土地也重新生长。
paragraphs: 《致德墨忒尔的荷马赞歌》讲述珀耳塞福涅采花时被哈得斯带走，宙斯的许可亦在故事中占有位置。母亲德墨忒尔四处寻觅，终于得知女儿下落。她的悲痛不是被动等待，而是以停止谷物生长影响整个世界。
饥荒威胁人类，也使诸神面临失去祭祀的危机。经过交涉，珀耳塞福涅获准返回，但她已吃下冥界的石榴籽，因而不能永远留在母亲身边。母女重逢使土地复苏，离别则被纳入日后反复运行的时间之中。
现代转述常把故事概括为四季起源，古代文本却还关乎婚姻、失落、神圣权利与仪式希望。冥界停留的时长也因版本而异。厄琉西斯秘仪确与这组神话相关，但其秘密内容不能凭空补写成完整的仪式脚本。

stories.title: 雅典娜与波塞冬争城
stories.summary: 雅典娜与波塞冬争夺阿提卡城邦的守护权，分别献出橄榄树与盐泉。居民选择可供食用与照明的树木，城市由此与雅典娜结缘，争议却未随命名消失。
paragraphs: 阿提卡的城邦尚未确定守护神，波塞冬与雅典娜都提出要求。依照常见传说，众神要比较双方送给居民的礼物。波塞冬先登上卫城，以三叉戟击开岩石，泉水从裂缝涌出；人们围上前去品尝，却发现水中带着海洋的咸味，无法直接灌溉田地。
轮到雅典娜时，她把长矛插进土里，一株橄榄树在岩坡上长起。树上的果实能够食用，压出的油可以照明，枝干还能提供木料。居民看见的不是一瞬间的奇观，而是今后需要耐心照料的生计。裁决者因而把守护权判给雅典娜，波塞冬却不肯平静接受失败。
城市此后以雅典娜为名，但并未把海神逐出宗教生活。卫城仍保存与盐泉、三叉戟痕迹相关的圣迹，橄榄树也被当作城邦记忆来守护。不同古代作者对谁作裁决、海神怎样报复说法不一；这场竞赛讲述的是共享一座城市的神圣力量，而非消灭其中一方。

en.title: Athena and Poseidon Contest the City
en.summary: Athena and Poseidon compete to protect an Attic city, offering an olive tree and a salt spring. The decision favors a lasting livelihood, but the losing god remains present in the city’s sacred landscape rather than simply disappearing.
paragraphs: Before the Attic city had chosen its divine protector, Poseidon and Athena both claimed the honor. In a familiar version, their gifts would decide the contest. Poseidon struck the Acropolis rock with his trident, opening a spring. People approached the remarkable water, but its saltiness connected it to the sea rather than to the fresh water their fields required.

Athena planted her spear in the ground, and an olive tree appeared on the rocky height. Its fruit offered food, its oil could light homes, and its branches supplied useful wood. Those judging the gifts chose the tree and awarded her the city. Poseidon resented the judgment; a decision about protection had become a dispute between powerful divine neighbors.

The city took Athena’s name without erasing Poseidon from its worship. Sacred places on the Acropolis continued to connect the sea god with the spring and marks in the rock, alongside Athena’s olive. Ancient accounts disagree about the judges and his retaliation. The story explains a contested sacred landscape, not the final expulsion of one deity by another.

stories.title: 忒修斯走出迷宫
stories.summary: 雅典青年被送往克里特，供养迷宫中的弥诺陶洛斯。忒修斯自愿同行，借阿里阿德涅的线团杀死怪物并逃脱，却因归航的黑帆使父亲误以为儿子已死。
paragraphs: 雅典受制于克里特王米诺斯，必须定期交出青年男女，送进关押弥诺陶洛斯的迷宫。忒修斯不愿再让同城的人无声消失，主动加入下一批贡品。出航之前，他与父亲埃勾斯约定：如果活着回来，就换上白帆，让守在海岸的父亲能够远远辨认胜利的船只。
到了克里特，王女阿里阿德涅决定帮助忒修斯，交给他一团线，并告诉他进门时先固定线头。迷宫里的岔路不断把人引向深处，他却一边前行一边放线。找到半人半牛的怪物后，他奋力将它杀死，再循着细线折返，带领被献祭的青年们逃出难以辨认的通道。
忒修斯与同伴乘船离开，阿里阿德涅却在纳克索斯与他分离；关于分离原因，古代叙事各有解释。返乡时船上仍挂着黑帆，埃勾斯误以为儿子遇害，投身海中。忒修斯虽然结束了贡赋，却没有以毫无损失的胜利抵岸，继承王位也伴随着无法挽回的家庭悲痛。

en.title: Theseus Escapes the Labyrinth
en.summary: Theseus joins the Athenian youths sent to Crete and enters the Minotaur’s labyrinth. Ariadne’s thread makes escape possible after he kills the monster, but an unchanged sail turns the voyage home into a fatal misunderstanding for his waiting father.
paragraphs: Athens had to send young people to King Minos of Crete, where they were placed inside the labyrinth that held the Minotaur. Theseus volunteered to join the next group and end the killing. Before departure, he promised his father Aegeus that a successful return would be announced by white sails, visible from the shore long before the ship landed.

In Crete, Minos’s daughter Ariadne gave Theseus a thread and instructions for using it. He secured one end at the entrance and unwound the rest while following the labyrinth’s confusing passages. After finding and killing the creature, he did not have to guess his way back. The thread led him toward daylight, allowing the intended victims to escape together.

Theseus sailed away, but Ariadne was left on Naxos; ancient accounts offer different explanations for their separation. The returning ship still carried dark sails because the promised change had been forgotten. Seeing them, Aegeus believed his son was dead and threw himself into the sea. Theseus ended the tribute, yet his homecoming brought grief as well as political succession.

stories.title: 俄耳甫斯的最后一眼
stories.summary: 欧律狄刻死后，俄耳甫斯凭歌声进入冥界，争得带她返回人间的机会。唯一条件是途中不可回头，他却在出口前因不安转身，使失而复得的妻子再次离去。
paragraphs: 欧律狄刻被毒蛇咬伤而死，俄耳甫斯不肯只在人间哀哭，带着竖琴走向亡者的国度。他的歌声使守门者停下阻拦，也让承受刑罚的灵魂暂时忘却痛楚。最后他来到冥王与王后面前，不请求自己长生，只请求让年轻的妻子暂缓命运，随他重新见到阳光。
冥界的统治者被歌声打动，允许欧律狄刻跟在他身后离开，却规定在返回地上以前不得回头看她。俄耳甫斯踏上昏暗而漫长的上坡路，妻子的脚步仿佛时有时无。他既怕她没有跟上，又怕神明只给了一个幻影，只能一面向前，一面与越来越强的不安搏斗。
出口的光亮已经接近，他终于忍不住转过头。欧律狄刻还没有完全走出冥界，立刻向黑暗退去，两人再次分别，重入冥界的请求也未获准许。这一结局在维吉尔、奥维德等罗马作者笔下尤为著名；不同传本细节有别，回望却始终使短暂的希望变成第二次失去。

en.title: Orpheus Looks Back
en.summary: After Eurydice dies, Orpheus wins permission to lead her out of the underworld through music. He must not look behind him before their return is complete. Near daylight, fear overcomes his trust, and his backward glance ends their reunion.
paragraphs: When Eurydice died from a snakebite, Orpheus carried his lyre into the realm of the dead. His music moved its guardians and interrupted the suffering of punished souls. Before the rulers below, he asked neither for immortality nor for dominion. He asked that his young wife be allowed to return with him, postponing the separation death had suddenly imposed.

The underworld’s rulers granted his request on one condition: Eurydice would follow, and he must not look back before their passage to the upper world was complete. He began climbing through the darkness. Without a clear sign that she remained behind him, hope became difficult to distinguish from deception. Each step brought him closer to daylight and deeper into uncertainty.

At the threshold, Orpheus turned. Eurydice had not yet completed the ascent, and she slipped back into the world below. His attempt to cross again was refused, leaving him with a second separation rather than a restored marriage. The familiar telling survives especially in Virgil and Ovid, Roman poets whose versions preserve different details of this Greek mythic tradition.

stories.title: 阿波罗与达芙妮的月桂
stories.summary: 阿波罗追逐拒绝婚配的达芙妮，她在逃亡尽头求援，身体化作月桂。此篇依后世罗马诗人奥维德的著名叙述，保留被追者的拒绝，不把强迫追逐解释为爱情胜利。
paragraphs: 在奥维德的《变形记》中，阿波罗嘲笑丘比特的弓箭，爱神便用两支不同的箭报复：金箭使阿波罗燃起欲望，铅箭使达芙妮厌恶求爱。达芙妮本来就向往林野与不婚生活，曾请求父亲允许她保有选择；如今神明突然出现，她清楚地拒绝，却没有得到停止追逐的回应。
阿波罗一面夸耀自己的身份与能力，一面追着达芙妮穿过树林。他说自己不是敌人，她却只能靠奔跑拉开距离。追赶越来越近，她的力量渐渐耗尽，河流和熟悉的土地也无法替她挡住来者。走投无路时，她向河神父亲求救，请求改变这个让自己遭到追逐的身体。
求援之后，她的双脚生根，皮肤化作树皮，双臂伸成枝条，头发变成月桂叶。阿波罗拥抱树干，宣布月桂将成为自己的荣冠，树身却仍回避他的亲吻。这是罗马诗人对希腊神话材料的著名改写，不代表唯一古老版本；结局保存的是拒绝与失去，不能称为双方自愿的结合。

en.title: Apollo and Daphne Become Laurel Lore
en.summary: In Ovid’s Roman retelling of Greek mythic material, Apollo pursues Daphne despite her refusal. She asks for rescue and becomes a laurel tree. His subsequent claim upon the tree does not turn her flight into a willing romantic union.
paragraphs: In Ovid’s Metamorphoses, Apollo mocks Cupid’s weapons, provoking a carefully unequal revenge. A golden arrow fills Apollo with desire, while a leaden arrow turns Daphne away from love. She already prefers woodland freedom to marriage and has asked her father to respect that choice. When Apollo approaches, their wishes do not meet: her refusal is clear from the beginning.

Apollo pursues Daphne through the countryside, announcing his divine identity and insisting that she need not fear him. His assurances do not stop the chase. She keeps running, but exhaustion narrows the distance between them. With escape almost impossible, she calls upon her river-god father, asking him to change the body that has made her the object of pursuit.

Roots hold her feet, bark covers her body, and leaves spread where her hair had been. Apollo embraces the laurel and claims its foliage for his honors, although the transformed Daphne still recoils. This celebrated account is a later Roman literary treatment of Greek material, not its single original form. Her transformation ends the pursuit without creating mutual consent.

cosmos.name: 奥林匹斯
cosmos.desc: 诸神议事与宴饮的居所，既关联真实山岳，也具有诗歌中的超凡性质，并非所有神的唯一住处。

cosmos.name: 冥界
cosmos.desc: 死者所往的地下领域，由哈得斯与珀耳塞福涅掌权；不同作者描述的地形与命运并不一致。

cosmos.name: 塔耳塔罗斯
cosmos.desc: 宇宙深处的幽暗区域，常与被囚禁的古老力量相连，在神谱中与普通死者领域有所区别。

myths.note: 此处以古代诗歌传统为主，城邦祭祀与哲学解释不尽相同。古代宗教不等于现代奇幻设定；当代也有重建或复兴相关信仰的实践者。

myths.name: 北欧神话
myths.subtitle: 世界树的枝头，霜与火共同低语
myths.description: 北欧神话主要通过古诺尔斯诗歌、斯诺里的著述与考古材料为今人所知。诸神居于世界树联系的诸域，在与巨人、怪物及彼此的交涉中维系不稳固的秩序。知识往往需要牺牲，勇气也不能取消终结；而毁灭之后的再生，使宇宙并未停在最后一战。
myths.era: 维京时代及更早传统，中世纪冰岛文献集中保存
myths.quote: 霜落在树根，枝头仍记得春天。

gods.name: 奥丁
gods.title: 诗歌、知识与战争之神
gods.desc: 为追索智慧而付出身体代价，也与亡者和王权相关。他善于变形与谋划，并不是无所不知的存在。

gods.name: 索尔
gods.title: 雷霆与边界的守护者
gods.desc: 挥动名为妙尔尼尔的锤，常与威胁神人与人间的力量交战。他也与庇护、祝福及日常祭祀有关。

gods.name: 弗蕾雅
gods.title: 爱情、丰饶与魔法之神
gods.desc: 属于华纳神族，与欲望、财富及赛德魔法相连。她也接纳部分战死者，不能仅用爱情女神概括。

stories.title: 悬树求知
stories.summary: 奥丁在树上悬挂九夜，经受饥渴与伤痛，终于拾取符文。诗歌以谜一样的自我献祭，讲述知识并非轻易获得的赠礼。
paragraphs: 《高人的箴言》中，奥丁以第一人称说自己悬在风吹的树上，身受长矛之伤，历经九夜。他被献给奥丁，也就是献给自己；这令人不安的循环，使求知既像祭献，也像跨越生死边缘的一场独自考验。
无人给予面包，也无人递来饮水。经过漫长忍受，他向下探视，拾取符文，并发出呼喊。诗句将文字、力量与顿悟联系起来，却没有给出可任意照做的仪式步骤；符文在这里也不只是现代意义的书写字母。
这棵树通常被理解为世界树，但原诗保留了自己的含混，不宜把每个空白都填成确定细节。悬树求符文与奥丁用一眼换取智慧的故事同属求知母题，却是不同叙事，不应被简化成同一次交换的连续过程。

stories.title: 诸神黄昏之后
stories.summary: 预言中的大战使诸神与强敌相继倒下，天地经历火焰与海水。诗歌随后让大地重新浮现，并留下幸存者与新的相会。
paragraphs: 《女先知的预言》描绘秩序崩解的征兆：亲族相残，束缚松脱，巨大的力量向诸神逼近。芬里尔狼与尘世巨蛇等敌手现身，海与天空也失去稳定。末日并不只是一场战争，而是伦理、自然与宇宙边界的共同动摇。
奥丁被狼吞噬，索尔杀死巨蛇后也因毒而倒下，其他对手亦各有结局。火焰吞卷世界，大地沉入海中。主要来源对顺序与细节的组织不尽相同；诸神虽知道危险，仍行动迎战，却无法由勇武保证自身不死。
随后，大地又从海里升起，田野重现，幸存的神相聚并回忆旧日，部分叙事还留下人类延续的线索。新世界不是简单取消失去，而是在记忆与残存中开始。相关诗歌保存于基督教时代，影响关系仍需谨慎讨论。

stories.title: 索尔取回雷神之锤
stories.summary: 巨人索列姆偷走雷神之锤，要求以芙蕾雅为新娘换回。索尔不愿受辱却别无选择，只能披上嫁衣赴宴，等锤被抬来祝婚时突然出手，夺回武器并击败巨人。
paragraphs: 索尔醒来发现雷神之锤不见了，便让洛基借来芙蕾雅的羽衣，飞往巨人国查探。巨人索列姆承认自己把锤藏在地下深处，除非诸神交出芙蕾雅做新娘，否则绝不归还。芙蕾雅听到要求勃然大怒，拒绝被当成交换武器的物品，诸神只好另想办法应付危机。
海姆达尔提出让索尔穿上婚服，戴上芙蕾雅的项链，再由洛基扮成侍女陪同。索尔担心受到嘲笑，洛基却提醒他失去神锤会让众神陷入危险。两人来到巨人宴席，索尔惊人的食量与锐利眼神几乎揭穿伪装，洛基便接连编造新娘因思念而多日未吃未睡的解释。
索列姆深信婚事即将成功，命人把神锤抬到新娘膝上，为结合举行祝圣。索尔看见熟悉的武器，立即伸手抓牢，不再维持温顺的新娘模样。他先击倒索列姆，继而扫平宴席上的敌手，带锤离开。这篇见于《诗体埃达》的故事以角色倒置制造喜剧，危机靠伪装而非直接挑战解决。

en.title: Thor Recovers His Hammer
en.summary: The giant Thrym steals Thor’s hammer and demands Freyja as his bride. When she refuses, Thor disguises himself for the wedding feast. He must survive suspicious questions until the stolen weapon is finally brought within reach for the ceremony.
paragraphs: Thor awoke to find his hammer missing. Loki borrowed Freyja’s feathered garment and flew to the giants, where Thrym admitted hiding the weapon deep underground. He would return it only in exchange for Freyja as his bride. When the demand reached her, she angrily refused. The gods needed another plan rather than treating her agreement as something already secured.

Heimdall proposed dressing Thor as the bride, with Loki accompanying him as a maid. Thor disliked the humiliation, but Loki warned what losing the hammer would mean for the gods. At the feast, the disguised bride ate enormously and stared fiercely. Loki explained each suspicious detail by claiming that anticipation had prevented her from eating or sleeping for days.

Thrym ordered the hammer placed on the bride’s knees to consecrate the marriage. Once his weapon was within reach, Thor seized it and abandoned the disguise. He struck down Thrym and defeated the other giants gathered there before returning with the hammer. Preserved in the Poetic Edda, the episode resolves its crisis through deception and comic reversals before force becomes possible.

stories.title: 芬里尔与提尔失去的手
stories.summary: 诸神害怕巨狼芬里尔未来带来灾祸，诱他试戴无法挣断的魔索。芬里尔要求有人以手担保，提尔于是伸手入狼口；骗局成真后，巨狼受缚，担保者也付出一只手。
paragraphs: 诸神把洛基的孩子芬里尔养在身边，却发现巨狼越长越快，预言又说他将给众神带来灾难。他们先后造出两副结实的锁链，请他把挣断锁链当作力量的游戏。芬里尔轻易扯碎束缚，诸神明白普通铁器无法制服他，只得托人向擅长制作宝物的矮人求助。
矮人造出看似柔软的格莱普尼尔，用猫的脚步声等不可能之物制成。诸神带着它来到湖中孤岛，称赞巨狼足够强大，理应也能挣脱丝带。芬里尔察觉圈套，要求一位神把手放进自己的口中，保证试验后会获释。众神互相观望，最后只有提尔走上前去承担担保。
魔索越挣越紧，芬里尔终于明白诸神并不打算释放自己，便咬断提尔的手。诸神把狼牢牢固定，暂时避开了惧怕的灾难，却也亲自背弃了保证。按照后来的末日叙事，芬里尔终将挣脱；这个结局没有把束缚说成毫无代价的胜利，提尔残缺的身体始终记着那次承诺。

en.title: Fenrir and Tyr’s Hand
en.summary: Fearing Fenrir’s future violence, the gods challenge him to test a magical binding. The wolf demands a hand as a pledge of honest release. Tyr supplies it, knowing the promise will fail, and loses his hand when the trap closes.
paragraphs: The gods raised Loki’s wolf-child Fenrir among them, but his rapid growth and threatening prophecies frightened them. Twice they presented strong chains as opportunities to demonstrate his strength. Twice he snapped the bonds. Realizing that ordinary metal would not hold him, they commissioned the dwarfs to make something whose apparent weakness would conceal a far more effective kind of restraint.

The dwarfs produced Gleipnir, a smooth ribbon made from impossible ingredients, including the sound of a cat’s footsteps. On an island, the gods invited Fenrir to test it. He suspected deception and demanded that one of them place a hand inside his mouth as a pledge that he would be released. Only Tyr stepped forward to provide the guarantee.

The more Fenrir struggled, the tighter Gleipnir became. When the gods refused to free him, he bit off Tyr’s hand. They secured the wolf and postponed the danger they feared, but their safety depended on a broken pledge. Later accounts anticipate his escape at the final catastrophe. Tyr’s missing hand leaves the cost of this temporary victory visibly unresolved.

stories.title: 伊敦与失窃的青春苹果
stories.summary: 巨人夏基逼洛基把守护青春苹果的伊敦诱出神域。诸神迅速衰老，洛基被迫前去营救，把她变成果仁带回；巨人化鹰追赶，最终在阿斯加德城墙外落入火中。
paragraphs: 奥丁、海尼尔与洛基远行时，发现锅中的肉怎么也煮不熟。树上的巨鹰声称是自己阻碍了烹煮，要求分食才肯放行，随后又吞下大块食物。洛基挥棍击鹰，棍子却粘在鹰身上，自己也被拖上天空。巨鹰原是巨人夏基，他逼洛基答应把伊敦和青春苹果带出诸神的住所。
洛基脱身以后，告诉伊敦林外有比她收藏的更好的苹果，请她带着自己的果实去比较。伊敦一离开神域，夏基便化鹰将她掳走。失去她保管的苹果，诸神的头发逐渐变白，身体不断衰弱。大家追查她最后出现的行踪，把责任追到洛基身上，命他立刻设法将人救回。
洛基借来羽衣，飞到巨人住处，趁夏基外出时把伊敦变成果仁抓在爪中。夏基发现后化作巨鹰追来，诸神则在城墙边备好木柴。洛基刚飞入安全处，火焰就升起烧伤追鹰的翅膀，巨人随即被杀。伊敦恢复原形，诸神重新得到苹果，但营救并未抹去最初诱骗她的责任。

en.title: Idunn and the Stolen Apples
en.summary: Forced into a bargain with the giant Thjazi, Loki lures Idunn away from the gods. Without her apples they grow old. He must return to the giant’s home, transform the captive for flight, and survive pursuit back to Asgard.
paragraphs: While traveling with Odin and Hoenir, Loki found that their meat would not cook. An eagle claimed responsibility and demanded a share before allowing the meal to proceed. When it took too much, Loki struck it with a pole and became trapped, dragged helplessly through the air. The eagle was the giant Thjazi, who demanded Idunn and her apples as ransom.

After his release, Loki told Idunn that better apples grew outside the gods’ enclosure and persuaded her to bring her own for comparison. Thjazi seized her once she ventured out. Deprived of her apples, the gods began to age. They traced her disappearance to Loki and threatened him until he agreed to undo the danger his deception had created.

Borrowing a feathered garment, Loki reached Thjazi’s home and transformed Idunn into a nut he could carry. The returning giant became an eagle and pursued them. At Asgard, the gods lit prepared wood after Loki crossed the wall, scorching their pursuer’s wings. They killed Thjazi, and Idunn restored their youth, although her rescue did not erase Loki’s responsibility for her capture.

stories.title: 巴德尔之死与未完成的归来
stories.summary: 弗丽嘉让万物发誓不伤巴德尔，却遗漏了槲寄生。洛基利用这个缺口诱导霍德尔投出致命枝条；众神试图以普遍哀哭换他归来，最后仍因一次拒绝而失败。
paragraphs: 巴德尔接连梦见死亡，母亲弗丽嘉便走遍世界，请火、水、金属、石头与生灵发誓不伤害他。众神发现武器真的无法伤他，竟把向他投掷东西当成娱乐。洛基见此不安，假扮来访者向弗丽嘉打听，终于知道幼小的槲寄生被认为不足为害，因此没有参加那场誓约。
洛基取来槲寄生，走到没有参与游戏的盲神霍德尔身旁，声称可以替他指明方向。霍德尔照着引导掷出枝条，巴德尔立即倒地死去。欢笑的场地变成哀悼之所，诸神却无法用愤怒撤回已经发生的投掷，只能准备葬礼，并派赫尔莫德骑马进入冥界请求释放死者。
冥界的赫尔提出条件：若万物都为巴德尔哭泣，就让他回来。使者遍访各处，生灵与无生命之物都留下眼泪，只有名叫索克的女巨人拒绝。请求因此失败，巴德尔继续留在冥界。这里依《散文埃达》的连贯叙述，其他古代材料的凶手关系与情节安排并不完全相同。

en.title: Baldr’s Death and the Failed Return
en.summary: Frigg secures promises that nothing will harm Baldr, overlooking mistletoe. Loki exploits the omission through the blind Hodr. A journey to the dead offers one remaining hope, but Baldr cannot return unless every being agrees to mourn him.
paragraphs: Troubled by dreams of death, Baldr became the focus of his mother Frigg’s protective efforts. She obtained promises from substances and living beings that they would not injure him. The gods then amused themselves by throwing weapons at him harmlessly. Disguised as a visitor, Loki questioned Frigg and learned that young mistletoe had been considered too insignificant to require an oath.

Loki obtained mistletoe and approached the blind god Hodr, who had not joined the game. Offering guidance, he helped Hodr throw the overlooked plant at Baldr. This time the target fell dead. The gathering’s amusement became grief, and the gods prepared a funeral. Hermod rode to the underworld, seeking a release that their strength could not force from death.

Hel agreed to release Baldr if everything in existence wept for him. Messengers gathered tears from living creatures and lifeless things, but a giantess called Thokk refused to mourn. The condition therefore failed, and Baldr remained below. This sequence follows the Prose Edda; other ancient witnesses arrange the killing and its participants differently, so it should not stand for every tradition.

cosmos.name: 世界树
cosmos.desc: 常称尤克特拉希尔，树根与枝干联系不同领域；文献并未提供一幅毫无矛盾的九界地图。

cosmos.name: 阿斯加德
cosmos.desc: 阿萨诸神的重要居所，与人间及其他领域通过路径和边界相连，常被后世图像重新空间化。

cosmos.name: 中庭
cosmos.desc: 人类居住的世界，被海洋与外围力量环绕；名称强调受到围护的区域及其并不牢固的边缘。

myths.note: 主要书面材料由基督教化后的作者保存，不能直接视为全部维京人的统一教义。现代北欧多神信仰亦有活态社群，符文不应被自动等同极端主义符号。

myths.name: 埃及神话
myths.subtitle: 日舟穿越长夜，尼罗河见证重生
myths.description: 古埃及神话在数千年的神庙、墓葬与仪式文本中不断变化。太阳的运行、尼罗河的滋养、王权与死后生命彼此关联，宇宙秩序需要每日维护。赫利奥波利斯、孟斐斯等地拥有不同创世传统；这些差异往往能够并存，而非等待被整理成唯一正确的神谱。
myths.era: 王朝时代持续发展，部分传统延续至希腊罗马时期
myths.quote: 长夜有河，太阳以归来回答黑暗。

gods.name: 拉
gods.title: 太阳与持续创造之神
gods.desc: 以日间航行和夜间更新维系生命，与其他神结合出多种形态。他的神话随时代、地区与仪式而变化。

gods.name: 伊西斯
gods.title: 守护、疗愈与神力的女神
gods.desc: 以哀悼、护子和有力的言语行动著称。她的崇拜后来传播至地中海多地，远超单一故事的范围。

gods.name: 奥西里斯
gods.title: 亡者与复生秩序之神
gods.desc: 遇害后成为亡者世界的重要统治者，与土地更新及王权传承相连，其复生不等同返回日常人世。

stories.title: 伊西斯寻回奥西里斯
stories.summary: 奥西里斯遭塞特谋害，伊西斯寻回并守护他的身体。借由神圣援助，生命与王权得以延续，荷鲁斯日后争取父亲的继承地位。
paragraphs: 奥西里斯之死与塞特的敌对构成古埃及重要的神话群，但古代材料多以仪式片段和暗示讲述，并非一开始就有完整长篇。广为流传的箱棺漂流、肢体散落等细节，往往还经过希腊语作者的整理与扩展。
伊西斯与奈芙蒂斯的寻找和哀悼，使破碎的身体重新成为被守护的整体。阿努比斯等神的协助，又把故事连接到防腐与葬仪。复生在这里并非取消死亡，而是让亡者获得另一种完整性，并使生命的关系继续发生。
伊西斯保护幼年的荷鲁斯，后者与塞特争夺继承权。奥西里斯则在亡者领域确立地位，而非简单重登人间王座。神话让哀悼、护育、审判与王权相互映照，也使个人的葬礼能够参与更宏大的更新秩序。

stories.title: 太阳穿过冥夜
stories.summary: 夕阳并非消失，而是进入夜间领域。太阳神沿隐秘水道前行，面对阿佩普等威胁，在神灵协力与更新之中迎来新的黎明。
paragraphs: 在《阿姆杜阿特》等冥界图文中，夜晚被描绘为有时段、有门径也有居民的深邃旅程。太阳进入人眼不可见的领域，乘舟经过危险水路。那些图像并不是一部统一旅行指南，而与具体墓葬和宗教知识有关。
巨蛇阿佩普象征对太阳运行和宇宙秩序的威胁，诸神以力量、言辞及仪式抵御它。某些传统还强调太阳与奥西里斯在深夜的相遇，使太阳的更新与亡者的复生相互联系，死亡因此不再只是孤立的终点。
黎明到来，太阳重新升起，但混乱并未从此永远消失。秩序需要反复维护，这是埃及宗教时间感的一条重要线索。神庙仪式与墓葬文本各以不同方式参与这场更新，不能把所有夜航版本拼成唯一固定路线。

stories.title: 荷鲁斯与塞特争夺王位
stories.summary: 奥西里斯死后，荷鲁斯与塞特长期争夺统治权。伊西斯用伪装迫使塞特承认儿子的继承资格，竞赛却仍不断继续，直到神庭裁定荷鲁斯继位，为塞特另作安排。
paragraphs: 《荷鲁斯与塞特之争》的纸草叙事中，奥西里斯死后，儿子荷鲁斯要求继承王位，叔父塞特却以自己的力量与护卫太阳神的功劳争取统治。神庭迟迟不能取得一致，争执延续八十年。伊西斯支持儿子，太阳神却屡次偏向塞特，使本来关于继承的案件变成漫长的审理与较量。
一次神庭移到岛上，塞特要求禁止伊西斯入内。她用金子说动摆渡者，变装成女子登岛，又向塞特诉说一个虚构案件：丈夫死后，陌生人要夺走儿子的牛群。塞特愤怒地判定，不该在儿子尚在时把财产给外人；伊西斯随即显露身份，让他的判断反过来支持荷鲁斯的要求。
争论并未当场结束，双方还比造石船；荷鲁斯以木船覆灰伪装，塞特的真石船却沉了。后来神庭向冥界的奥西里斯征询意见，终于承认荷鲁斯继位，塞特则被太阳神接纳，与天上的雷声相连。这是特定纸草本的诙谐曲折叙述，并非所有埃及材料都按同样顺序安排继承之争。

en.title: Horus and Seth Contest the Throne
en.summary: After Osiris’s death, Horus and Seth dispute the throne before a divided divine court. Isis disguises herself to expose a contradiction in Seth’s claim. Further contests prolong the quarrel before Horus receives kingship and Seth gains a different divine place.
paragraphs: In the papyrus narrative called The Contendings of Horus and Seth, Osiris’s son claims his father’s kingship, while Seth argues from strength and his service defending the solar god. The court cannot agree, and the dispute lasts eighty years. Isis supports her son, but the sun god repeatedly favors Seth, turning the question of succession into a prolonged series of hearings.

When proceedings move to an island from which Isis is excluded, she bribes the ferryman with gold and arrives disguised as a woman. She tells Seth that a stranger threatens to take her dead husband’s cattle from their son. Seth condemns the seizure. Isis reveals herself: his answer supports a son’s inheritance, contradicting the argument he has advanced against Horus.

More contests follow, including a race in stone boats. Horus disguises wood beneath a coating, while Seth’s real stone boat sinks. After the court consults Osiris below, Horus finally receives the throne. Seth is accepted by the solar god and associated with thunder. This particular papyrus preserves a winding, sometimes comic dispute, not a sequence shared identically by all Egyptian sources.

stories.title: 伊西斯与拉的秘密名字
stories.summary: 伊西斯渴望知道太阳神隐藏的名字，取拉的唾液和泥土造出毒蛇，令他在巡行途中受伤。众神无法解毒，拉最终交出秘密，她才以咒语解除毒患，神话也成为治蛇伤的依据。
paragraphs: 在保存这则故事的埃及治蛇伤咒文中，伊西斯希望获得太阳神拉未向其他神明透露的名字。年老的拉行走时唾液落地，她便取来唾液，揉进泥土，塑成一条毒蛇，放在他每日经过的路上。这条蛇出自他的身体，却不是他亲自创造的生灵，因此成为他未曾防备的危险。
拉经过时被蛇咬中，毒液蔓延全身，痛得发抖，召来众神也不能解除。伊西斯上前声称能够治愈，但必须知道他的名字才能施咒。拉先列举创造天地的功业与人们熟知的称号，仍不肯说出隐藏的那个名字；她指出这些并非所求，毒势便继续逼迫受伤的太阳神作出选择。
拉终于同意让秘密的名字从自己传到伊西斯那里，叙事没有把它直接写给读者。获得所需知识以后，她命令毒液离开，宣告拉继续生存、毒害消退。咒文随后把这场神明获救的先例用于现实中的蛇伤患者；故事讲的是隐秘知识与有效言语，不是伊西斯把太阳神永久杀死或废黜。

en.title: Isis and the Secret Name of Ra
en.summary: Seeking Ra’s hidden name, Isis shapes a serpent from his saliva and earth. Its bite defeats ordinary divine help. She offers healing in exchange for the secret, and the resulting cure becomes a mythical precedent invoked for people suffering snakebite.
paragraphs: In an Egyptian healing text, Isis desires the name that the sun god Ra has concealed from other divinities. As the aging god passes, saliva falls from his mouth. She combines it with earth, shapes a serpent, and places it along his regular path. Made from his own substance but not fashioned by him, it presents a danger he has not anticipated.

The serpent bites Ra, and poison spreads through his body. He trembles in pain and summons the gods, but their presence brings no cure. Isis says that she can heal him if he reveals his name. Ra lists his creative achievements and familiar titles instead. She rejects these as insufficient, while the poison forces him to reconsider withholding the concealed name.

Ra finally agrees that the secret name should pass from him to Isis. The narrative does not disclose it directly to its readers. Possessing the required knowledge, she commands the poison to leave and declares that Ra will live. The spell applies this divine rescue to a human snakebite victim: effective hidden knowledge restores the god rather than permanently overthrowing him.

stories.title: 染红的啤酒让女神止怒
stories.summary: 拉得知人类谋反，派出自己的眼惩罚逃入荒野的人群。杀戮将失去限度，他便用红色矿料染红啤酒，诱使女神饮醉，幸存者因此免遭灭绝，太阳神却选择离开地面。
paragraphs: 《天牛之书》叙述太阳神拉衰老以后，人类暗中谋划反抗。他召来诸神商议，原初之神努恩建议派出拉之眼惩罚叛逆。人群逃入荒野，女神哈托尔承担这股毁灭力量，追赶并杀死他们。她因屠杀获得满足，惩罚眼看要从镇压谋反扩展为使人类再也无法延续的灾难。
拉随后决定保全剩下的人，命使者从象岛运来红色矿料，让人磨碎掺进大量啤酒，装满七千罐。人们连夜把染成血色的酒倒在女神即将经过的田野，地面看起来像遍布鲜血。她清晨到来，看见液面映出自己的面容，便俯身畅饮；酒精使她醉倒，再不能辨认和追杀人类。
拉迎回已经止怒的女神，幸存者得以继续生活；这一段也与后来为女神奉酒的仪式发生联系。但太阳神已经厌倦与人类同住，随后由化成天牛的努特承载升离地面。故事的结局不仅是危险解除，还解释了天地分隔；其中女神的凶烈形象不宜与所有哈托尔或塞赫麦特传说混成一篇。

en.title: Red Beer Stops the Goddess’s Slaughter
en.summary: When humanity rebels, Ra sends his Eye to punish the fugitives. The killing threatens their survival, so he disguises beer as blood and intoxicates the goddess. Humanity survives, but the weary solar ruler subsequently withdraws from life upon the earth.
paragraphs: The Book of the Heavenly Cow tells how humans plotted against the aging Ra. He assembled the gods, and the primordial Nun advised sending his Eye against the rebels. Hathor pursued the people who had fled into the wilderness and delighted in killing them. Punishment now threatened to exceed the rebellion and leave no human population to survive afterward.

Ra decided to spare those who remained. Messengers fetched red mineral pigment from Elephantine, and workers ground it into beer, filling seven thousand jars. The colored drink was spread over the fields during the night. Arriving at dawn, the goddess saw her reflection in the apparently bloody liquid and drank deeply. Intoxication left her unable to recognize and continue pursuing human victims.

Ra welcomed the pacified goddess, allowing the survivors to live; the episode also provided a setting for ritual offerings of drink. Yet the sun god no longer wished to remain among humanity. Nut, transformed into a heavenly cow, carried him away from the ground. The narrative therefore explains cosmic separation as well as rescue, not every tradition concerning Hathor or Sekhmet.

stories.title: 亡者的心脏与真理之羽
stories.summary: 亡者进入奥西里斯的审判庭，陈述自己没有犯下的罪行，心脏随后与玛阿特的羽毛相衡。阿努比斯照看天平，托特记录结果，获判正直者才被引到冥王面前继续来世生活。
paragraphs: 按照《亡灵书》相关咒文与常见审判图像，亡者来到双重真理的厅堂，面对奥西里斯及审判者。他报出神明的名字，申明自己没有杀人、偷盗或侵夺祭品，请求获准进入来世。这里既有对生前行为的辩白，也有必须正确掌握的仪式言语，并非只要携带贵重陪葬品就能通过。
阿努比斯把亡者引向天平，照看心脏与代表玛阿特的羽毛是否平衡。心脏被认为保存个人的思想与行为，因此可能成为不利证人；有关咒文请求它不要起身反对主人。托特在旁记录，兼有鳄鱼、狮子与河马特征的吞噬者阿米特守候秤边，使审判失败的威胁有了可见形象。
在获准通过的常见图像中，荷鲁斯引领被称为声音真实的亡者来到奥西里斯面前，确认他可以进入神圣的来世。苇原中的生活仍可能包括耕作，而不是无限享乐的奖赏。这些文字与画面在不同纸草卷中组合有别，不能把全部细节当成每位埃及人都相信的单一固定剧情。

en.title: The Heart and the Feather of Truth
en.summary: A deceased person answers before divine judges, then faces the weighing of the heart against Maat’s feather. Anubis attends the balance and Thoth records its result. Successful judgment permits an introduction to Osiris and continued existence in the world beyond.
paragraphs: In related Book of the Dead spells and familiar judgment pictures, the deceased enters the Hall of the Two Truths before Osiris and divine assessors. Knowing their names, the speaker denies offenses such as murder, theft, and taking sacred offerings. Admission requires both claims about earthly conduct and appropriate ritual speech; expensive burial equipment alone does not constitute the depicted test.

Anubis attends the balance as the heart is weighed against the feather representing Maat. Since the heart preserves thought and action, it can testify against its owner; a related spell asks it not to oppose the deceased. Thoth records the outcome. Nearby waits Ammit, combining crocodile, lion, and hippopotamus features, whose presence gives visible form to the danger of failed admission.

In familiar successful scenes, Horus brings the vindicated deceased before Osiris, confirming access to a blessed existence. Life in the Field of Reeds may still involve cultivating crops rather than receiving unlimited leisure. Texts and pictures vary between papyri, however. These connected episodes describe a recognizable funerary pattern, not an identical continuous script subscribed to by every person in ancient Egypt.

cosmos.name: 努恩
cosmos.desc: 创世之前的原初水域，也作为未分化力量环绕世界；它不是某条可在地图上定位的河流。

cosmos.name: 杜阿特
cosmos.desc: 与夜间太阳和死者旅程相关的隐秘领域，其地形在不同葬仪文本与图像中有多种安排。

cosmos.name: 玛阿特
cosmos.desc: 兼为女神与真实、正义、适当秩序的观念，是宇宙及社会需持续实践的原则，而非地名。

myths.note: 埃及神话跨越漫长时段，神名、关系与中心地位均会改变。本条不以单一王朝代表全部传统，也不把木乃伊、审判或神庙实践简化为猎奇的死亡崇拜。

myths.name: 凯尔特神话
myths.subtitle: 雾中的彼岸，藏在丘陵与潮汐之间
myths.description: 凯尔特神话是对多种语言与地域传统的统称，并非一个统一神系。本条以中世纪爱尔兰文献保存的故事为主，兼顾其口传背景。达努神族、技艺卓绝的英雄与隐现的彼岸，使土地、主权和亲缘彼此交织；威尔士等地的叙事则应在各自脉络中阅读。
myths.era: 古代宗教背景深远，主要爱尔兰叙事存于中世纪手稿
myths.quote: 雾没有遮住道路，只把彼岸留给倾听的人。

gods.name: 达格达
gods.title: 丰饶、力量与技艺的神
gods.desc: 爱尔兰达努神族的重要成员，常关联神奇的锅与竖琴。他的形象兼有威严、幽默和多种技能。

gods.name: 卢格
gods.title: 精通多艺的神圣领袖
gods.desc: 以掌握多种技艺进入诸神之列，在第二次玛格图瑞德之战中居于关键位置，不宜仅称太阳神。

gods.name: 莫莉甘
gods.title: 战争与命运的神圣女性
gods.desc: 在战场、预言与主权叙事中出现，常与乌鸦意象相连。她与其他女性神名的关系随文本而变。

stories.title: 卢格叩门
stories.summary: 卢格来到达努神族的宫廷，逐一报出自己的本领，却被告知已有专才。直到他问起是否有人兼通诸艺，门才终于为他打开。
paragraphs: 在第二次玛格图瑞德之战的故事中，卢格来到努阿达的宫廷，请求进入。他说自己是工匠、战士、诗人，也掌握其他技艺，守门人却一一回答宫中已有这样的人。单独一种卓越，似乎还不足以使陌生人得到位置。
卢格于是提出另一问题：宫中可有人同时具备这些本领？这一次，答案改变了。他得以入内，并在考验和协作中获得更重要的角色。故事的转折不在于否认各位专才，而在于看见能够联结多种能力的新价值。
当神族面对弗摩尔人的压迫与战争时，卢格的多艺成为组织集体力量的条件。他并非孤身取代所有同伴，而是让不同专长各得其所。这样的领袖形象将智慧与协调置于武力旁边，也使叩门成为资格重估的时刻。

stories.title: 布兰驶向彼岸
stories.summary: 布兰听见来自异界的歌声，遂率伙伴渡海，见到不受人间时间支配的岛屿。归途中的一次登岸，让漫长岁月突然显露重量。
paragraphs: 爱尔兰《布兰航海记》里，一位神秘女子带来关于远方国土的歌声与召唤。布兰随后出海，海面不再只是隔开陆地的水域，而成为认识另一种现实的路径。旅途中出现的存在，也提示人类目光所见并非世界全貌。
船队来到令人欢乐的岛屿，在那里停留的时间似乎短暂而轻盈。后来伙伴思念故乡，坚持返航，却被告诫不要踏上故土。彼岸的丰足并不意味着毫无界限，跨越两个领域的人必须面对各自不相同的时间与规则。
归来时，人们已把布兰当作久远传说中的名字。一位伙伴登岸，立即化为尘土，显露两地时间之间的巨大错位。布兰没有照常返回生活，而是在船上讲述所见；故事让航行本身成为传递彼岸知识的最后桥梁。

stories.title: 库丘林如何获得名字
stories.summary: 少年瑟坦赴铁匠库兰的宴席，被守门猛犬袭击。他为自保杀死猎犬，随后承诺在新犬长成以前亲自守护主人；德鲁伊据此赐名库丘林，意为库兰之犬。
paragraphs: 年幼的瑟坦来到阿尔斯特，渴望加入康霍巴尔王的武士队伍。一天国王应邀去铁匠库兰家赴宴，途中看见他正在玩球，便叫他稍后跟来。少年想先完成比赛，国王却在入席后忘了这位迟来的客人，告诉主人同行者已经到齐，库兰于是放开负责看守宅院的猛犬。
夜色降临，瑟坦独自赶到门外，守犬立刻向他扑去。少年没有同伴接应，只能用随身球具迎战；常见叙述说他把球击进犬口，随后将猛犬杀死。屋内众人听到声响赶出来，国王庆幸孩子尚在，库兰却为失去守护家园与牲畜的忠实猎犬而悲伤不已，也担忧此后的安全。
瑟坦并未用胜利来回绝主人的损失，而是提出替他养一条同样出色的幼犬，并在幼犬长成前亲自守卫宅院。德鲁伊卡斯巴德听见这个承诺，称他为库丘林，也就是库兰之犬。少年接受新名，离开时带走的不仅是勇武声誉，还有因自己行动而承担的具体责任与约定。

en.title: How Cú Chulainn Received His Name
en.summary: Young Sétanta arrives late at Culann’s feast and must kill the smith’s guard dog to survive. When he sees the owner’s loss, he promises to serve as guardian until a replacement grows, earning the name Cú Chulainn: Culann’s hound.
paragraphs: The boy Sétanta sought a place among the warriors of Ulster. On his way to a feast at the smith Culann’s home, King Conchobar saw him playing ball and invited him to follow. Sétanta stayed to finish the game. At the feast, the king forgot his invitation, assured Culann that everyone had arrived, and allowed the great watchdog to be released.

Arriving alone after dark, Sétanta faced the charging hound without anyone to explain his presence. In a familiar telling, he drove his playing ball into its mouth and killed it. The guests rushed outside at the noise. Conchobar rejoiced that the boy was alive, but Culann mourned the protector whose death left his household and cattle vulnerable to future attacks.

Sétanta offered to rear another hound and guard Culann’s property himself until the young dog could take over. Hearing this promise, the druid Cathbad named him Cú Chulainn, the hound of Culann. The boy accepted the name. His new identity therefore arose not only from extraordinary strength, but from an undertaking to repair the harm his necessary defense had caused.

stories.title: 普伊尔与安努恩之王
stories.summary: 戴维德的普伊尔在狩猎中冒犯异界猎犬的主人，答应与安努恩之王阿劳恩交换形貌一年。他遵守约定击败对手，也尊重王后的处境，最终以克制换得友谊与名声。
paragraphs: 在威尔士《马比诺吉昂》第一支中，戴维德领主普伊尔外出狩猎，看见一群白身红耳的猎犬扑倒雄鹿。他赶走那些犬，让自己的猎犬吃食，随后才遇见主人阿劳恩。阿劳恩自称安努恩之王，指出这场冒犯；普伊尔愿意补偿，便接受交换形貌与国度一年零一天的安排。
普伊尔来到安努恩，众人都把他当作阿劳恩。他白天处理事务，夜晚虽然与王后同寝，却始终背过身，不借他人的身份索取亲密。一年期满，他依照嘱咐迎战阿劳恩的敌人哈夫甘，只用一击将其重创；对方请求再击一次，他却拒绝，避免落入让敌人恢复力量的圈套。
敌人败退以后，普伊尔将统治权完整交还，回到戴维德。他发现阿劳恩也以公正治理了自己的领地，双方由赔偿关系转为友谊。阿劳恩后来从王后那里得知普伊尔的克制，更深信这位盟友可靠。普伊尔因此获得安努恩之主的称号，这是一则具体的威尔士异界故事，而非所有凯尔特传统共有的历史。

en.title: Pwyll and the King of Annwn
en.summary: Pwyll offends the owner of an uncanny hunting pack and accepts a yearlong exchange of identities as compensation. In Annwn he must defeat a rival without abusing his borrowed position. Keeping both obligations transforms the encounter into an enduring alliance.
paragraphs: In the First Branch of the Welsh Mabinogi, Pwyll of Dyfed came upon white hounds with red ears bringing down a stag. He drove them away and fed his own dogs on their kill. Their owner, Arawn, king of Annwn, challenged the insult. Pwyll offered compensation and agreed to exchange appearances and kingdoms with him for a year and a day.

Living as Arawn, Pwyll governed the other kingdom and shared the queen’s chamber, but turned away each night rather than exploit his assumed identity. At the appointed encounter, he struck Arawn’s rival Hafgan once, as instructed. The wounded rival begged for another blow. Pwyll refused, avoiding the action that would have restored his opponent and defeated the purpose of their bargain.

After the victory, the two rulers resumed their own appearances and returned to their kingdoms. Pwyll discovered that Arawn had governed Dyfed well; Arawn learned from the queen how carefully Pwyll had respected their household. Compensation became friendship, and Pwyll gained his title associated with Annwn. The episode belongs to a particular Welsh literary tradition, not an interchangeable pan-Celtic account.

stories.title: 芬恩与智慧鲑鱼
stories.summary: 芬恩替诗人芬尼加斯烹煮寻获的智慧鲑鱼，不慎烫伤手指，吮吸时尝到鱼汁。诗人发现预言指向的并非自己，便让少年吃鱼，智慧从此与芬恩相随。
paragraphs: 年少的芬恩还没有成为费奥纳勇士的首领时，曾向诗人芬尼加斯学习。依照爱尔兰少年事迹中的著名讲述，诗人多年守候博因河，等待一条能带来智慧的鲑鱼。他终于捕到鱼，便交给少年烹煮，特别叮嘱不可先尝一口，希望把长久追寻的智慧留给自己。
芬恩看守炉火，留意鱼皮不要烧焦。鱼身鼓起一处水泡，他伸出拇指按住，滚烫的油汁却灼伤手指。他本能地把拇指放进口中止痛，没有想到这个细小动作已经让他尝到鲑鱼。端鱼上桌以后，诗人追问他是否吃过，他如实说自己没有吃肉，只曾吮过烫伤的手指。
诗人又问少年的名字，听见芬恩之名，明白关于智慧归属的预言落在眼前的学生身上，而不是久候河边的自己。他让芬恩吃下鲑鱼，完成所得。此后遇到疑难，芬恩把拇指放到齿边，便能获得隐秘知识；这段成长故事解释了英雄的洞察力，而非一场靠武力赢得的比赛。

en.title: Fionn and the Salmon of Knowledge
en.summary: Young Fionn cooks the salmon that his teacher has long sought. A burnt thumb brings an accidental taste, revealing who was meant to receive its knowledge. The disappointed poet recognizes the prophecy and allows his pupil to finish the fish.
paragraphs: Before becoming leader of the Fianna, young Fionn studied with the poet Finnéces, also known as Finegas. In the familiar Irish boyhood tale, the teacher had waited beside the River Boyne for a salmon carrying extraordinary knowledge. When he finally caught it, he asked his pupil to cook the fish, expressly forbidding him to taste any of its flesh.

While watching the cooking, Fionn noticed a blister rising on the salmon’s skin. He pressed it with his thumb, burning himself, and instinctively put the injured finger into his mouth. When the fish was ready, his teacher asked whether he had eaten any. Fionn answered honestly: he had taken no meat, but had sucked his thumb to soothe the burn.

After asking the boy’s name, the poet recognized that the promised recipient of the salmon’s knowledge was his pupil, not himself. He gave Fionn the fish to eat, completing the transfer he had hoped to secure. Thereafter, putting his thumb to his tooth could reveal hidden knowledge. The episode explains the hero’s insight through an accidental act rather than a martial victory.

stories.title: 里安农的考验与归来的孩子
stories.summary: 里安农的婴儿夜间失踪，侍女害怕受罚，杀犬伪造她吞食孩子的证据。她被迫在宫门受辱，直到特尔农带回救下的男孩，失踪真相才使王后恢复名誉。
paragraphs: 在威尔士《马比诺吉昂》第一支中，里安农嫁给普伊尔以后，终于生下众人期盼的继承人。六名妇女轮流守护婴儿，却在一夜之间全都睡去，醒来时发现摇篮已空。她们害怕承担失职的后果，便杀死一只幼犬，把血涂在熟睡王后的脸上，诬称母亲吞食了自己的孩子。
里安农否认指控，却没有证人替她辩明。宫廷决定让她受罚七年：坐在宫门旁的上马石边，向来客复述那项罪名，并提出背他们入内。与此同时，领主特尔农守候自家母马产驹，看见巨爪伸来抢夺，挥剑将它砍断；追到门外时，他发现一个被遗留的男婴，便带回抚养。
男孩渐渐长大，容貌越来越像普伊尔。特尔农听说王后失子受罚的遭遇，把线索联系起来，带着孩子前往宫廷说明发现经过。男孩的身世终于得到确认，里安农不必再承担虚假的罪名，儿子后来取名普里德里。这场重逢提前结束惩罚，并不意味着她曾经真的伤害过婴儿。

en.title: Rhiannon’s Ordeal and the Returning Child
en.summary: When Rhiannon’s baby vanishes, frightened attendants manufacture evidence that she killed him. She must endure a humiliating punishment at the palace gate. Elsewhere, Teyrnon rescues a mysterious infant whose growing resemblance to Pwyll eventually reunites the family and clears her.
paragraphs: In the First Branch of the Welsh Mabinogi, Rhiannon and Pwyll finally had the heir their household awaited. Six women watched over the baby, but all fell asleep one night. On waking, they found him gone. Fearing punishment for their negligence, they killed a puppy, smeared its blood on the sleeping queen, and accused her of devouring her own child.

Unable to prove her innocence, Rhiannon was sentenced to seven years beside the mounting block outside the palace. She had to recount the accusation and offer to carry visitors inside. Meanwhile, Teyrnon guarded his mare during foaling. He cut off a monstrous claw reaching for the newborn foal, pursued its owner, and discovered an abandoned baby boy, whom his household raised.

As the boy grew, Teyrnon noticed his resemblance to Pwyll. Hearing about the missing royal child and Rhiannon’s disgrace, he connected the events and brought his foster son to court. His account enabled the family to recognize the child, later named Pryderi. Rhiannon’s punishment ended before its full term: the reunion exposed a false accusation, not a mother’s actual violence.

cosmos.name: 彼岸
cosmos.desc: 爱尔兰叙事中多样的超凡领域，可在海岛、湖底或丘中显现，并非一律等同死者的归宿。

cosmos.name: 神丘
cosmos.desc: 丘陵与古冢常被叙事视为超凡居民的居所或入口，其意义与具体地景、名称和地方记忆相连。

cosmos.name: 人间海路
cosmos.desc: 航海叙事以熟悉的海洋连接未知世界，边界既是空间距离，也涉及知觉、时间和禁忌的改变。

myths.note: 凯尔特是比较性总称，本条不把爱尔兰、威尔士、布列塔尼诸传统混成一部经典。中世纪抄写者的基督教背景与早期材料相互交织，现代复兴实践也各有差别。

myths.name: 罗马神话
myths.subtitle: 从炉火到城墙，神意写入公共生活
myths.description: 罗马神话生长在家宅仪式、国家祭祀与城市起源的叙述之中，也长期吸收并改写希腊等地的故事。诸神守护边界、誓约、农事与共同体，英雄传说则讨论建城所需的选择和代价。它不只是希腊神名的替换表，更承载了罗马人理解历史与公共秩序的方式。
myths.era: 共和国及帝国时期文献与祭祀丰富，根基更早
myths.quote: 一座城先点亮炉火，才向远方伸出道路。

gods.name: 朱庇特
gods.title: 天空、誓约与国家秩序之神
gods.desc: 在罗马公共宗教中居重要地位，与雷霆、盟约和胜利相连。与宙斯的对应不抹除其本土祭祀意义。

gods.name: 雅努斯
gods.title: 门户、开端与过渡之神
gods.desc: 以双面形象著称，关乎门道、启始和时间转换。他不能被简单纳入希腊诸神的一一对应关系。

gods.name: 维斯塔
gods.title: 炉火与共同体的守护神
gods.desc: 连接家庭炉灶与罗马的公共圣火，祭祀强调延续和照护。她的重要性常通过仪式而非冒险故事显现。

stories.title: 埃涅阿斯背父离城
stories.summary: 特洛伊陷落时，埃涅阿斯背起父亲、牵着儿子离开火海。他所携带的不只是家人，还有家神与未来共同体的艰难使命。
paragraphs: 维吉尔《埃涅阿斯纪》把罗马的起源追索到特洛伊的毁灭。城池陷落之夜，埃涅阿斯必须在战斗、家人和神意之间作出选择。父亲安喀塞斯起初不愿离开，直到征兆改变决定，逃亡才成为可能的道路。
埃涅阿斯背起父亲，让儿子阿斯卡尼俄斯随行，妻子克瑞乌萨随后而来，却在混乱中失散。他返回寻找，最终只能接受不能挽回的别离。叙事中的责任不是毫无痛苦的服从，承担未来也意味着正视无法保全的一切。
父亲、儿子与被带走的家神，使逃亡的身影同时承载过去与尚未到来的时代。这是奥古斯都时代史诗对使命与祖源的塑造，并不是建城事件的直接记录。它的庄严之下，也始终留着流离、战争与失去的阴影。

stories.title: 罗慕路斯划定城界
stories.summary: 被遗弃的双生兄弟成长后筹划新城，却为征兆与城界发生争执。雷穆斯之死使罗马的开端同时带有创建共同体与亲族破裂的印记。
paragraphs: 罗慕路斯与雷穆斯的童年传说包含河中漂流、母狼哺育和牧人抚养等情节。长大后，他们恢复家族地位，又打算建立自己的城市。共同的身世没有消除竞争，谁应掌权、何处建城，很快成为难以调和的问题。
兄弟通过观鸟征兆争取资格，但鸟出现的先后与数目又引发争议。随后，雷穆斯越过新城界线而遇害；不同作者对行凶者和经过各有安排。城墙尚未完备，边界的神圣性就已被鲜血与不可逆的选择刻入叙事。
后世常把这故事当作罗马勇武的开端，它也能被读为对共同体暴力的反省：建立秩序的人，可能先破坏最亲近的关系。古代作者并未消除这一难题，反而让矛盾留在城市祖源之中，与罗马后来的内战经验相互回响。

stories.title: 萨宾妇女走入战阵
stories.summary: 罗马人在节庆中掳走萨宾妇女，随后与前来讨还女儿的亲族交战。被迫处于双方之间的妇女走入战阵阻止杀戮，促成共同统治，但和解并不能洗去掳掠的伤害。
paragraphs: 罗马建城传说中，新城缺少女子，向邻邦求婚又遭到拒绝。罗慕路斯便举行节庆，邀请周围居民携家人观看比赛，随后发出信号，让罗马男子抢走前来的年轻妇女。李维记述的这场掳掠不是自愿结亲；受害者被带离父母，所谓婚姻首先建立在强制与背叛宾客信任之上。
萨宾亲族没有接受既成事实，国王提图斯塔提乌斯带军攻打罗马。双方在城中激战时，被掳的妇女奔入兵刃之间，披散头发，恳求父亲与丈夫停止互相杀害。她们已经被迫与两个阵营发生联系，无论哪边获胜，失去父亲或丈夫的痛苦都将落在自己与孩子身上。
妇女的介入使战斗停下，两方首领随后议和，决定把居民合成一个共同体，由罗慕路斯和塔提乌斯共同统治。这是罗马作者解释早期共同体如何吸纳萨宾人的传统，不是可以独立核实的建城实录。妇女成功制止了眼前的杀戮，也不能反过来证明最初的掳掠正当或出于双方自愿。

en.title: The Sabine Women Enter the Battle
en.summary: Roman men abduct visiting women during a festival, provoking war with their Sabine relatives. The women intervene between the armies and help secure shared government. Their success in stopping further bloodshed does not excuse the coercion that created the conflict.
paragraphs: In Rome’s foundation tradition, the new settlement lacked women and failed to obtain marriage alliances with neighboring communities. Romulus invited families to a festival, then signaled his men to seize the young female visitors. Livy’s account describes an abduction, not a voluntary exchange of brides. The subsequent households began with coercion and the betrayal of people attending as guests.

The Sabines eventually marched under Titus Tatius to recover their relatives and attack Rome. During the fighting, the abducted women entered the space between the armies, their hair disordered, and appealed to fathers and husbands alike. Their forced position connected them to both sides. Whichever army won, the continuing slaughter would leave them mourning relatives and expose their children to further loss.

The intervention halted the battle and led the leaders to negotiate. Romans and Sabines formed a single community under the joint rule of Romulus and Tatius. Roman writers used this tradition to explain the incorporation of Sabines into early Rome; it is not an independently verified foundation record. Ending the immediate violence did not make the original seizure consensual or justified.

stories.title: 努马与林泉中的埃革里亚
stories.summary: 努马继位后希望约束罗马的战争习性，声称在林中向女神埃革里亚请教祭仪。传说把宗教制度归于这场相会，诗人又写他死后女神悲泣，最终化成泉水。
paragraphs: 罗慕路斯之后，罗马传说中的第二任国王努马被请来治理城市。面对惯于用兵的居民，他试图用祭仪、节期与神圣约束改变生活的节奏。李维记述他常独自进入有泉水的林地，并宣称在那里与埃革里亚相会，关于敬神的安排都是听从这位女神的教导而制定。
努马设立或整理祭司职务，把不同神明的祭礼交给相应人员，又划分历法，使人们知道何时举行公共仪式。林中会谈为这些安排赋予神圣权威，而不是留下可供旁人旁听的议事记录。李维的叙述也把这种说法放在国王治理人心的策略中，不能直接当作女神亲授制度的史实。
奥维德后来另写努马死后的埃革里亚：她退入阿里奇亚的林谷，不断哭泣，连希波吕托斯讲述自身苦难也不能使她停止悲伤。狄安娜最终怜悯她，把她化成清冷的泉水。于是国王留下祭祀制度，女神则以泉水延续哀悼；这是诗人的后续叙事，不应与李维的文字混作同一记录。

en.title: Numa and Egeria in the Sacred Grove
en.summary: Numa seeks to turn Rome from constant warfare toward regulated religious life. He attributes his instructions to meetings with Egeria beside a woodland spring. Later poetry follows the grieving goddess after his death, giving their association a different, watery ending.
paragraphs: After Romulus, Roman tradition made Numa the city’s second king. He sought to temper a population accustomed to warfare by establishing religious obligations and a shared calendar. Livy describes his solitary visits to a grove with a spring, where he claimed to meet the goddess Egeria. Instructions attributed to her gave divine authority to the practices he introduced among the Romans.

Numa organized priestly offices, assigned the care of particular rites, and regulated the calendar so that public worship followed an established order. Meetings in the grove provided a sacred explanation for these decisions, not a transcript that other citizens could examine. Livy also presents the claim as a ruler’s means of governing minds; it should not be mistaken for verified divine legislation.

Ovid later tells what happened to Egeria after Numa died. She withdrew to the wooded valley at Aricia and wept inconsolably; even Hippolytus’s account of his own suffering could not relieve her grief. Diana finally transformed the mourning nymph into a cool spring. The king left religious institutions behind, while this poetic continuation gave his companion an enduring form of lament.

stories.title: 雅努斯开启门后的沸泉
stories.summary: 萨宾军逼近罗马，朱诺替来敌移开门闩，雅努斯便引出掺有硫黄的沸泉阻路。奥维德借神明自述，说明当地祭坛的来历，以及战时开门、和平关门的仪式含义。
paragraphs: 奥维德《岁时记》中，诗人询问雅努斯，为何他在罗马特定的门旁享有祭祀。神明回忆萨宾王塔提乌斯攻城之时，塔尔佩娅贪求臂饰，引导敌军登上堡垒。军队沿坡路走向谷地与广场，朱诺又把挡路的门闩移开，原本保护城市的通道突然向进攻者敞开。
雅努斯不愿与强大的朱诺正面争斗，转而运用自己掌管开合的力量。他先把硫黄放进水道，再开启泉口，让滚沸的水突然冲向来路。萨宾军不能穿过灼热的水流，被迫退下；危险解除以后，水泉恢复平常面貌，当地则为这次援助设立祭坛与小祠，以谷物和饼献祭。
诗人接着问，为何雅努斯的门在战争中打开、和平时反而关闭。神回答，开门为远征的民众留出归路，关门则让和平不要离去。这是奥维德公开讲述的城邦祭祀起源，不是关于私人幸运的泛泛寓言；沸泉解围与门的仪式相连，也不表示萨宾战争从此没有其他冲突。

en.title: Janus Opens the Boiling Springs
en.summary: When Juno unbars a Roman gate for the advancing Sabines, Janus opens another passage: springs made scalding with sulphur. Ovid connects this rescue to a local shrine and explains why the god’s doors open during war but close during peace.
paragraphs: In Ovid’s Fasti, the poet asks Janus why a particular Roman gateway belongs to his worship. The god recalls the attack of the Sabine king Tatius. Bribed with the promise of armlets, Tarpeia admitted enemies to the citadel. They descended toward the valley and forums, while Juno removed the bars of a gate that should have blocked their advance.

Unwilling to confront Juno directly, Janus used his own power over openings. He placed sulphur in the water channels, then opened the mouths of the springs. Scalding water rushed out and prevented the Sabines from passing. After the attackers were repulsed, the place returned to its ordinary appearance. A small shrine and altar commemorated the intervention with offerings of grain and cake.

The poet then asks why the god’s doors stand open during war and close during peace. Janus explains that departing citizens need an open road home, whereas closed doors keep peace from leaving. Ovid thus supplies a specific public narrative about a shrine and its ritual, not a general promise of personal luck or an account ending every Roman conflict.

stories.title: 普罗塞耳皮娜与刻瑞斯的寻找
stories.summary: 普罗塞耳皮娜被冥王掳走，刻瑞斯遍地寻女，使田野失去收成。朱庇特允诺归还，却因少女已吃冥界石榴而改为分居两界，此篇依奥维德的罗马改写叙述。
paragraphs: 在奥维德的《变形记》中，普罗塞耳皮娜在西西里采花，冥王狄斯突然驾车出现，把她强行带走。少女呼喊母亲，鲜花从衣襟散落，泉水女神库阿涅试图阻止，也没能拦下车辆。冥王以权杖裂开大地，带她进入地下；留在地上的母亲刻瑞斯并不知道女儿被带往何处。
刻瑞斯举着火炬走过各地，后来在泉水中发现女儿遗落的腰带，又从阿瑞图萨那里得知她已经身处冥界。愤怒的母亲让耕作失去成果，种子与田野不能继续供养人类。她向朱庇特要求归还女儿，得到附带条件的答复：只有少女尚未吃过冥界食物，才可完全返回地上。
然而普罗塞耳皮娜已在冥界吃下石榴籽，并有目击者作证。朱庇特于是安排她每年一半时间陪伴母亲，一半留在冥界，刻瑞斯才让大地重新结实。这里采用奥维德的平分年岁结局；它是罗马诗人接受希腊得墨忒耳故事的版本，不能拿别的传本种子数量推算所有叙述的月份。

en.title: Proserpina and the Search of Ceres
en.summary: Dis abducts Proserpina, and Ceres searches for her daughter while withholding the earth’s harvest. Jupiter permits a return, but food eaten below prevents a permanent reunion. Ovid’s Roman adaptation ends with the daughter dividing each year equally between two realms.
paragraphs: In Ovid’s Metamorphoses, Proserpina gathers flowers in Sicily when Dis appears in his chariot and carries her away. She calls for her mother as flowers fall from her clothing. The spring goddess Cyane attempts to stop the abduction, but cannot prevail. Dis strikes open a route beneath the earth, leaving Ceres without knowledge of where her daughter has gone.

Ceres searches widely with burning torches. Finding her daughter’s discarded belt and hearing Arethusa’s report, she learns that Proserpina is in the underworld. She prevents the land from producing its harvest and appeals to Jupiter for her child’s return. He makes full restoration conditional upon one requirement: the girl must not have eaten any food in the realm below.

Proserpina has already eaten pomegranate seeds, and a witness reports it. Jupiter therefore divides her year equally between her mother and the underworld; Ceres allows the earth to bear again. This follows Ovid’s Roman adaptation of Greek Demeter traditions. Its division should not be recalculated from seed counts borrowed from other tellings, as though every ancient account used one calendar.

cosmos.name: 天界
cosmos.desc: 天上神明与征兆关联公共决策和祭祀，但罗马宗教并不依赖一幅统一完整的宇宙层级图。

cosmos.name: 冥府
cosmos.desc: 拉丁文学中的亡者领域吸收多种传统；史诗中的游历路线不能代表所有罗马人的死后观。

cosmos.name: 家宅与城界
cosmos.desc: 炉火、门槛和划定的城界都可具有宗教意义，神圣空间不仅在远方，也存在日常生活之中。

myths.note: 本条区分拉丁文学叙事与公共、家庭宗教实践。罗马帝国境内信仰高度多样，吸收希腊、伊特鲁里亚及其他传统，不等于所有地方都遵循同一套神谱。

myths.name: 两河神话
myths.subtitle: 泥版留住洪水，也留住人的追问
myths.description: 两河神话汇聚苏美尔、阿卡德、巴比伦与亚述等不同语言和时代的传统，泥版上的故事随抄写不断改编。城市各有守护神，王权、洪水、农田与死亡构成反复出现的主题。相近神名可以互相对应，却不意味着所有故事从一开始就属于同一部神圣经典。
myths.era: 公元前三千纪起文字材料渐丰，跨多个古代政体流传
myths.quote: 泥土记得洪水，人仍向星辰追问归期。

gods.name: 伊南娜／伊什塔尔
gods.title: 爱情、战争与权力的女神
gods.desc: 两名分别属于不同语言脉络，后来广泛对应。她兼具欲望、战力与王权关联，不能仅称爱情女神。

gods.name: 恩基／埃阿
gods.title: 智慧与地下淡水之神
gods.desc: 在多种故事中以谋略和技艺帮助众神或人类。苏美尔与阿卡德称名之间的关联有历史发展过程。

gods.name: 马尔杜克
gods.title: 巴比伦城的主神
gods.desc: 随巴比伦政治与宗教地位上升而获得突出位置，在《埃努玛·埃利什》中成为建立宇宙秩序的战胜者。

stories.title: 伊南娜下到冥界
stories.summary: 伊南娜进入妹妹埃列什基伽勒掌管的冥界，每过一道门便失去一件饰物。她倒下后获救，却必须面对冥界索取替代者的规则。
paragraphs: 在苏美尔语的下冥界叙事中，伊南娜离开天上与地上的职责，前往埃列什基伽勒的国度。出发之前，她嘱咐侍从宁舒布尔：若自己不能回来，便向诸神求助。这个预先安排使她的冒险从一开始便带着危险的自觉。
经过七道门时，她的冠冕、饰物与衣着逐一被取下，最后以失去权势标记的状态面对冥界。她遭到裁决而死，身体被悬挂起来。外界的援助随后到来，恩基设计的使者以恰当回应接近冥界女王，取得复生的机会。
然而返归并非没有条件，冥界要求有人替代，杜穆兹因此卷入故事。后续牵连哀悼、追逐与轮替，不宜简化为一次胜利的探险。阿卡德语《伊什塔尔下冥界》另有结构与细节，不能把两个版本任意接成同一篇章。

stories.title: 吉尔伽美什寻找不死
stories.summary: 恩奇都的死亡迫使吉尔伽美什踏上远行。他找到洪水的幸存者，听见长生的秘密，却最终失去能使人返老还童的植物。
paragraphs: 吉尔伽美什与恩奇都共同经历远征，也因行动触动诸神的裁决。恩奇都死去后，强大的乌鲁克王第一次如此切身地面对自身终将死亡。他离开城墙与王座，穿越荒野，去寻找获得特殊生命的乌特纳皮什提姆。
旅程把他带到常人难至的边缘，洪水幸存者向他讲述诸神毁灭人类而又留下余生的往事。吉尔伽美什无法完成不眠的考验，后来虽取得使衰老者恢复青春的植物，却在沐浴时被蛇夺走，努力再次落空。
他终究返回乌鲁克，史诗把目光重新投向城墙、生活与可传述的经验。故事不是说悲伤可以轻易消失，而是让人的有限成为必须承认的事实。泥版有残缺也有不同编次，今日常读的长篇是漫长传承累积的结果。

stories.title: 阿达帕错失生命之食
stories.summary: 阿达帕折断南风的翅膀，被召到天神面前。埃阿告诫他不要吃喝天上的食物，他依言拒绝，却错过神明提供的生命之食；智慧与服从没有使凡人获得永生。
paragraphs: 阿达帕是埃里都侍奉埃阿的智者，拥有非凡知识，却没有永恒生命。一次他出海捕鱼，南风把船吹翻，他愤而诅咒，折断南风的翅膀，使风连续多日不能吹动。天神阿努察觉异常，追问原因，命人召来这位敢于伤害风的凡人，阿达帕因此必须离开日常祭祀之地接受询问。
埃阿先教他怎样应对：穿上丧服，在天门前为杜穆兹与宁吉什兹达哀悼，争取两位神的好感。他又警告，若有人给他死亡之食与死亡之水，绝对不要接受，却可以使用衣服与油。阿达帕照着指示进入天庭，门神替他说话，阿努听过解释后，反而命人拿来生命之食和水。
阿达帕牢记告诫，拒绝进食饮水，却接受衣服并涂上油。阿努追问他为何不吃，得知这是埃阿的叮嘱，便让他返回地上，生命的机会已被错过。现存传本有残缺与差异，埃阿为何如此告诫也存在解释争论；不能额外编出他承认蓄意欺骗的对白，来替这个含混结局定案。

en.title: Adapa Refuses the Food of Life
en.summary: After disabling the South Wind, Adapa must answer to Anu in heaven. Ea prepares him for the encounter and warns him against heavenly food. His faithful refusal nevertheless passes over an offer of life, leaving wisdom unable to secure immortality.
paragraphs: Adapa serves Ea at Eridu and possesses exceptional understanding, but not everlasting life. While he is fishing at sea, the South Wind overturns his boat. In anger, he breaks the wind’s wings, preventing it from blowing for several days. Anu notices the disturbance and summons the mortal responsible. The wise attendant must now explain himself before the ruler of heaven.

Ea tells Adapa to wear mourning clothes and lament Dumuzi and Ningishzida at heaven’s gate, winning their support. He also warns him not to consume the food and water of death, although clothing and oil may be accepted. Adapa follows these instructions. The gatekeepers speak favorably for him, and Anu, after hearing the case, orders food and water of life instead.

Remembering Ea’s warning, Adapa refuses to eat or drink, while accepting clothing and anointing himself with oil. Asked why, he names his teacher’s instructions. Anu sends him back to earth, the opportunity lost. Surviving witnesses are incomplete and differ; Ea’s purpose remains debated. The narrative does not supply an additional confession proving that the advice was deliberately designed to deceive him.

stories.title: 埃塔纳乘鹰寻找生育之草
stories.summary: 没有继承人的埃塔纳听从沙马什指引，救起陷坑中的鹰，盼它带自己升天取得生育之草。大地在脚下渐渐缩小，他却因恐惧要求返回，残存泥版没有保全完整结局。
paragraphs: 一只鹰曾与蛇起誓，住在同一棵树上，彼此照顾幼兽，后来却背弃盟约，吃掉蛇的孩子。蛇向太阳神沙马什申诉，依照指引藏入牛尸，趁鹰下来啄食时将它抓住，损伤翅膀并抛进坑里。鹰无法自行脱身，只能祈求援助；与此同时，基什王埃塔纳因为缺少继承人而苦恼。
埃塔纳请求沙马什帮助自己找到生育之草，神便指向困鹰所在。他来到陷坑，给鹰食物，照料它恢复羽翼，换取带自己飞上天空的帮助。鹰让国王贴紧身体，抓住羽毛，然后一层层向上飞去。途中它不断让他俯看下方，原本广大的田野与海水逐渐缩成小块，最后几乎不再可见。
升得越高，埃塔纳越害怕，终于请求停止飞行，返回地面；鹰护着他下降，这次尝试没有替他取回所求。后续残篇又涉及梦境与升天，但泥版缺损使完整收束无法确定。苏美尔王表另记他有儿子巴利赫，却不能用那条王统记录填成他在这篇故事中必然拿到神草的结尾。

en.title: Etana Rides the Eagle Toward Heaven
en.summary: Without an heir, Etana seeks a plant of birth and rescues an eagle at Shamash’s direction. The bird carries him upward, but the shrinking earth terrifies him. He asks to descend, while damaged tablets leave the larger adventure’s conclusion incomplete.
paragraphs: An eagle and a serpent once swore friendship and raised their young in the same tree. The eagle broke the oath by eating the serpent’s offspring. Following Shamash’s advice, the serpent hid inside a bull’s carcass, caught the feeding eagle, damaged its wings, and abandoned it in a pit. Elsewhere, King Etana of Kish suffered because he lacked an heir.

Etana prayed to Shamash for the plant of birth. The god directed him to the trapped eagle, which he fed and helped recover. In return, it agreed to carry him into heaven. Holding tightly to its body and feathers, he rose through successive heights. The eagle repeatedly asked him to look down, where land and sea grew smaller and eventually almost disappeared.

Frightened by the height, Etana asked to return, and the eagle supported his descent. This attempt did not bring back the plant. Further fragments concern dreams and renewed ascent, but damaged tablets prevent a secure reconstruction of the complete ending. The Sumerian King List separately gives Etana a son, Balih; that notice cannot simply supply a missing scene of successful retrieval.

stories.title: 马尔杜克与提亚马特的战争
stories.summary: 原初神族的冲突使提亚马特组织军队，马尔杜克则以胜利后拥有最高权威为条件迎战。他用风与箭杀死海神，整理宇宙并安排人类劳役，巴比伦神的地位由此确立。
paragraphs: 巴比伦《埃努玛埃利什》中，年轻众神的喧闹引发原初神族冲突。提亚马特起初反对毁灭后代，后来在阿普苏被埃阿杀死以及新的纷争之后，转而组织可怕的军队。她把命运之板交给统帅金古，众神不敢迎战；马尔杜克于是提出条件，若自己取胜，众神必须承认他的最高号令。
神会确认马尔杜克的权力，他备好弓箭、网与诸风，驾车迎向提亚马特。交战时，他用网罩住她，把恶风送入她张开的嘴里，使她无法合口，随后以箭射穿身体，杀死这位对手。他又制服她的军队，取走金古持有的命运之板，原先压倒众神的联盟因此瓦解，胜者开始支配战后安排。
马尔杜克把提亚马特的身体剖开，以其中一半架成天空，设置守卫约束水域，又安排星辰与历法。金古后来被处死，埃阿依照计划用他的血创造人类，让人承担供养诸神的劳役。众神修建巴比伦并赞颂马尔杜克的名号；这篇创世诗同时确立神的等级，不只是勇士消灭一头怪兽。

en.title: Marduk’s War Against Tiamat
en.summary: Conflict among the first generations of gods brings Tiamat’s army against younger divinities. Marduk accepts battle in exchange for supreme authority. His victory establishes cosmic arrangements and humanity’s labor, while the poem exalts Babylon and its god within a divine hierarchy.
paragraphs: In the Babylonian Enuma Elish, noisy younger gods provoke conflict among the primordial powers. Tiamat initially opposes destroying her descendants, but after Ea kills Apsu and further disputes arise, she assembles a terrifying army. She gives its commander, Qingu, the Tablet of Destinies. Marduk offers to fight only if victory will establish his commands as supreme among the assembled gods.

The divine assembly confirms his authority. Armed with bow, net, and winds, Marduk rides against Tiamat. He encloses her in the net and drives an evil wind into her open mouth, preventing it from closing. An arrow pierces her body and kills her. He then captures her forces and removes the Tablet of Destinies from Qingu, breaking the opposing coalition.

Marduk divides Tiamat’s body, setting up one half as heaven and stationing guards to restrain its waters. He orders stars and the calendar. Qingu is executed, and Ea uses his blood to fashion humans who will perform the gods’ labor. The gods build Babylon and praise Marduk’s names. Creation here establishes divine hierarchy as well as defeating a formidable opponent.

stories.title: 恩基为世界安排职掌
stories.summary: 恩基巡视大地，使河流田野获得供养，并把耕作、牧养与纺织分派给不同神明。伊南娜见诸神各有职责，前来质问自己的位置，恩基便列举她已有的力量回应抱怨。
paragraphs: 苏美尔诗《恩基与世界秩序》并不从空无讲起，而是让已经拥有神权的恩基巡视大地，确认城邦、山野与海域的命运。他赞颂苏美尔与乌尔，为土地安排繁盛，也让河流水量丰盈。世界的问题不是还没有天地，而是河渠怎样通水、牲畜怎样养活、诸神各自负责什么。
恩基把具体事务逐项交付：有人照看河流与灌溉，有人掌管农田与谷物，牧神管理牲畜，杜穆兹照料羊圈牛栏，使诸神的餐桌获得乳脂与食物。他又安排边界、城邑和田地，把纺织交给乌图女神。分工从流水一直延伸到衣物，神圣秩序因而落实在人们每天从事的生产活动中。
伊南娜却哭着来到恩基面前，列举姐妹们掌握的接生、书写与渔业，质问为何自己没有职掌。恩基回应她，指出她已经拥有装饰、男女生活以及扰动战场的力量，并非被排除在秩序之外。诗末虽有缺行，仍以赞颂恩基收束；这里没有另篇伊南娜与恩基故事中酒后运走神力的情节。

en.title: Enki Assigns the World Its Duties
en.summary: Enki travels through an existing world, supplying waterways and assigning divine responsibility for farming, herding, and weaving. Inanna complains that other goddesses have received defined functions while she has not. His answer recalls her established powers rather than inventing another landscape.
paragraphs: The Sumerian poem Enki and the World Order does not begin with an empty universe. Enki already holds divine authority when he surveys lands, cities, and waters and determines their fortunes. He blesses Sumer and Ur and makes the rivers abundant. The task is to organize an inhabited world: channels need water, animals need care, and divine responsibilities need definition.

Enki assigns oversight of waterways, agriculture, and grain, while pastoral divinities supervise wild and domestic animals. Dumuzi’s sheepfolds and cattle pens supply rich food for divine tables. Boundaries, cities, and fields receive their places, and the goddess Uttu receives responsibility for textile work. From flowing water to finished clothing, the poem locates sacred organization within the practical activities that sustain human communities.

Inanna approaches Enki in tears, naming the functions her sisters have received in childbirth, writing, and fisheries. Where, she asks, are her own duties? Enki answers by listing her existing powers over adornment, relations between the sexes, and upheaval in battle. Although the closing passage is damaged, the poem ends in praise of Enki, not with another tale’s removal of divine powers.

cosmos.name: 阿普苏
cosmos.desc: 与地下淡水及原初存在相关，苏美尔语对应词常译阿勃祖；名称在不同文本中兼有多重意义。

cosmos.name: 天与地
cosmos.desc: 宇宙的主要区分，也与诸神分工、城市神庙和政治秩序相连，不同时代的创世安排各不相同。

cosmos.name: 无返之地
cosmos.desc: 冥界在许多作品中是不易返回的死者之域，其门、守卫和生活状态依文本呈现不同细节。

myths.note: 两河是地理总称，不是单一民族或宗教。苏美尔故事、阿卡德史诗及巴比伦创世诗在此分开标明，神名对应仅为阅读便利，不主张它们历来完全相同。

myths.name: 印度神话
myths.subtitle: 莲花初开，时间在劫与劫之间呼吸
myths.description: 印度拥有众多宗教、语言与地方叙事，本条主要介绍印度教史诗和往世书中的神圣故事。诸神的化现、宇宙周期与维护正法的行动，连接日常祭祀与哲学思考。同一故事可因教派、地区和表演传统而变化，不应把印度全部信仰压缩成一套固定的众神关系。
myths.era: 吠陀时代至史诗、往世书传统层累发展，持续传承
myths.quote: 海被搅动之时，光与毒也一同醒来。

gods.name: 毗湿奴
gods.title: 维系宇宙秩序的神
gods.desc: 在毗湿奴派等传统中具有至高地位，以不同化身回应世界危机；其意义不能仅由功能分工概括。

gods.name: 湿婆
gods.title: 苦行、转化与宇宙之舞的神
gods.desc: 兼有静坐苦行者和家庭成员等形象，在湿婆派中被尊为至高者，毁灭也可通向更新与解脱。

gods.name: 提毗
gods.title: 女神的多种神圣显现
gods.desc: 是女神的称谓，可显现为杜尔迦等多种形态；在性力派传统中，女神是宇宙根本力量与至高实在。

stories.title: 搅动乳海
stories.summary: 天神与阿修罗合力搅动乳海，以山作杵、以蛇为绳，求取甘露。海中先后涌出宝物与剧毒，所得并非只有期待中的长生。
paragraphs: 天神失去力量后，依照毗湿奴的指引，与阿修罗合作搅动乳海。曼陀罗山成为搅杵，蛇王婆苏吉成为长绳；当山难以稳立时，毗湿奴以龟的化身承托它。巨大的行动需要对立者暂时携手，也需要可靠的支撑。
海中陆续出现宝物、神圣存在与危险的毒。湿婆承接剧毒，喉部因此呈现青色，这一行动使求取甘露的过程免于毁灭。故事提醒读者，深处被唤醒的并不只有财富，维系世界还需要有人面对难以承受的部分。
甘露出现后，分配又引发冲突，毗湿奴的迷人化现参与其中。不同往世书对涌出之物、先后与争夺细节有不同说法。它既是壮阔的宇宙叙事，也仍在讲诵、节庆与图像中被重新理解，不能仅作奇观清单观看。

stories.title: 杜尔迦迎战水牛魔
stories.summary: 水牛魔摩希沙压迫诸神，众神的光辉汇成女神的显现。杜尔迦接受诸般武器，与不断变换形态的敌手交战，恢复受损的秩序。
paragraphs: 《女神颂》等传统讲述摩希沙夺取诸神地位，使世界陷于威胁。诸神的愤怒与光辉汇聚，显现为威严的女神，诸般武器交到她手中。在这一神圣叙事里，女性力量不是附属点缀，而是面对危机的决定性存在。
杜尔迦乘狮出战，对手及其军队以猛烈攻势和变化形态抵抗。摩希沙在水牛、人物与其他形态间转换，女神最终制伏并击败他。图像中踏住水牛、举持武器的姿态，凝聚了这场持续交锋的关键时刻。
故事在杜尔迦祭与其他节庆中仍具有活态意义，也被解释为神圣母性、保护与克服傲慢的显现。不同地区的仪式、图像和讲法不完全相同；尊重这一点，便不会把节庆中的敬奉简单看作对古代战争故事的演出。

stories.title: 象头神的诞生
stories.summary: 帕尔瓦蒂造出守门的少年，少年因不认湿婆而坚守命令，冲突中被斩首。为平息母亲的悲痛，湿婆使他获得象头重生，并授予他领众与先受礼敬的地位。
paragraphs: 在《湿婆往世书》流传的一种版本中，帕尔瓦蒂以沐浴时身体上的膏垢造出一个少年，赋予生命，吩咐他守在门口，不许任何人进入。湿婆回来时，少年并不知道这位神是谁，只认母亲的命令，挡住入口。守门者的忠诚由此变成一场众神也卷入的冲突。
湿婆的随从无法轻易制服少年，双方争战升级，最终湿婆斩下他的头。帕尔瓦蒂得知儿子被杀，悲痛而震怒，威胁使世界陷入毁灭。诸神于是请求补救，湿婆命随从寻找可以接续的头颅；他们带回象头，将它安放到少年身上，使他重新获得生命。
复生的少年被确认为帕尔瓦蒂的儿子，也被湿婆接纳，受封为群众之主，成为象头神伽内什。众神承诺在重要礼仪开始时先向他致敬，冲突由承认与恢复秩序结束。印度教另有不同的诞生叙事，这里只讲其中一支，不把所有象头由来合成一段。

en.title: The Birth of Ganesha
en.summary: Parvati creates a boy to guard her door. His obedience brings him into conflict with Shiva, who kills him without recognizing their bond. An elephant’s head restores his life, and divine recognition establishes his honored place in worship.
paragraphs: In one version transmitted in the Shiva Purana, Parvati fashions a boy from material rubbed from her body while bathing and gives him life. She commands him to guard her entrance and admit nobody. When Shiva returns, the boy does not know who he is. Remaining loyal to his mother’s instruction, he blocks the doorway, beginning a confrontation that draws in other divine beings.

Shiva’s attendants cannot easily overcome the young guardian. Fighting escalates until Shiva cuts off his head. When Parvati learns that her son has been killed, grief becomes terrible anger, threatening the world’s stability. The gods seek a remedy. Shiva sends attendants to obtain a replacement head; they return with an elephant’s head, which is placed upon the boy’s body to restore his life.

The restored child is acknowledged as Parvati’s son and accepted by Shiva. He becomes Ganesha, lord of the divine hosts, and receives the honor of being invoked before important undertakings and rites. Recognition and renewed life resolve the household conflict. Hindu traditions preserve other birth accounts as well; this telling follows one Puranic strand rather than merging every explanation of his elephant head.

stories.title: 克利须那托举戈瓦尔丹山
stories.summary: 牧人原要祭祀因陀罗，克利须那劝他们敬奉养育牛群的山林。暴雨随之而来，他举起戈瓦尔丹山，让村人和牲畜避雨七日，最终使因陀罗收回愤怒。
paragraphs: 《薄伽梵往世书》讲述，弗林达文的牧人准备向掌管雷雨的因陀罗献祭，年幼的克利须那却询问父亲难陀为何举行仪式。他劝大家重视牛群、牧人的职责与供给草木水源的戈瓦尔丹山。牧人听从建议，备下食物，敬奉山与牛，并绕山行礼。
因陀罗认为牧人怠慢自己，调来猛烈的雨云，风雨与冰雹袭击村落，牛群和居民无处躲避。克利须那见他们受苦，举起整座戈瓦尔丹山，如同撑起巨伞，招呼众人带着牲畜来到山下。大家离开露天的险地，在他托举的山体下面聚集，等待风暴过去。
他连续托山七天，牧人们与牛群平安避过暴雨。因陀罗见自己的力量不能迫使他们屈服，终于止住风雨；天空放晴后，克利须那让大家离开，再把山放回原处。后续叙事中因陀罗前来认错，这场灾难以护佑和谦卑收束，也是信众持续纪念的宗教故事。

en.title: Krishna Lifts Mount Govardhana
en.summary: Krishna persuades the herders to honor the mountain, cattle, and work that sustain their community rather than perform their customary offering to Indra. A devastating storm follows. By lifting Govardhana for seven days, Krishna shelters everyone and humbles the storm’s sender.
paragraphs: In the Bhagavata Purana, the herders of Vraja prepare an offering to Indra, the deity associated with rain. Young Krishna questions his father Nanda about the ceremony. He urges the community to honor their cattle, their pastoral duties, and Govardhana, whose environment sustains their livelihood. They accept his counsel, prepare abundant food, worship the mountain and cows, and proceed around the mountain together.

Indra interprets the change as an insult and unleashes devastating clouds. Wind, rain, and hail batter the settlement, leaving people and cattle exposed. Seeing their distress, Krishna lifts Mount Govardhana like an enormous umbrella. He invites the herders to bring their families and animals beneath it. The community gathers in this extraordinary refuge while the storm continues to rage outside their shelter.

For seven days Krishna holds the mountain aloft, protecting the herders and their cattle. Indra realizes that his power cannot break their refuge and recalls the storm.
