His contentious relationships in poetry should be distinguished from cult practice: divine stories explored authority and vulnerability rather than supplying uncomplicated moral examples.

figures.name: 赫拉
figures.title: 婚姻秩序与王后尊荣的维护者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 赫拉是克洛诺斯与瑞亚之女，也是宙斯的姐妹与妻子，在奥林波斯拥有王后地位。她与婚姻、合法结合及女性人生阶段有关；阿尔戈斯和萨摩斯的崇拜显示，她绝非只依附丈夫而存在。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 伊娥被宙斯变成母牛后，赫拉令百眼巨人阿耳戈斯看守；赫尔墨斯杀死守卫，她又派牛虻追逐伊娥。赫拉还长期阻挠赫拉克勒斯，使其出生延迟并派蛇袭击婴儿。史诗中的她则支持阿开亚军，与宙斯围绕特洛伊战争激烈角力。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 赫拉常戴高冠、持权杖或石榴，表现庄严王后形象。孔雀与她的关联尤见于后期传统，尾羽的眼状图案被解释为死去阿耳戈斯的百眼。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 萨摩斯赫拉神庙与阿尔戈斯赫拉圣域都是重要祭祀中心。地方仪式重视婚姻与群体身份；文学中的嫉妒形象，不应遮蔽她独立而复杂的宗教地位。

en.name: Hera
en.title: Guardian of marriage and royal dignity

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Hera is a daughter of Cronus and Rhea, sister and wife of Zeus, and queen among the Olympians. Her religious concerns include marriage, legitimate unions, and female life transitions. Important sanctuaries at Argos and Samos demonstrate her substantial independent standing.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: After Zeus transformed Io into a cow, Hera entrusted her to the many eyed Argus. Hermes killed the guardian, and Hera sent a gadfly to torment Io. She also obstructed Heracles from birth. In the Iliad, her determined support for the Achaeans repeatedly brings her into conflict with Zeus himself.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A high crown, sceptre, and sometimes a pomegranate mark Hera as queen. Later traditions associate her with the peacock, explaining its patterned feathers as the preserved eyes of her dead guardian Argus.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The sanctuaries of Hera at Samos and Argos anchored regional worship and collective identity. Ritual attention to marriage and womanhood differs from literary portrayals of jealousy; those stories should not erase her independent religious authority or local significance.

figures.name: 雅典娜
figures.title: 智慧与城邦的守护者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 雅典娜是宙斯之女，赫西俄德说宙斯吞下怀孕的墨提斯，后来她全副武装从父亲头部出生。她兼掌谋略、纺织与城市保护，以处女神身份维护雅典，也帮助英雄完成艰难任务。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 雅典娜与波塞冬竞争雅典的守护权，献出橄榄树，与海神制造的咸水泉形成对照。她指引珀耳修斯借盾面反光斩杀美杜莎，又在《奥德赛》中屡次化身援助奥德修斯和忒勒马科斯，使漂泊的父亲能够返乡并夺回家园。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 头盔、长矛、圆盾与埃癸斯构成武装形象，胸前常见蛇发女妖头像。猫头鹰代表敏锐观察，橄榄树则关联城邦资源；纺织工具提示她的工艺职能。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 泛雅典娜节以游行、竞技和献织袍纪念女神，帕特农神庙彰显城邦权力。她的军事智慧强调策略与纪律，但各地崇拜并不完全等同雅典的政治解释。

en.name: Athena
en.title: Guardian of wisdom, crafts, and the city

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Athena is the daughter of Zeus. In Hesiod, he swallows the pregnant Metis before Athena emerges armed from his head. A virgin goddess of strategy, weaving, and civic protection, she guards Athens while guiding heroes through difficult and dangerous undertakings.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Athena competed with Poseidon for patronage of Athens, offering an olive tree against his saltwater spring. She helped Perseus approach Medusa through a reflected image rather than a fatal direct glance. In the Odyssey, her disguises and advice protect Telemachus and enable Odysseus to recover his household after prolonged wandering.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Her helmet, spear, shield, and aegis distinguish the armed goddess. A Gorgon head often appears on her breast. The owl suggests alert perception, while olive branches and weaving tools express civic prosperity and skill.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The Panathenaic festival celebrated Athena through procession, contests, and presentation of a woven robe. The Parthenon linked her to Athenian power. Her wider Greek worship nevertheless included local traditions that cannot be reduced to one city’s political ideology.

figures.name: 阿波罗
figures.title: 预言、音乐与净化之神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 阿波罗是宙斯与勒托之子，阿耳忒弥斯的兄弟，传统称他出生于提洛岛。他关联神谕、乐艺、弓箭及疫病与疗愈；古希腊的太阳神原本是赫利俄斯，两者的认同主要见于后期发展。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 阿波罗在德尔斐杀死巨蛇皮同，建立著名的神谕中心，女祭司皮提亚传达他的启示。《伊利亚特》开篇，他因祭司受辱而向阿开亚军营射下瘟疫。另一故事中，他追逐达芙涅，少女化为月桂，他遂将月桂作为自己的标志。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 里拉琴、弓箭和月桂冠最易识别阿波罗，雕像常呈无须青年。乌鸦、海豚和三足鼎也与他有关，其中三足鼎尤其指向德尔斐神谕的祭祀环境。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 德尔斐神谕参与殖民、战争与净化事务，皮提亚赛会兼有音乐和竞技。阿波罗并非单纯温和的艺术神；准确的弓箭与瘟疫同样体现其可怖权能。

en.name: Apollo
en.title: God of prophecy, music, and purification

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Apollo is the son of Zeus and Leto and brother of Artemis, traditionally born on Delos. He governs prophecy, music, archery, disease, and healing. Helios was originally the distinct Greek sun god; stronger identification between the two developed in later traditions.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Apollo killed the serpent Python at Delphi and established the sanctuary where the Pythia delivered divine responses. At the opening of the Iliad, he sends plague against the Achaean camp after his priest is dishonoured. Another story describes his pursuit of Daphne, whose transformation into laurel ends her attempted escape.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A lyre, bow, and laurel wreath identify Apollo, normally shown as a youthful, beardless figure. Ravens, dolphins, and the tripod also belong to his imagery, with the tripod particularly recalling Delphic divination.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Delphi advised communities about colonisation, conflict, and ritual purification. Its Pythian festival included musical and athletic competition. Apollo should not be reduced to gentle artistic inspiration: his precise arrows and power over plague make him an equally formidable presence.

figures.name: 阿耳忒弥斯
figures.title: 荒野、狩猎与成长边界的女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 阿耳忒弥斯是宙斯与勒托之女，阿波罗的姐妹，常作为拒绝婚姻的处女猎神出现。她保护野生动物，又能将其猎杀，并关注少女成长和分娩；她与月亮的认同不能取代早期独立的塞勒涅。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 阿克泰翁意外看见阿耳忒弥斯沐浴，遭她变成鹿，最终被自己的猎犬撕裂。尼俄柏夸耀子女众多、轻视勒托，阿耳忒弥斯与阿波罗便射杀她的儿女。伊菲革涅亚的故事则存在献祭与被女神以鹿替换、迁往陶里斯的不同结局。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 短衣、弓箭、箭囊和鹿表现她的荒野行动力，身旁也可能出现猎犬。以弗所的阿耳忒弥斯具有特殊地方造型，不宜直接按希腊少女猎神解释。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 布劳伦的少女仪式将她与成长和群体过渡联系起来，以弗所神庙则展现另一套地方传统。她既守护生命边界也施加死亡，体现荒野的双重力量。

en.name: Artemis
en.title: Goddess of wilderness, hunting, and transitions

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Artemis is the daughter of Zeus and Leto and sister of Apollo. A virgin huntress, she both protects and kills wild animals, and oversees girls approaching adulthood and childbirth. Her later lunar associations should not obscure the originally distinct moon goddess Selene.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: When Actaeon saw Artemis bathing, she transformed him into a stag, and his own hunting dogs destroyed him. She and Apollo also killed Niobe’s children after their mother insulted Leto. Stories of Iphigenia differ: some describe sacrifice, while others let Artemis substitute a deer and transport the girl to Tauris.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A short hunting dress, bow, quiver, deer, and hounds express her mobility outside settled society. The distinctive cult image of Artemis at Ephesus belongs to a local tradition rather than simply reproducing this huntress.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Rituals at Brauron connected Artemis with girls and transitions toward adulthood. Her Ephesian sanctuary expressed a different regional identity. Protection and sudden death coexist in her character, reflecting the dangerous boundaries between human settlement, bodily change, and wild nature.

figures.name: 波塞冬
figures.title: 海洋、地震与马匹的驾驭者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 波塞冬是克洛诺斯与瑞亚之子，宙斯及哈迪斯的兄弟。泰坦战争后，他抽签获得海洋领域，但其权能并不限于海水：古老称号撼地者和与马匹相关的崇拜，显示其跨越陆海的力量。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 奥德修斯刺瞎独眼巨人波吕斐摩斯后，波塞冬应儿子的请求阻挠英雄归航，以风暴和海难延长其漂泊。他与雅典娜争夺雅典时击出咸水泉；在特洛伊传说中，他曾修筑城墙，却因拉俄墨冬拒付报酬而派海怪惩罚当地。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 三叉戟是最鲜明的标志，常与蓄须男性、海豚和海马共同出现。他也驾驭马拉战车；马的意象提醒观者，海神并不是仅有航海职能的神祇。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 科林斯地峡赛会奉献给波塞冬，苏尼翁海岬的神庙连接航路与城邦景观。航海者祈求其平息波涛，地震频发的希腊社会也敬畏他的撼地能力。

en.name: Poseidon
en.title: Lord of seas, earthquakes, and horses

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Poseidon is a son of Cronus and Rhea and brother of Zeus and Hades. After the Titan war he received the sea by lot. His ancient title Earth Shaker and strong associations with horses reveal powers extending far beyond maritime travel.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: After Odysseus blinded the Cyclops Polyphemus, Poseidon answered his son’s appeal by obstructing the hero’s return with storms and shipwreck. He competed with Athena for Athens by striking a saltwater spring. At Troy, he helped build the walls, then sent a sea monster when King Laomedon withheld the promised payment.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The trident identifies Poseidon, often represented as a mature bearded man accompanied by dolphins or sea horses. Horse drawn chariots also appear, recalling an important dimension of his power beyond the open sea.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The Isthmian Games near Corinth honoured Poseidon, while his sanctuary at Sounion overlooked major sea routes. Sailors sought calm passages, but communities exposed to earthquakes also feared him. Maritime protection and destructive instability remained inseparable aspects of his worship.

figures.name: 哈迪斯
figures.title: 冥界与地下财富的君主

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 哈迪斯是克洛诺斯与瑞亚之子，在兄弟分掌宇宙时获得地下亡者领域。他并非死亡本身的化身塔纳托斯，也不是邪恶魔王；普路同这一称号强调地下矿产与农业生长所含的财富。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《得墨忒耳颂》叙述哈迪斯经宙斯同意带走珀耳塞福涅，引发得墨忒耳停止谷物生长。他让少女吃下石榴籽，使她必须定期返回冥界。俄耳甫斯以音乐求回欧律狄刻时，他允许亡妻随行，却规定出境之前不可回头观看。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 权杖、双齿叉、丰饶角与守门犬刻耳柏洛斯常见于其图像。隐形头盔出现在英雄故事中；严肃的王座形象，比近代流行的恶魔造型更合古代传统。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 希腊人常以委婉称号称呼冥界之主，部分祭祀与大地和丰饶相连。有关来世的观念因时代、地域和秘仪而异，不能拼成一套始终统一的冥界教义。

en.name: Hades
en.title: Ruler of the dead and underground wealth

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Hades is a son of Cronus and Rhea who received the realm of the dead when the brothers divided cosmic territories. He is distinct from Thanatos, personified death, and is not a devil. His title Plouton emphasises wealth hidden beneath the earth.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In the Homeric Hymn to Demeter, Hades takes Persephone with Zeus’s approval, provoking her mother to suspend agricultural growth. Pomegranate seeds bind Persephone to recurring residence below. When Orpheus seeks Eurydice, the underworld rulers permit her return on the condition that he does not look back before reaching the surface.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A sceptre, two pronged staff, cornucopia, and the watchdog Cerberus accompany Hades. His helmet grants invisibility in heroic narratives. Ancient images usually present a solemn enthroned king rather than a demonic adversary.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Greeks often used respectful or euphemistic names for the underworld ruler. Some cult contexts connected him with earth and abundance. Beliefs about the dead differed across periods, places, and mystery traditions, rather than forming one universally fixed ancient doctrine.

figures.name: 阿佛洛狄忒
figures.title: 欲望、魅力与结合的女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 阿佛洛狄忒的身世有不同谱系：赫西俄德称她从乌拉诺斯被割下的生殖器所激起的海沫诞生，荷马则称她为宙斯与狄俄涅之女。她掌管吸引、性欲和结合，且在部分城市拥有武装形态。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 特洛伊王子帕里斯评判三位女神的美貌时，阿佛洛狄忒许诺让他得到海伦，从而赢得金苹果，并卷入战争起源。她与凡人安喀塞斯结合，生下埃涅阿斯；在阿多尼斯故事中，她哀悼青年猎人的死亡，使爱情与失落紧密相连。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 鸽子、桃金娘、玫瑰和海中贝壳构成常见意象，厄洛斯常随侍其旁。裸体或出浴形象在古典后期尤为著名，但早期与地方神像也可着衣甚至持械。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 塞浦路斯帕福斯和基西拉是重要崇拜地点，显示她与海上交流的联系。其近东关联值得比较，但不能简单认作异名；古代所谓圣娼制度也须谨慎考证。

en.name: Aphrodite
en.title: Goddess of desire, attraction, and union

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Aphrodite has differing genealogies. Hesiod makes her arise from sea foam surrounding the severed genitals of Uranus; Homer calls her the daughter of Zeus and Dione. She governs attraction, sexuality, and union, while some communities also honoured her in armed forms.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: During the judgement of Paris, Aphrodite promised the Trojan prince Helen and won the golden apple, helping set the Trojan conflict in motion. Her union with the mortal Anchises produced Aeneas. In traditions concerning Adonis, her grief for the young hunter connects erotic attachment with vulnerability, mourning, and irreversible loss.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Doves, myrtle, roses, and marine shells accompany Aphrodite, often with Eros nearby. Famous nude or bathing images represent only part of her iconography: earlier and local forms could be clothed or armed.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Paphos on Cyprus and Cythera were important centres of worship, reflecting maritime connections. Comparisons with Near Eastern goddesses are useful but should not erase differences. Claims about widespread institutional sacred prostitution require particular caution and critical assessment of evidence.

figures.name: 奥丁
figures.title: 智慧、诗歌与战死者之主

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 奥丁是包尔与贝斯特拉之子，阿萨神族的重要领袖，与兄弟维利、韦杀死原初巨人尤弥尔并塑造世界。他追求知识而非全知，既关联王权与诗歌，也支配战争、狂喜和部分战死者的归宿。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《高人的箴言》叙述奥丁在风吹之树上悬挂九夜，以自身献祭自身而获得卢恩知识。他又以一只眼睛换取密米尔泉的饮水，并冒险取得诗蜜。诸神黄昏中，他虽预知灾难并集结英灵战士，仍将被巨狼芬里尔吞噬而死。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 独眼、宽檐帽、长矛冈格尼尔与八足马斯莱普尼尔是常见标志。乌鸦胡金与穆宁巡游世界带回消息，两只狼随侍；这些伙伴突出知识与战场的联系。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 主要叙事见于中世纪冰岛保存的埃达与萨迦，文本书写晚于北欧改宗。诗歌、地名和考古材料可补充其崇拜背景，但不能把奥丁视为所有北欧社群唯一的最高神。

en.name: Odin
en.title: Seeker of wisdom and lord of the battle dead

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Odin, son of Borr and Bestla, is a leading god of the Aesir. With his brothers Vili and Ve he kills the primordial Ymir and shapes the world. He pursues knowledge rather than possessing omniscience, governing poetry, kingship, frenzy, and battle.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In Havamal, Odin hangs for nine nights on a windswept tree, offering himself to himself and gaining knowledge of runes. He sacrifices an eye for a drink from Mimir’s well and steals the mead of poetry. Despite foreknowledge and his gathering of fallen warriors, Fenrir will swallow him at Ragnarok.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: One eye, a broad hat, the spear Gungnir, and the eight legged horse Sleipnir identify Odin. His ravens Huginn and Muninn gather information; accompanying wolves reinforce his association with battlefields and the dead.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Medieval Icelandic Eddas and sagas preserve most extended narratives, after conversion to Christianity. Poetry, place names, and archaeology supply other evidence. These materials reveal varied traditions, not proof that every Scandinavian community treated Odin as its sole supreme deity.

figures.name: 索尔
figures.title: 雷霆与人神世界的守护者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 索尔是奥丁与大地女神约尔德之子，妻子为金发的西芙。他以强大体力和直接行动著称，保护阿斯加德与人类世界免受巨人威胁；与奥丁的隐秘谋略相比，他的角色更突出公开对抗。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 巨人索列姆盗走雷神之锤并索求弗蕾雅为妻，索尔在洛基协助下乔装新娘，取回锤子后击杀巨人。他也曾出海钓起环绕世界的巨蛇耶梦加得，双方终将在诸神黄昏互相杀死；索尔击毙巨蛇后只走九步便因蛇毒倒下。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 雷神之锤妙尔尼尔、力量腰带和铁手套是重要装备，两只山羊拉动其战车。锤形护符具有明确考古证据，既可显示守护期待，也可表达佩戴者的宗教身份。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 雷神之名保存在地名、人名和星期名称中，锤形饰物在维京时代广泛出现。文学中既有滑稽乔装，也有宇宙大战，不能以现代英雄形象替代古代多样传统。

en.name: Thor
en.title: Thunderer and defender of gods and humans

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Thor is the son of Odin and the earth goddess Jord, and husband of Sif. Renowned for strength and direct action, he protects divine and human communities against giants. His confrontational manner differs from the secrecy and shifting strategies frequently associated with Odin.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: When Thrym steals Mjolnir and demands Freyja as his bride, Thor disguises himself as the bride with Loki’s assistance. Once the hammer is returned, he kills the giants. Elsewhere he fishes for the world serpent Jormungandr. At Ragnarok he kills that enemy, then falls after nine steps from its venom.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Mjolnir, a strengthening belt, and iron gloves are his characteristic equipment. Two goats pull his chariot. Archaeologically attested hammer pendants suggest protective associations and could also communicate religious affiliation within changing Scandinavian societies.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Thor survives in personal names, place names, and weekday terminology. Hammer pendants were widespread during the Viking Age. Medieval stories range from comic disguise to cosmic combat; modern superhero adaptations should not be mistaken for complete representations of historical traditions.

figures.name: 洛基
figures.title: 越界、机巧与灾变的推动者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 洛基是法布提与劳菲之子，与阿萨诸神共同活动，却具有复杂的巨人亲缘。他能改变形体与性别，既为诸神排解危机也不断制造危险；芬里尔、耶梦加得和赫尔是他与安格尔博达所生的子女。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 洛基剪去西芙的头发后，被迫请矮人工匠打造金发，并促成雷神之锤等宝物诞生。他化为母马引走筑墙者的骏马，后来生下八足马。另一叙事中，他引导盲神霍德尔用槲寄生杀死巴德尔，最终遭绑缚，并受滴落蛇毒折磨。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 洛基没有像雷神之锤那样稳定、明确的古代专属徽记。鲑鱼、母马和捕网来自具体变形故事，绑缚与毒蛇则指向惩罚；现代角盔并非可靠的古代识别标志。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 洛基故事主要由中世纪冰岛文献保存，其独立祭祀证据十分有限。他不能简单等同基督教魔鬼；协助、嘲讽和破坏在同一角色中并存，形成北欧神话的张力。

en.name: Loki
en.title: Shapeshifter, boundary crosser, and catalyst

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Loki is the child of Farbauti and Laufey and a companion of the Aesir with complicated giant connections. Changing form and gender, he solves divine problems while creating new dangers. With Angrboda he fathers Fenrir, Jormungandr, and Hel, figures associated with catastrophe.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: After cutting Sif’s hair, Loki commissions golden replacements from dwarfs, indirectly producing several divine treasures. As a mare, he distracts a builder’s stallion and later bears Sleipnir. He also guides blind Hodr’s fatal use of mistletoe against Baldr. The gods eventually bind him beneath a serpent whose dripping venom causes torment.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Loki lacks an unambiguous ancient emblem comparable to Thor’s hammer. Salmon, mare, and fishing net belong to particular transformations. Bonds and a venomous snake evoke punishment; modern horned helmets are not reliable historical attributes.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Medieval Icelandic texts preserve most Loki narratives, while evidence for an independent cult is very limited. He should not simply be equated with the Christian devil. Assistance, mockery, and destruction coexist in a figure whose ambiguities drive divine stories.

figures.name: 弗蕾雅
figures.title: 爱欲、魔法与战场选择的女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 弗蕾雅属于华纳神族，是尼约德之女、弗雷尔的姐妹，在两族和解后进入阿萨诸神的世界。她关联爱欲、财富与赛德魔法，也在弗尔克旺接纳部分战死者，因而不能只称为爱情女神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《巨人索列姆之歌》中，巨人以归还雷神之锤为条件索求弗蕾雅，她愤怒拒绝，项链随震动弹起，迫使索尔另谋乔装之策。另一些传统叙述她寻找远行的丈夫奥德尔，并流下红金般的眼泪，显示欲望、离别和财富的相互联系。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 布里辛加门项链、猫拉战车与可供飞行的鹰羽外衣是常见标志。野猪希尔迪斯维尼也与她相关；金色泪珠和华美首饰强调珍贵财富与情感代价的关联。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 埃达诗歌与斯诺里著作保存了不同面向，部分地名也被联系到她的崇拜。赛德魔法与性别规范的关系复杂，不宜用现代女巫或浪漫爱情标签概括她的权能。

en.name: Freyja
en.title: Goddess of desire, magic, and the battle dead

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Freyja belongs to the Vanir, daughter of Njord and sister of Freyr, entering the Aesir’s world after reconciliation between divine groups. Associated with desire, wealth, and seidr magic, she also receives a share of slain warriors in Folkvang, exceeding a purely romantic role.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In the poem about Thrym, the giant demands Freyja in exchange for Thor’s stolen hammer. Her angry refusal shakes her necklace and forces the gods to adopt a different plan involving Thor’s disguise. Other traditions describe her search for her absent husband Odr and tears that become precious red gold.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The necklace Brisingamen, a chariot drawn by cats, and a feather garment enabling flight identify Freyja. The boar Hildisvini also accompanies her. Golden tears connect precious wealth with longing and emotional loss.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Eddic poetry and Snorri’s prose preserve different aspects of Freyja, supplemented cautiously by place names. Seidr involved complex relations with gender and social authority. Modern categories of romantic goddess or witch therefore capture only fragments of her historical character.

figures.name: 弗雷尔
figures.title: 丰收、和平与王权繁荣之神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 弗雷尔属于华纳神族，是尼约德之子、弗蕾雅的兄弟，在神族和解后与阿萨诸神共同居住。他关联雨水、阳光、土地丰收和社会和平，也与瑞典王族的神圣祖先传统相连，居所称为亚尔夫海姆。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 弗雷尔坐上高座，望见巨人女子格尔德后陷入苦恋，派侍从斯基尔尼尔前往求婚。《斯基尔尼尔之歌》呈现礼物、威胁与咒术交织的谈判，最终约定相见。他为此交出的宝剑后来不在身边，诸神黄昏时遂无法抵挡火焰巨人苏尔特。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 金鬃野猪古林布尔斯提、可折叠收起的宝船斯基德布拉德尼，以及丰饶性的男性形象与弗雷尔相关。野猪强调光辉和生命力，宝船则显示便利航行与充足资源。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 瑞典地方记忆与英格林王族谱系突出他的繁荣王权，部分考古像的身份仍有争论。求婚诗中的强迫语言应被如实说明，而不宜美化为没有冲突的田园爱情。

en.name: Freyr
en.title: God of harvest, peace, and prosperous kingship

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Freyr belongs to the Vanir, son of Njord and brother of Freyja. After the divine groups reconcile, he lives among the Aesir. He governs sunshine, rain, agricultural abundance, and peace, and features in Swedish royal ancestry traditions. Alfheim is named as his dwelling.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: From a high seat Freyr sees the giant woman Gerd and becomes overwhelmed with desire. His servant Skirnir negotiates the union through gifts, threats, and curses, eventually securing a meeting. Freyr gives away his sword in connection with this mission. At Ragnarok, lacking that weapon, he falls against the fiery Surtr.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Freyr possesses the golden bristled boar Gullinbursti and the foldable ship Skidbladnir. Fertile male imagery is also associated with him. These attributes connect radiance, movement, abundant resources, and reproductive power rather than agriculture alone.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Swedish traditions and Yngling royal genealogies emphasise prosperity and sacred kingship. Identification of some archaeological images remains disputed. The coercive language in his courtship poem deserves acknowledgement rather than being softened into an entirely peaceful romance of seasonal fertility.

figures.name: 提尔
figures.title: 勇气、誓约与牺牲之神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 提尔是北欧神祇中与战斗勇气和约束性承诺相关的一位，其父系在文献中并不统一，有称奥丁，也有称巨人希密尔。他的名字与更古老的日耳曼神名传统相连，但早期地位不能直接从词源重建。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 诸神畏惧芬里尔不断增长的力量，便用矮人制作的细索格莱普尼尔试图束缚它。巨狼怀疑欺骗，要求一位神将手放入自己口中作为担保；只有提尔应允。当芬里尔发现无法挣脱，便咬断提尔的右手，使担保成为真实而永久的代价。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 缺失的右手是最有叙事依据的识别点，狼与束缚绳索可辅助辨认。提瓦兹卢恩与其名字相关，但现代用符的含义多有再造，不能直接代表古代全部信仰。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 英语星期二的名称保存了其日耳曼同源神名，埃达资料则集中表现失手的牺牲。称他为现代意义的法律部长过于简化，勇武、信用和必要欺骗之间的冲突更为关键。

en.name: Tyr
en.title: God of courage, pledges, and costly sacrifice

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Tyr is associated with martial courage and binding commitments. Surviving texts disagree about his ancestry, naming Odin or the giant Hymir as his father. His name connects with an older Germanic divine vocabulary, but etymology alone cannot securely reconstruct his earlier religious status.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Fearing Fenrir’s growing strength, the gods persuade the wolf to test the slender magical bond Gleipnir. Suspecting deception, Fenrir demands a divine hand in his mouth as security. Tyr alone accepts. When the wolf discovers that the bond cannot be broken, he bites off Tyr’s right hand, exacting the promised pledge.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The missing right hand is Tyr’s clearest narrative attribute; a wolf and binding cord can clarify the scene. The Tiwaz rune relates to his name, although modern symbolic applications often introduce meanings not securely documented.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Tuesday preserves the name of Tyr’s Germanic counterpart in English. Eddic narratives concentrate on his costly pledge. Calling him a modern legal administrator is misleading: the story exposes tensions between courage, trustworthy guarantees, communal survival, and necessary divine deception.

figures.name: 巴德尔
figures.title: 死亡与复归希望中的光辉神祇

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 巴德尔是奥丁与弗丽嘉之子，妻子为南娜，儿子为福尔塞提，居所称布雷达布利克。斯诺里将他写成美丽、明亮而广受赞誉的神，但直接把他定义为太阳神，并无足够早期材料支持。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 巴德尔梦见死亡后，弗丽嘉要求万物发誓不伤害他，却漏掉看似幼弱的槲寄生。洛基利用这一缺口，引导盲眼霍德尔射出致命枝条。赫尔答应若万物为他哭泣便放人，女巨人索克却拒绝；诸神黄昏之后，他将从亡者世界归来。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 槲寄生、葬船与妻子南娜的形象最能提示其故事，明亮面貌主要来自文学描写。古代没有充分证据支持一套固定太阳轮徽记，现代光之王形象应谨慎使用。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 埃达与萨克索笔下存在明显不同的巴德尔叙事，后者更接近英雄竞争故事。死亡、哀悼和复归可作比较研究，但不能据相似情节直接认定源自基督教或季节仪式。

en.name: Baldr
en.title: Radiant god of death, mourning, and return

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Baldr is the son of Odin and Frigg, husband of Nanna, and father of Forseti. His dwelling is Breidablik. Snorri describes him as beautiful, radiant, and widely praised, but securely identifying him as a solar deity goes beyond the surviving early evidence.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: After Baldr dreams of death, Frigg obtains promises from almost everything not to harm him, overlooking mistletoe. Loki exploits the exception and guides blind Hodr in delivering the fatal missile. Hel offers release if all beings mourn, but the giantess Thokk refuses. After Ragnarok, Baldr is expected to return from death.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Mistletoe, a funeral ship, and Nanna evoke Baldr’s narratives. Radiant appearance derives principally from literary description. Evidence does not establish a universal ancient solar emblem, despite influential modern representations of a shining divine prince.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Eddic accounts differ markedly from Saxo’s more heroic narrative of rivalry. Death, mourning, and return invite comparison with other traditions. Such parallels, however, do not by themselves establish direct Christian borrowing or prove an underlying annual vegetation ritual.

figures.name: 海姆达尔
figures.title: 诸神边界与虹桥的警戒者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 海姆达尔是守护诸神边界的重要神祇，传统称其由九位母亲所生，居住在接近虹桥的希明约格。他拥有极敏锐的听觉与视力，睡眠需求极少，能在昼夜之间持续警戒来自巨人世界的威胁。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 诸神黄昏临近时，海姆达尔将吹响加拉尔号角，召集诸神迎战，最后与洛基相互杀死。《索列姆之歌》中，他提出让索尔乔装新娘取回神锤的办法。《里格之歌》的开头又把行旅者里格联系到他，叙述人类社会阶层的产生。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 加拉尔号角、虹桥与守望姿态是最可靠的识别线索，金牙也见于文学称号。公羊关联在研究中仍有讨论，若仅以角形头饰辨认，容易把现代设计当成古代定式。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 海姆达尔的材料零散分布于埃达诗歌、吟唱诗与斯诺里散文，彼此并非完整一致。社会起源诗反映等级想象，不能直接当作北欧历史社会组织的客观说明。

en.name: Heimdall
en.title: Watchman of the gods and guardian of boundaries

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Heimdall guards the divine boundary from his dwelling Himinbjorg near the rainbow bridge. Traditions give him nine mothers and extraordinary hearing and sight. Requiring very little sleep, he maintains watch by night and day against dangers approaching from the world of giants.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: At Ragnarok, Heimdall sounds Gjallarhorn to summon the gods, then ultimately kills and is killed by Loki. In the poem about Thrym, he proposes that Thor recover his hammer disguised as a bride. The introduction to Rigsthula identifies the travelling Rig with Heimdall before recounting the origins of human social ranks.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Gjallarhorn, the rainbow bridge, and a watchful stance are his clearest identifiers. Literary titles mention golden teeth. Proposed ram associations remain debated, so horned modern costume should not be treated as a fixed ancient attribute.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Evidence for Heimdall is scattered across Eddic poetry, skaldic verse, and Snorri’s prose, without forming one seamless biography. The social origins poem expresses an ideological hierarchy rather than providing a straightforward historical description of Scandinavian classes or institutions.

figures.name: 朱庇特
figures.title: 罗马公权力、天空与誓约的保障者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 朱庇特是罗马天空与雷霆的重要神，与朱诺、密涅瓦构成卡庇托利欧三神。他以至善至大者称号接受国家崇拜，守护誓言、条约和公共秩序；与希腊宙斯的认同并未消除其独特的罗马制度背景。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 罗马传统称努马王与朱庇特谈判，用象征性供物替代可怕的赎罪要求，并获得有关避雷仪式的知识。另一建国叙事中，罗慕路斯向止退者朱庇特许愿，请他阻止罗马军队溃逃。胜利将领举行凯旋时，则登上卡庇托利欧向他献祭。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 雷霆、鹰、权杖与橡叶冠是常见标志，神像多呈庄严蓄须男性。卡庇托利欧神庙的位置及凯旋献祭场景，往往比单独的鹰更能提示罗马政治语境。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 执政官就职、战争誓愿和凯旋礼均与朱庇特相关，祭司及占卜制度强化其公共地位。文学虽大量吸收希腊故事，理解他仍须兼顾罗马国家礼仪与公民责任。

en.name: Jupiter
en.title: Guarantor of Roman authority, sky, and oaths

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Jupiter is Rome’s major god of sky and thunder and a member of the Capitoline triad with Juno and Minerva. As Optimus Maximus he guards public order, treaties, and oaths. Identification with Greek Zeus never erased his distinctive place within Roman institutions.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Roman tradition describes King Numa negotiating with Jupiter over alarming expiatory demands, substituting symbolic offerings and learning lightning rituals. In another foundation story, Romulus vows a sanctuary to Jupiter Stator to halt a Roman retreat. Victorious commanders later conclude triumphal processions by ascending the Capitol and sacrificing to the god.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Thunderbolts, an eagle, sceptre, and oak wreath accompany Jupiter’s mature bearded image. The Capitoline temple and triumphal setting often communicate his specifically Roman public significance more clearly than an eagle alone can do.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Consular inaugurations, military vows, and triumphs involved Jupiter, supported by specialised priesthoods and divinatory procedures. Roman literature absorbed many Greek divine stories, but his role must also be understood through civic obligation, state ceremony, and the maintenance of public trust.

figures.name: 朱诺
figures.title: 罗马共同体与女性生命的守护者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 朱诺是罗马重要女神，与朱庇特和密涅瓦组成卡庇托利欧三神。她的称号分别体现王后尊荣、分娩援助和公共警示等功能；她与希腊赫拉长期对应，但罗马女性、公民共同体和地方城市赋予她独特位置。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 高卢人夜袭卡庇托利欧时，朱诺圣域的鹅发出叫声，传统认为警报使罗马守军及时应敌，并与莫奈塔称号相联。《埃涅阿斯纪》中，她因偏爱迦太基而阻挠特洛伊人，最后接受埃涅阿斯后代建立秩序，但要求拉丁人的名称和习俗延续。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 王冠、权杖和庄严长袍显示女神尊荣，孔雀来自与赫拉相通的图像传统。拉努维乌姆的救助者朱诺却披羊皮、持武器，展示鲜明的地方守护形象。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 三月的妇女节庆与卢基娜称号关注婚姻和生产，莫奈塔神庙又联系罗马铸币历史。不同称号与圣域功能不能压缩为嫉妒妻子，更不只是赫拉的拉丁译名。

en.name: Juno
en.title: Guardian of Roman community and women’s lives

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Juno is a major Roman goddess within the Capitoline triad alongside Jupiter and Minerva. Her titles express queenship, assistance in childbirth, and public warning. Although frequently identified with Hera, she occupied distinctive positions in Roman women’s lives, civic religion, and local Italian communities.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: During a Gallic attack on the Capitol, sacred geese associated with Juno raise an alarm and save the defenders, a tradition linked with Moneta. In the Aeneid, her loyalty to Carthage drives resistance to Aeneas. She finally accepts the future settlement while requiring the preservation of Latin names and customs.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A crown, sceptre, and stately robes convey Juno’s authority; peacocks reflect shared imagery with Hera. At Lanuvium, however, Juno Sospita wears goatskin and carries weapons, revealing a distinctly local protective and martial form.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The Matronalia and Juno Lucina concerned married women and childbirth, while Moneta’s temple became associated with minting. Her titles and local sanctuaries show functions beyond a jealous wife, making her much more than a Latin translation of Hera.

figures.name: 密涅瓦
figures.title: 技艺、学习与公共智慧的女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 密涅瓦是罗马工艺、技艺和智慧的重要女神，与朱庇特、朱诺共同受祀于卡庇托利欧。她的意大利背景与伊特鲁里亚门尔瓦传统有关，后来大量吸收雅典娜的形象，却仍联系罗马匠人、学校和行业生活。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 奥维德讲述织女阿拉克涅挑战女神，密涅瓦在织毯上展示诸神威严，少女则织出诸神的欺骗与侵害。冲突结束后，阿拉克涅变成蜘蛛继续编织。这个罗马文学版本既借用希腊题材，也通过技艺竞赛呈现权力、创作与惩罚的紧张关系。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 头盔、长矛、盾牌与猫头鹰常用于辨识密涅瓦，纺锤和织机则强调手艺。图像与雅典娜高度相似时，题铭、神庙位置和出土环境比造型本身更重要。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 奎因夸特鲁斯节与她关系密切，工匠、教师和学生均可参与相关庆祝。帝国时代又出现密涅瓦与地方神的结合，如不列颠苏利斯密涅瓦，显示崇拜的适应性。

en.name: Minerva
en.title: Patron of skilled work, learning, and civic wisdom

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Minerva is a Roman goddess of skilled work, knowledge, and wisdom, worshipped with Jupiter and Juno on the Capitol. Her Italian background connects with Etruscan Menrva. Greek Athena influenced her imagery strongly, but Roman craftspeople, teachers, and professional communities gave her particular social roles.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In Ovid’s account, Arachne challenges the goddess to a weaving contest. Minerva depicts divine authority, while the mortal exposes divine deception and sexual wrongdoing. The confrontation ends with Arachne transformed into a spider, still weaving. This Roman literary treatment of Greek material explores artistic excellence, unequal power, punishment, and contested representation.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Helmet, spear, shield, and owl identify Minerva, while spindle and loom emphasise skilled production. Because her appearance often resembles Athena’s, inscriptions, sanctuary locations, and archaeological settings can be more informative than costume alone.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The Quinquatrus festival involved Minerva and attracted craftspeople, teachers, and pupils. Imperial worship also produced local combinations such as Sulis Minerva in Britain. These traditions demonstrate adaptation within Roman religion rather than a single unchanging copy of Greek mythology.

figures.name: 马尔斯
figures.title: 罗马武力、祖源与土地的保护者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 马尔斯是罗马公共宗教的核心神祇之一，不仅关乎战争，也保护田地、群体与军事秩序。罗马人奉他为罗慕路斯与雷穆斯之父，由此把神的力量接入城市祖源；他与阿瑞斯的文学认同并不能概括全部职能。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 建城传统称维斯塔贞女雷娅西尔维娅与马尔斯生下双胞胎，婴儿被放逐到河边，后由母狼哺育。奥古斯都又以复仇者马尔斯名义纪念为凯撒复仇及收回军旗，将王朝叙事纳入神庙。相较希腊战神的失控暴力，这些故事突出罗马祖源与正当武力。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 头盔、长矛、盾牌和军装构成常见形象，狼与啄木鸟也与马尔斯相联。萨利祭司守护的圣盾和仪式舞蹈，提示武力同时受到传统礼仪的组织与约束。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 三月和十月的军政节庆与出征、归来相关，净田祭也向马尔斯祈求牲畜和作物安全。战神与农业保护并非互相矛盾，而是共同维护罗马群体存续的不同方面。

en.name: Mars
en.title: Protector of Roman arms, ancestry, and land

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Mars stands near the centre of Roman public religion, protecting warfare, fields, collective survival, and military discipline. As father of Romulus and Remus, he also anchors Roman ancestry. Literary identification with Ares does not encompass these civic, agricultural, and genealogical dimensions of his importance.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Foundation traditions make Mars the father of twins born to the Vestal Rhea Silvia. Exposed beside the river, the infants survive through a she wolf’s care. Augustus later promoted Mars Ultor to commemorate vengeance for Caesar and recovered military standards, integrating the god into dynastic memory and claims of legitimate force.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Helmet, spear, shield, and military dress identify Mars; the wolf and woodpecker also belong to his traditions. Sacred shields carried by the Salii and their ritual dancing connect armed strength with inherited ceremonial discipline.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: March and October ceremonies marked military departures and returns, while agricultural purification invoked Mars for crops and livestock. Warfare and rural protection were therefore complementary rather than contradictory roles, both concerned with safeguarding the Roman community and its resources.

figures.name: 维纳斯
figures.title: 魅力、繁衍与罗马祖源的女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 维纳斯在罗马关联魅力、性欲、繁衍与有利的神恩，后来与阿佛洛狄忒广泛融合。她作为埃涅阿斯的母亲，被纳入罗马祖源叙事；凯撒家族又借尤鲁斯的谱系，自称出自这位女神以支持政治地位。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《埃涅阿斯纪》中，维纳斯化装成女猎人向儿子指路，并使丘比特激发狄多的爱意，为特洛伊人争取庇护。后来她请伏尔坎打造铠甲，盾面展现罗马未来历史。这里的母亲角色不仅保护个人，也把情感、战争与帝国命运连接起来。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 鸽子、桃金娘、玫瑰、丘比特与贝壳是常见线索，持盾的胜利者形象也很重要。祖源女神与胜利女神的题铭，能提示同一形象背后不同的政治诉求。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 凯撒奉祀祖源者维纳斯，庞培则突出胜利者维纳斯，两者展示竞争性的政治使用。维纳斯节庆也涉及婚姻与性规范，因此不能只把她当作抽象美貌或浪漫爱情的化身。

en.name: Venus
en.title: Goddess of attraction, fertility, and Roman ancestry

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Venus concerns attraction, sexuality, fertility, and favourable divine influence in Roman tradition, later merging extensively with Aphrodite. As mother of Aeneas she enters Rome’s ancestral narrative. Caesar’s family claimed descent through Iulus, turning her genealogy into a source of political authority and distinction.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In the Aeneid, Venus guides her son disguised as a huntress and uses Cupid to awaken Dido’s love, securing refuge for the Trojans. Later she persuades Vulcan to make divine armour. Its shield depicts Rome’s future, connecting maternal protection with warfare, imperial destiny, and the emotional costs of founding a people.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Doves, myrtle, roses, Cupid, and shells commonly accompany Venus. Armed or shield bearing forms also matter. Inscriptions naming Venus Genetrix or Victrix clarify different ancestral and military claims behind apparently similar divine images.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Caesar promoted Venus Genetrix, while Pompey emphasised Venus Victrix, revealing competing political appropriations. Festivals also engaged marriage and sexual conduct. Her Roman significance therefore exceeds abstract beauty or romance, encompassing collective origins, victory, social regulation, and negotiated divine favour.

figures.name: 雅努斯
figures.title: 门户、开端与过渡的双面神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 雅努斯是罗马本土特色鲜明的神，掌管门户、开端、通行与状态转换，没有简单对等的希腊奥林波斯神。古代作者有时把他写成拉丁姆早期君王，有时赋予宇宙起始的意义，不同解释并存而非统一谱系。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 奥维德《岁时记》中，雅努斯解释自己的双面可以同时观看前后，又讲述曾收留来到意大利的萨图尔努斯。另一故事说萨宾人攻入时，他以突然喷发的热水阻挡敌军。其神庙门户在战争期间开启，和平时期关闭，成为政治宣示的重要仪式。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 面向相反方向的两张脸最易识别雅努斯，钥匙与手杖也表现开启和引导。门道、拱门或硬币上的双面头像，应与具体建筑或发行背景一起解释其意义。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 献祭祷告常先呼唤雅努斯，以确保仪式顺利开启，一月名称也与他相联。奥古斯都强调关闭神门以宣示和平，但这种象征不能等同帝国所有地区事实上毫无战争。

en.name: Janus
en.title: Two faced god of doorways and beginnings

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Janus is a distinctly Roman god of doorways, beginnings, passage, and changes of state, without a straightforward Olympian equivalent. Ancient writers sometimes describe him as an early ruler in Latium and sometimes give him a cosmic role. These interpretations coexist rather than forming one fixed genealogy.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In Ovid’s Fasti, Janus explains that his two faces watch opposing directions and recounts welcoming Saturn to Italy. Another account credits him with releasing hot water against invading Sabines. His sanctuary doors stood open during war and were closed in peace, making their ritual management a prominent statement about Roman public affairs.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Two faces looking in opposite directions are Janus’s clearest attribute. Keys and a staff express opening and guidance. Doorways, arches, and coin portraits require their architectural or monetary settings to clarify particular historical meanings.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Roman prayers often invoked Janus first so that ritual could begin successfully, and January preserves his name. Augustus publicised the closing of his doors as a sign of peace, but this symbolism did not mean warfare vanished throughout the empire.

figures.name: 达格达
figures.title: 爱尔兰诸神中的丰足与技艺之主

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 达格达是爱尔兰神话图阿哈德达南族的重要人物，常被称为好神，含义偏向多才多艺而非道德完美。他与布鲁纳博因的神圣景观相连，是安格斯与布里吉德等人物的父亲，但各文本谱系并不完全一致。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《第二次莫伊图拉之战》写达格达在大战前与莫莉甘相会，获得对抗弗莫尔人的援助。他曾被敌人以巨大份量的粥试探，却将食物吃尽；战后他的竖琴遭夺走，他召回竖琴，并奏出悲、笑、眠三种曲调，使敌人陷入无法抵抗的情绪。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 能使人死亡或复生的大棒、无人离开时仍饥饿的丰饶锅，以及可支配情绪的竖琴构成主要标志。夸张食量和粗朴衣着体现叙事幽默，并不意味着地位低微。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 主要资料由中世纪爱尔兰文献保存，抄写者处于基督教文化环境。巨石墓与其居所的联系属于后世神话地景，不能直接证明史前建造者已经用同一名字崇拜他。

en.name: The Dagda
en.title: Irish master of abundance and many skills

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: The Dagda is a major member of the Irish Tuatha De Danann. His title Good God indicates broad competence rather than flawless morality. Associated with the sacred landscape of Bru na Boinne, he fathers figures including Aengus and Brigid, although genealogies vary between sources.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In the Second Battle of Mag Tuired, the Dagda meets the Morrigan before confronting the Fomorians and gains assistance. His enemies test him with an enormous portion of porridge, which he consumes. When his harp is stolen, he summons it back and plays melodies producing grief, laughter, and sleep among his opponents.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: His great club can kill and restore life, his cauldron leaves nobody hungry, and his harp commands emotions. Exaggerated appetite and rough clothing supply narrative humour without cancelling his authority or considerable supernatural competence.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Medieval Irish manuscripts preserve the narratives within a Christian scribal environment. Connections between his dwelling and prehistoric passage tombs belong to later mythic geography; they do not establish that the original builders worshipped this named figure in the same way.

figures.name: 布里吉德
figures.title: 爱尔兰诗艺、医治与锻造的女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 布里吉德是爱尔兰传统中的女神，常被列为达格达之女。《科尔马克词汇集》将她与诗人相连，并提及同名的医治与锻造女神姐妹；这一材料可以说明多重职能，却不足以建立完整统一的三相女神教义。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《第二次莫伊图拉之战》中，布里吉德与布雷斯的儿子鲁阿丹进入敌方营地，试图杀害铁匠戈布纽，却在攻击后遭反杀。她来到战场为儿子哀哭，故事将爱尔兰的尖声哀悼起源联系到这一时刻，使诗艺、亲属冲突和战争创伤交织。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 诗歌、炉火、铁匠工具与疗愈活动可提示布里吉德的职能。灯火、圣井和编织十字更多关联后世圣布里吉德传统，使用时应标明时代，避免全部倒推为古代徽记。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 女神布里吉德与基尔代尔圣布里吉德之间存在复杂名称和传统联系，却不能简单视为同一人的连续传记。今日节庆、基督教敬礼与现代异教实践，应分别尊重其自身语境。

en.name: Brigid
en.title: Irish goddess of poetry, healing, and smithcraft

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Brigid is an Irish goddess commonly called the Dagda’s daughter. Cormac’s Glossary associates her with poets and mentions sisters bearing her name who oversee healing and smithcraft. This evidence suggests related functions but does not establish a fully articulated universal triple goddess theology.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In the Second Battle of Mag Tuired, Brigid’s son Ruadan, fathered by Bres, infiltrates the opposing camp and attacks the smith Goibniu. The smith survives and kills him in return. Brigid comes to lament her son, and the narrative connects this mourning with the first keening heard in Ireland during warfare.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Poetry, hearth fire, smithing tools, and healing activities evoke Brigid’s functions. Lamps, holy wells, and woven crosses often belong to Saint Brigid’s later traditions and should not automatically be projected into ancient goddess worship.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The goddess and Saint Brigid of Kildare share complex connections of name and tradition, not a securely continuous personal biography. Contemporary festivals, Christian devotion, and modern Pagan practices deserve interpretation in their respective settings rather than being collapsed into one timeless religion.

figures.name: 卢格
figures.title: 爱尔兰多艺者与战胜暴君的英雄神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 卢格是爱尔兰图阿哈德达南族的多艺者，父亲为基安，母亲为弗莫尔领袖巴洛尔之女埃丝纽。他因拥有多种技能得以进入塔拉王廷，并在战争中领导诸神；长臂者称号与战斗能力相关，不宜直接译成太阳神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 卢格来到努阿达的宫廷时，守门人说每一种技艺已有专才，他便指出无人能同时精通全部本领，最终获准入内。在第二次莫伊图拉大战中，他以投石攻击外祖父巴洛尔的致命眼睛，翻转敌军优势。另在《夺牛长征记》中，他帮助儿子库丘林疗伤。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 长矛、投石索与多种工艺工具可表现卢格的武力和全能，具体宝物名称随文本而变。将耀眼外貌直接解释为太阳轮崇拜，容易把较晚研究假说当成古代事实。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 卢格纳萨节与卢格及养母塔尔蒂乌的纪念传统相连，结合竞赛、集会和收获季节。大陆卢古斯与威尔士勒乌可供语言比较，但不能把三者故事无区别地拼接。

en.name: Lugh
en.title: Irish master of arts and victorious leader

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Lugh is the many skilled figure of the Irish Tuatha De Danann, son of Cian and Ethniu, daughter of the Fomorian Balor. His combined abilities secure entry to Tara’s court. The epithet Long Arm concerns exceptional reach or prowess, not an automatic identification with the sun.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: At Nuada’s court, the doorkeeper explains that every individual craft already has a specialist. Lugh replies that nobody possesses all his skills together and gains admission. At the Second Battle of Mag Tuired he strikes Balor’s destructive eye with a slingstone. In the Tain, he also helps heal his son Cu Chulainn.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A spear, sling, and varied craft implements express Lugh’s fighting skill and broad competence, though named treasures vary across texts. Reading every radiant description as proof of solar worship turns a scholarly hypothesis into supposed historical certainty.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Lughnasa connects Lugh with commemorations for his foster mother Tailtiu, assemblies, contests, and the harvest season. Continental Lugus and Welsh Lleu offer linguistic comparisons, but their surviving narratives should not be indiscriminately merged into one interchangeable pan Celtic biography.

figures.name: 莫莉甘
figures.title: 爱尔兰战场、预言与权力危机的女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 莫莉甘是爱尔兰叙事中关联战争、预言、牲畜和统治危机的女性神圣人物，名字常译作幻影王后或伟大王后，解释仍有争议。她与巴德布、玛哈等名称的关系随文本改变，不宜固定成一套整齐的三位一体。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《夺牛长征记》中，莫莉甘以女子形貌接近库丘林，遭拒后化成鳗鱼、狼和母牛干扰战斗，并在交锋中受伤。她后来伪装成挤奶老妇，从英雄的祝福中得到医治。莫伊图拉之战后，她又宣告胜利，并预言秩序衰败与灾难将临。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 战场上的乌鸦或渡鸦、变形动物和带有威胁的预言构成主要线索。鸟类意象既关联死亡也关联观察；现代黑翼女战士形象并不是中世纪文献唯一允许的外貌。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 她的故事保存在爱尔兰史诗与神话文献中，不能不加区分地推广为所有凯尔特地区的共同信仰。现代复兴宗教赋予她新的意义，需与中世纪文本证据分别说明。

en.name: The Morrigan
en.title: Irish power of battle, prophecy, and crisis

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: The Morrigan is an Irish supernatural female figure associated with warfare, prophecy, cattle, and threatened sovereignty. Her name is variously interpreted as Phantom Queen or Great Queen. Relationships with Badb, Macha, and other names vary between sources rather than defining a stable universal trinity.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In the Tain, the Morrigan approaches Cu Chulainn as a woman. Rejected, she obstructs him as an eel, wolf, and heifer, receiving injuries in the fighting. Disguised as an old milkmaid, she later gains healing through his blessings. Following Mag Tuired, she announces victory and foretells a future collapse of social order.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Battlefield crows or ravens, transformed animals, and threatening prophecy supply key identifiers. Bird imagery suggests both death and watchful knowledge. The modern black winged warrior woman is not the only appearance permitted by medieval narratives.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Irish epic and mythological texts preserve her changing roles; these cannot automatically stand for every Celtic speaking region. Modern revival religions give her additional meanings, which deserve respectful distinction from claims based specifically on surviving medieval textual evidence.

figures.name: 库丘林
figures.title: 爱尔兰阿尔斯特英雄与悲剧战士

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 库丘林是爱尔兰阿尔斯特叙事群的凡人英雄，原名塞坦塔，母亲为德赫蒂，父系常联系神祇卢格。他幼年杀死铁匠库兰的猛犬，答应暂代守卫，因此得到库兰之犬这一名字，其英雄身份从责任承诺开始。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《夺牛长征记》中，阿尔斯特战士遭虚弱诅咒时，年轻的库丘林独自守住渡口，阻挡康诺特军。他与昔日同窗费尔迪亚德连续决斗，最终以可怕的加耶博尔格杀死朋友，胜利却充满哀痛。死亡故事中，他将自己绑在石柱上，直到乌鸦落肩才被敌人确认已死。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 战车、长矛、猎犬以及战斗时身体扭曲的狂暴状态是重要标志。绑于石柱的垂死形象突出不屈，却也显示英雄身体的毁坏，而非不受限制的神圣无敌。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 主要文本由中世纪爱尔兰抄本保存，兼有散文、诗歌和不同版本。近现代民族运动与公共纪念重塑了他的形象，阅读时应区分早期英雄伦理与后来的国家象征。

en.name: Cu Chulainn
en.title: Tragic champion of the Irish Ulster tales

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Cu Chulainn is a mortal hero of Ireland’s Ulster Cycle, originally named Setanta. His mother is Deichtine, and his paternity is often connected with Lugh. After killing Culann’s fierce watchdog, he promises to replace its protection, earning the name Hound of Culann through responsibility.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In the Tain, while Ulster’s warriors suffer a debilitating curse, Cu Chulainn defends its border against the invading army of Connacht. His prolonged duel with former companion Fer Diad ends in a devastating victory using the Gae Bolga. In his death tale, he binds himself upright to a stone until a bird reveals his death.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A chariot, spear, hound, and the terrifying bodily distortion of battle frenzy identify him. The dying hero tied to a stone represents resistance but also physical destruction, rather than the effortless invulnerability of a god.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Medieval Irish manuscripts preserve prose, verse, and competing versions of his career. Modern nationalism and public monuments reshaped his image. Early heroic obligations, tragic violence, and later uses as a national emblem should therefore remain analytically distinct from one another.

figures.name: 里安农
figures.title: 威尔士四支故事中的尊荣与坚忍者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 里安农是威尔士《马比诺吉昂》四支故事的重要女性，首先出现于戴维德领主普伊尔的经历中，后来嫁给他并生下普里德里。她具有超常来历和行动能力，但现存文本并未直接把她列为一位拥有完整神谱的马女神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 普伊尔追赶骑白马的里安农，总是无法接近，直到开口请求她停下。两人成婚后，婴儿失踪，侍女将罪责嫁祸给她；她被罚在宫门背负来客。孩子获救归来后真相大白。第三支故事中，她又与普里德里一同消失在魔法囚禁之中，最终获释。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 缓缓前行却追不上的白马、宫门与背负旅人的惩罚最能辨识里安农。她的神鸟见于相关威尔士文本，歌声可影响生者与死者，但并非每段叙事都出现。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 里安农属于威尔士语文学传统，不能当作爱尔兰诸神家族的一员。与高卢埃波娜或古代马崇拜的联系属于比较研究，文本中的婚姻选择、诬告和尊严同样值得重视。

en.name: Rhiannon
en.title: Welsh figure of dignity, ordeal, and restoration

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Rhiannon is a central woman in the Welsh Four Branches of the Mabinogi, first encountered in the story of Pwyll, lord of Dyfed. She marries him and bears Pryderi. Although clearly extraordinary, the surviving narrative does not present a systematic divine genealogy or explicitly label her a horse goddess.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Pwyll cannot catch Rhiannon’s slowly moving white horse until he asks her to stop. After their marriage, her infant disappears and attendants frame her for his death. She must offer to carry visitors at the gate until the recovered child clears her name. Later, she and Pryderi disappear into magical captivity before eventual release.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The uncatchable white horse, palace gateway, and humiliating burden of visitors identify Rhiannon. Her birds appear in related Welsh literature, with song affecting living and dead, but do not accompany every episode of her story.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Rhiannon belongs to Welsh language literature, not an Irish divine family. Proposed connections with Gaulish Epona or ancient horse cults remain comparative interpretations. Her decisions about marriage, wrongful accusation, endurance, and restored dignity also deserve attention on their own narrative terms.

figures.name: 拉
figures.title: 太阳航行与宇宙更新的创造神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 拉是古埃及重要太阳神，在赫利奥波利斯创造传统中具有核心地位，并与阿图姆、凯普利等太阳形态相连。他可以体现白昼运行的太阳，也与王权及宇宙秩序相联系；不同时代和城市存在多种融合名称。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 拉乘太阳船穿越白昼天空，夜间进入地下世界，与危及秩序的巨蛇阿波菲斯对抗，翌晨重新升起。《天牛之书》又叙述人类反叛后，拉派出自己的眼惩罚他们；杀戮几乎失控，他以染红的啤酒让女神醉倒，终于停止对人类的毁灭。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 隼首人身、头顶日轮及环绕日轮的圣蛇是常见形象，太阳船显示周期航行。与凯普利融合时可出现圣甲虫，与阿图姆或其他神结合时形象又有所变化。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 金字塔铭文、棺椁铭文和王陵地下世界图像不断发展太阳更新观念。阿蒙拉等复合神名并不意味着旧神被简单取代，而是埃及神学将不同神力组织在一起的方式。

en.name: Ra
en.title: Solar creator and voyager of cosmic renewal

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Ra is a major Egyptian solar god, central to creation traditions at Heliopolis and closely associated with Atum and Khepri. He embodies the sun’s movement, kingship, and cosmic order. Different periods and religious centres combined his identity with other gods in several complementary forms.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Ra travels across the daylight sky in a solar boat, then passes through the underworld at night, resisting the serpent Apophis before rising again. In the Book of the Heavenly Cow, rebellious humans provoke his destructive Eye. When punishment threatens extermination, red coloured beer intoxicates the goddess and brings the slaughter to an end.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A falcon headed man wearing a sun disk and protective cobra commonly represents Ra. The solar boat emphasises cyclical travel. Scarab imagery evokes Khepri, while composite identities can introduce further shapes and divine attributes.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Pyramid Texts, Coffin Texts, and royal tomb compositions elaborate solar renewal across centuries. Composite names such as Amun Ra do not simply record one god replacing another; they express Egyptian theological strategies for joining divine powers while preserving multiple local traditions.

figures.name: 奥西里斯
figures.title: 亡者王权、复生与丰饶之神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 奥西里斯通常是盖布与努特之子，伊西斯的兄弟及丈夫、荷鲁斯的父亲，在亡者领域拥有王者地位。他与土地丰饶、合法继承及死后更新相关；故事散见不同年代文本，完整连贯版本多由较晚作者整理。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 塞特杀害奥西里斯，伊西斯寻找遗体，并与奈芙蒂斯及阿努比斯等帮助者完成哀悼与保存。某些版本还叙述尸体被分割、各部分重新聚合。伊西斯使丈夫恢复生殖能力并孕育荷鲁斯，但奥西里斯并未回到阳世为王，而是成为冥界的统治者。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 木乃伊式裹身、阿泰夫冠、牧杖与连枷是主要标志，绿色或黑色皮肤关联再生和沃土。杰德柱常与他的稳定、脊柱及重建生命的观念相联系。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 阿拜多斯的节庆与朝拜使亡者同奥西里斯的关系格外重要，陪葬文本也常称死者为某某奥西里斯。这是仪式性的身份结合，不意味着所有埃及人拥有完全一致的来世观。

en.name: Osiris
en.title: King of the dead and power of regeneration

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Osiris is usually the son of Geb and Nut, brother and husband of Isis, and father of Horus. His authority encompasses the dead, fertility, legitimate succession, and renewal. Accounts survive across many periods; later authors organise scattered traditions into more continuous narrative biographies.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Seth murders Osiris, and Isis searches for his body. With Nephthys, Anubis, and other helpers, she mourns and preserves him. Some versions describe dismemberment followed by reassembly. Isis restores his reproductive capacity and conceives Horus, but Osiris does not resume earthly government: he becomes ruler in the realm of the dead.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A wrapped body, atef crown, crook, and flail identify Osiris. Green or black skin suggests regeneration and fertile soil. The djed pillar connects with stability, his backbone, and the restoration of enduring life.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Festivals and pilgrimage at Abydos strengthened identification between deceased people and Osiris. Funerary texts often call an individual the Osiris followed by their name. This ritual assimilation should not be mistaken for evidence of one perfectly uniform Egyptian belief about death.

figures.name: 伊西斯
figures.title: 魔法、王权与母性保护的女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 伊西斯是盖布与努特之女，奥西里斯的姐妹及妻子、荷鲁斯的母亲。她以有效的魔法、忠诚的哀悼和保护继承者而著称，名字及早期冠饰与王座相连，显示母性和王权从一开始便密不可分。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 伊西斯寻找并守护被塞特杀害的丈夫，借助魔法孕育荷鲁斯，又在沼泽隐居抚养孩子，防范蛇蝎与仇敌。另一故事中，她以拉的唾液和泥土造出毒蛇，使太阳神中毒；她要求得知他的秘密真名才肯医治，从而取得更强的神圣知识。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 王座形冠饰最能提示早期伊西斯，后期常戴牛角夹日轮，容易与哈托尔混淆。展开双翼、哺乳荷鲁斯和手持生命符的形象，都表现她对生命与王位的保护。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 伊西斯崇拜在希腊罗马时代遍及地中海，菲莱神庙则长期维持埃及祭仪。跨文化传播带来新的仪式和诠释，不应把后期普世女神形象直接当作所有早期传统的原貌。

en.name: Isis
en.title: Goddess of magic, protective motherhood, and kingship

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Isis is the daughter of Geb and Nut, sister and wife of Osiris, and mother of Horus. Powerful magic, effective mourning, and protection of the royal heir define her roles. Her name and early throne shaped crown connect motherhood with legitimate authority from the outset.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Isis searches for her murdered husband and uses magic to conceive Horus, whom she raises secretly in marshes while protecting him from poison and enemies. Another narrative has her fashion a snake from Ra’s saliva and earth. After it poisons him, she demands his hidden name before providing the cure and gaining secret knowledge.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The throne shaped crown identifies early Isis. Later she often wears cow horns surrounding a solar disk, resembling Hathor. Outstretched wings, nursing Horus, and the ankh express protection of life, the deceased, and legitimate succession.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Isis worship spread widely across the Mediterranean under Greek and Roman rule, while Philae maintained Egyptian ritual traditions. Cross cultural expansion brought fresh interpretations and ceremonies; the later universal goddess should not be projected unchanged onto every earlier Egyptian religious setting.

figures.name: 荷鲁斯
figures.title: 天空、王位继承与王者保护之神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 荷鲁斯是埃及隼形神祇的重要名称，包含不同地方与神学形态，不能全部化约成单一人物。作为伊西斯与奥西里斯之子，他争取父亲王位；作为天空之神和王者标识，他又拥有更广泛且古老的政治意义。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《荷鲁斯与塞特的争讼》描写两神为王位展开漫长诉讼与较量，众神会议反复裁决，伊西斯也以计谋协助儿子。荷鲁斯在冲突中眼睛受伤，后获修复；最终他被确认为合法继承者，奥西里斯则在亡者领域保持权威，王权秩序由此重新确立。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 隼鸟、隼首人身和上下埃及双冠是主要标志，乌加特眼强调恢复与完整。幼年荷鲁斯常以手指近嘴的儿童形象出现，这在埃及图像中表示幼年而非命令噤声。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 法老使用荷鲁斯名表达王者身份，埃德富神庙则保存丰富的地方仪式传统。希腊罗马时代的哈耳波克拉底来自幼年形态，其后来的沉默寓意不宜倒推为原始埃及含义。

en.name: Horus
en.title: Falcon god of sky, succession, and royal protection

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Horus names several related Egyptian falcon deities and local theological forms rather than one entirely uniform personality. As the child of Isis and Osiris he claims his father’s throne. As a sky god and royal emblem, he also carries older and broader political meanings.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: The Contendings of Horus and Seth describes prolonged litigation, contests, and repeated deliberations over legitimate succession, with Isis assisting her son through strategy. Horus suffers injury to his eye, which is restored. His eventual recognition as heir renews earthly kingship, while Osiris retains authority among the dead in a complementary arrangement.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A falcon, falcon headed man, and double crown identify royal Horus. The wedjat eye signifies restoration and wholeness. Child Horus often holds a finger near his mouth, an Egyptian indication of childhood rather than enforced silence.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Pharaohs used a Horus name to express royal identity, while Edfu preserved elaborate local ceremonies. The Greek and Roman Harpocrates derives from child Horus; later interpretations linking him with silence should not be projected back as the original Egyptian meaning.

figures.name: 塞特
figures.title: 风暴、边疆与危险力量之神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 塞特是盖布与努特之子，奥西里斯、伊西斯和奈芙蒂斯的兄弟，关联沙漠、风暴、外国地域与难以控制的力量。他在不同年代既可受王室尊奉，也可遭到贬抑，并不是自始至终都等同绝对邪恶的单一魔神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 塞特杀死奥西里斯并与荷鲁斯争夺王位，是王权叙事中的破坏者；他在审判、变形比赛和暴力冲突中反复挑战继承秩序。然而太阳船传统也让他站在拉身旁，凭强力刺击阿波菲斯，抵御足以吞没太阳的混沌之蛇，显示危险力量能够转为守护。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 长而弯曲的口鼻、竖起且顶部方截的耳朵和分叉尾巴组成所谓塞特兽，其具体动物原型仍有争议。长矛及太阳船上的战斗场景，可突出他作为护卫的一面。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 拉美西斯时代王名塞提表明塞特曾享有王室敬意，较晚时期又出现系统性排斥。把他简单对应撒旦，会遮蔽埃及人对于力量、边疆与秩序相互依赖的复杂理解。

en.name: Seth
en.title: God of storms, frontiers, and dangerous power

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Seth is the son of Geb and Nut and brother of Osiris, Isis, and Nephthys. Associated with desert, storms, foreign regions, and disruptive strength, he received royal honour in some periods and condemnation in others. He was not consistently an embodiment of absolute evil.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Seth murders Osiris and contests Horus’s inheritance through trials, transformations, and violent encounters. Yet solar traditions also place him beside Ra, wielding a spear against Apophis, the serpent threatening the sun’s passage. The same dangerous strength that disrupts succession can therefore defend the cosmos against a still more fundamental destructive force.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The Seth animal has an elongated curved snout, tall squared ears, and a forked tail; its zoological identity remains debated. A spear and combat aboard the solar boat can emphasise his protective rather than murderous role.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Royal names such as Seti show Seth’s prestige during the Ramesside period, whereas later evidence includes systematic rejection. Equating him with Satan obscures changing historical attitudes and Egyptian ideas about the uneasy dependence of ordered life on dangerous, boundary crossing powers.

figures.name: 阿努比斯
figures.title: 遗体保存、墓地与审判的守护者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 阿努比斯是埃及犬科形象的丧葬神，守护遗体处理、墓地和通往亡者世界的过程。他的父母谱系因时代而异，较晚故事常说他是奈芙蒂斯与奥西里斯之子；早期宗教地位则不能完全从这一家族故事解释。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 在奥西里斯传统中，阿努比斯帮助保存和包裹死去神王的遗体，成为理想防腐程序的神圣典范。《亡灵书》的审判图像中，他引领死者来到天平，并检查称量是否正确：心脏与玛阿特之羽相衡，托特记录结果，奥西里斯主持最终的接纳。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 黑色犬科头、人身与墓上俯卧的犬是主要形态，黑色关联沃土和再生而非自然毛色。防腐器具、木乃伊台与天平，也帮助区分他与其他犬科形象的神祇。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 祭司在丧葬仪式中可扮演阿努比斯角色，开口仪式则帮助死者恢复感官功能。他不是把人判入现代意义地狱的恶魔，图像重点在保存、引导和审判程序的可靠执行。

en.name: Anubis
en.title: Guardian of embalming, cemeteries, and judgement

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Anubis is an Egyptian canine funerary god who protects bodily preservation, cemeteries, and passage into the world of the dead. His parentage varies; later accounts often name Nephthys and Osiris. His early religious importance cannot be explained solely through that later family narrative.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In Osirian traditions, Anubis helps preserve and wrap the murdered king, establishing a divine model for embalming. Judgement scenes in the Book of the Dead show him leading the deceased and attending the scales. The heart balances against Maat’s feather, Thoth records the outcome, and Osiris presides over admission among the justified.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A black canine head on a human body, or a recumbent canine above a shrine, identifies Anubis. Black evokes fertile soil and regeneration. Embalming equipment, a mummy couch, and scales further clarify his funerary functions.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Funerary priests could enact Anubis’s role, while the Opening of the Mouth restored capacities needed after death. He is not a demon assigning people to a modern hell: preservation, guidance, and correct judicial procedure are central to his religious character.

figures.name: 安努
figures.title: 天空权威与神圣等级的源头

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 安努是阿卡德语传统的天空神，对应苏美尔语的安，处于两河诸神等级的重要高位。他与乌鲁克及埃安纳圣域关系密切，常被尊为诸神之父；不同城市的神谱和创世解释并不完全一致，配偶与子女也随文献而变。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《吉尔伽美什史诗》中，伊什塔尔求爱被拒后，向安努索取天牛报复乌鲁克；他起初担忧饥荒，最终仍让天牛降临。在《阿达帕》故事中，他召见凡人智者，并提供生命之食与水，但阿达帕听从埃亚的警告而拒绝，从此错失超越凡人命运的机会。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 角冠是神性权威的常见标志，安努也可由置于神座的冠饰象征，未必出现完整人形。天空意象与高位神座固然有关，但单凭星形符号不能可靠识别其专属身份。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 苏美尔、阿卡德及后期巴比伦材料呈现不同面貌，晚期乌鲁克尤其发展安努崇拜。神谱中的最高地位并不自动代表每座城市或每个时代都以他为最主要的日常祭祀对象。

en.name: Anu
en.title: Source of heavenly authority and divine rank

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Anu is the Akkadian sky god corresponding to Sumerian An, occupying a high position in Mesopotamian divine hierarchies. Closely associated with Uruk and its Eanna sanctuary, he is often called father of the gods. Genealogies, partners, and creation schemes nevertheless differ across cities and texts.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In the Epic of Gilgamesh, Ishtar demands the Bull of Heaven after the hero rejects her. Anu initially raises concerns about famine but eventually releases it against Uruk. In Adapa’s story, he offers the summoned sage life giving food and water; following Ea’s warning, Adapa refuses and loses a chance to escape mortality.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A horned crown expresses divine authority, and Anu can be represented by a crown placed upon a throne rather than a complete human figure. Neither generic stars nor elevated seating alone securely establish his exclusive identity.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Sumerian, Akkadian, and later Babylonian sources reveal changing emphases, with an especially developed Anu cult in late Uruk. Supreme genealogical rank does not automatically mean that every Mesopotamian city or period treated him as its principal recipient of everyday worship.

figures.name: 恩利尔
figures.title: 神圣命令、王权与天地秩序之主

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 恩利尔是苏美尔传统中的核心大神，圣城为尼普尔，主要神庙称埃库尔，配偶为宁利尔。他关联神圣命令、命运裁定及王权的合法性，名字虽常被释为风之主，其宗教职能却远不止自然风暴这一层面。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《安祖》故事中，怪鸟夺走恩利尔掌握的命运之版，使神界权威陷入危机，最终由战神宁努尔塔击败盗贼、恢复秩序。《阿特拉哈西斯》则写人类喧扰令恩利尔不堪忍受，他接连降灾并决定洪水灭世，埃亚却帮助智者造船，使生命得以延续。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 角冠、庄严神座以及埃库尔神庙的山岳意象可提示恩利尔的权威，命运之版强调号令的效力。两河图像常共享神性标记，缺乏题铭时不宜把任何持杖大神都认作他。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 尼普尔长期具有跨城邦宗教威望，君王通过修庙和奉献争取恩利尔认可。巴比伦崛起后，部分主权观念转移到马尔杜克，并不意味着早期恩利尔传统立即消失或全然相同。

en.name: Enlil
en.title: Lord of divine decree, kingship, and ordered authority

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Enlil is a central Sumerian god whose chief sanctuary, Ekur, stood at Nippur. His spouse is Ninlil. He governs binding divine commands, decisions about destiny, and legitimate kingship. Although his name is often rendered Lord Wind, his religious importance extends well beyond a meteorological function.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In the Anzu narrative, a monstrous bird steals the Tablet of Destinies associated with Enlil’s authority, threatening divine government until Ninurta defeats it and restores order. In Atrahasis, human noise provokes Enlil to send successive disasters and finally a flood. Ea’s intervention enables a wise human to build a boat and preserve life.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Horned crowns, an imposing throne, and Ekur’s mountain imagery express Enlil’s authority. The Tablet of Destinies embodies effective command. Since Mesopotamian gods share many visual markers, an unnamed enthroned figure cannot automatically be identified as Enlil.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Nippur retained religious prestige across competing political centres, and rulers sought Enlil’s approval through temple patronage. Babylon’s rise transferred some sovereign language to Marduk, but this development did not instantly erase Enlil’s cult or make the two gods historically interchangeable.

figures.name: 恩基
figures.title: 地下淡水、智慧与文明技艺之主

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 恩基是苏美尔神祇，阿卡德语传统称埃亚，圣城为埃里都，主要神庙与地下淡水阿勃祖相连。他关联智慧、工艺、净化和生命创造，常凭机巧调解冲突；神谱中通常是安之子，但不同文本并无完全一致的家族安排。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《伊南娜与恩基》中，恩基宴饮时将文明的神圣权能赠给伊南娜，酒醒后派使者追索，却未能阻止她把这些力量运到乌鲁克。洪水传统中，埃亚绕开诸神保密誓言，对芦苇墙发出警告，让阿特拉哈西斯或乌特纳比什提姆得知灾难，并造船保存生命。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 肩头流出的水及水中游鱼是恩基埃亚图像的重要线索，角冠显示其神格。羊鱼混合动物和曲杖也与他有关，流动水源尤能表达地下淡水与生命供应的关系。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 埃里都传统使恩基与古老城市文明相连，咒语、医治和净化文献又强调埃亚的知识。他的帮助常以间接表达和权宜手段实现，不宜概括为始终反对诸神的现代人类主义者。

en.name: Enki
en.title: Lord of fresh water, wisdom, and civilisation’s skills

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Enki, called Ea in Akkadian tradition, is the god of Eridu and the subterranean freshwater Apsu. Associated with wisdom, craftsmanship, purification, and the making of life, he often resolves crises through ingenuity. He is commonly An’s son, although divine family arrangements differ between texts.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In Inanna and Enki, the god gives away civilisation’s sacred powers during a drinking feast. After recovering his judgement, he attempts unsuccessfully to retrieve them from Inanna’s journey to Uruk. In flood traditions, Ea addresses a reed wall to evade divine secrecy, allowing Atrahasis or Utnapishtim to learn the warning and construct a survival vessel.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Streams flowing from his shoulders, often containing fish, are important visual clues, alongside the divine horned crown. The goat fish and curved staff also belong to his imagery, linking fresh water, skilled provision, and living abundance.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Eridu traditions associate Enki with ancient urban civilisation, while incantations and healing texts stress Ea’s expert knowledge. His aid often relies on indirect speech and expedient compromise; he should not be simplified into a modern humanist consistently opposing every other god.

figures.name: 伊南娜
figures.title: 爱欲、战争与权力转换的女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 伊南娜是苏美尔的重要女神，与阿卡德伊什塔尔逐渐认同，关联爱欲、战争、王权与金星，乌鲁克埃安纳是其重要圣域。她常被说成月神南纳之女，但另有安之女等谱系，不能强行统一不同城市的神学传统。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 伊南娜进入姐姐埃列什基伽勒统治的冥界，经过七道门时逐一除去衣饰与权能，最终被杀并悬挂。恩基派出的使者使她复生，但离开必须提供替身；她选中未为自己哀悼的杜穆兹，随后又与其姐妹格什提南娜分担冥界停留，形成复杂的替代安排。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 八芒星、狮子和武器是常见标志，某些图像以肩部伸出的兵器强调战争力量。金星晨昏可见的变化支持其多面性，但著名裸身浮雕的具体身份仍须谨慎判断。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 苏美尔赞歌、阿卡德史诗与各地祭仪保留不同面貌，诗人恩赫杜安娜作品传统尤其重要。现代常以性或赋权概括她，却不应忽视其暴烈权威、政治关系和地方宗教差异。

en.name: Inanna
en.title: Goddess of desire, warfare, and changing power

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Inanna is a major Sumerian goddess increasingly identified with Akkadian Ishtar, associated with desire, warfare, kingship, and Venus. Uruk’s Eanna was an important sanctuary. Often called daughter of the moon god Nanna, she has other genealogies, reflecting different local theological traditions rather than one fixed biography.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Descending into her sister Ereshkigal’s underworld, Inanna passes seven gates and loses her clothing and powers before being killed and hung up. Enki sends helpers who restore her, but departure requires a substitute. She selects Dumuzi, who has not mourned her; an arrangement later divides underworld residence between him and his sister Geshtinanna.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The eight pointed star, lions, and weapons commonly identify her. Arms emerging from the shoulders emphasise martial force. Venus’s changing visibility supports multiple associations, but famous nude reliefs should not all be assigned to her without qualification.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Sumerian hymns, Akkadian narratives, and local rituals preserve different aspects, with the literary tradition associated with Enheduanna especially significant. Modern emphases on sexuality or empowerment should not obscure political patronage, violent authority, and substantial variation across her long religious history.

figures.name: 马尔杜克
figures.title: 巴比伦城神与宇宙王权的承担者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 马尔杜克是巴比伦的城神，通常称埃亚与达姆金娜之子，主要神庙为埃萨吉拉，配偶为萨尔帕尼图。他的地位随巴比伦政治影响上升，逐渐取得众神领袖称号；这种历史发展不应被理解成两河宗教从来只有一个最高神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《埃努玛埃利什》中，马尔杜克答应对抗提亚马特，条件是诸神授予最高权威。他用网与狂风制敌，再以箭射穿其身体，将遗体分为天地，并安排星辰历法。随后人类由金古之血被创造，以承担劳役；诸神则建造巴比伦，确认新王的地位。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 锹形器具、穆什胡舒龙及王者姿态是主要线索，龙具有混合动物的角、鳞与爪。并非所有持弓战龙图像都能无争议认作马尔杜克，出土地点与题铭仍很关键。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 巴比伦新年阿基图节与王权更新相连，创世史诗在部分节庆程序中诵读。诗篇赞颂宇宙秩序也服务城市威望，应与苏美尔较早传统和亚述改写版本分别看待。

en.name: Marduk
en.title: Patron of Babylon and bearer of cosmic kingship

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Marduk is Babylon’s patron god, usually son of Ea and Damkina, with Sarpanitum as his consort and Esagila as his chief temple. His supremacy developed alongside Babylon’s political influence. This historical ascent should not imply that Mesopotamian religion always recognised one unchanging supreme deity.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In Enuma Elish, Marduk agrees to confront Tiamat if the gods grant him supreme authority. Using a net, winds, and an arrow, he defeats her and divides her body into cosmic regions, arranging stars and calendars. Humanity is fashioned from Kingu’s blood to perform labour, while the gods establish Babylon and acclaim their ruler.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The spade shaped implement, the hybrid mushhushshu dragon, and royal bearing help identify Marduk. The dragon combines horns, scales, and claws. Not every archer confronting a monster can securely be named Marduk without supporting inscriptions or context.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Babylon’s Akitu New Year festival renewed kingship, and the creation epic was recited within some festival procedures. Its cosmic vision also promoted civic prestige. Earlier Sumerian traditions and Assyrian adaptations require separate consideration rather than being treated as identical versions.

figures.name: 吉尔伽美什
figures.title: 乌鲁克英雄王与死亡的追问者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 吉尔伽美什是乌鲁克的传奇君王，苏美尔王表及史诗传统均提到他，母亲为女神宁孙。标准巴比伦史诗称他三分之二为神、三分之一为人；早期统治者可能有历史基础，但不能将整部史诗当作其真实传记。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 吉尔伽美什与恩奇都由对手成为挚友，共赴雪松林杀死洪巴巴，又击败天牛。恩奇都死亡使他恐惧自身命运，于是远行寻访洪水幸存者乌特纳比什提姆。他未能通过不眠考验，取得的返老还童植物又被蛇偷走，最终回到乌鲁克，面对城墙与凡人有限的一生。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 乌鲁克城墙、雪松、狮子、旅途衣装和失去的生命植物可提示其故事。美索不达米亚常见的裸身卷发英雄并不都能确定是他，古代图像题名不足时应保留疑问。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 苏美尔独立故事、古巴比伦片段和标准巴比伦版本逐步形成复杂传统，泥版抄写跨越多个世纪。史诗的核心并非获得永生的成功，而是友谊、哀悼与对死亡界限的认识。

en.name: Gilgamesh
en.title: Hero king of Uruk and seeker of mortality’s meaning

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Gilgamesh is the legendary king of Uruk, appearing in the Sumerian King List and several narrative traditions. His mother is the goddess Ninsun, and the standard epic calls him two thirds divine. A possible historical ruler does not make the surviving poem a factual personal biography.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Gilgamesh and Enkidu become companions, kill Humbaba in the Cedar Forest, and defeat the Bull of Heaven. Enkidu’s death drives the king to seek the flood survivor Utnapishtim. He fails a test of wakefulness, then loses a rejuvenating plant to a snake. Returning to Uruk, he confronts the city’s walls and the limits of mortal achievement.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Uruk’s walls, cedar trees, lions, travelling clothes, and the lost plant evoke his journey. Mesopotamian images of a naked curly haired hero cannot all securely be identified as Gilgamesh when inscriptions or narrative context are missing.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Independent Sumerian tales, Old Babylonian fragments, and the Standard Babylonian epic form a layered tradition transmitted over centuries. The poem does not celebrate successful immortality; it investigates companionship, bereavement, human accomplishment, and the difficult recognition that every human life ends.

figures.name: 阿胡拉·马兹达
figures.title: 祆教活态信仰中的智慧之主

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 阿胡拉马兹达意为智慧之主，是祆教信仰的核心，关联创造、真理与善的秩序阿沙。《伽萨》、较晚《阿维斯塔》及中古波斯文献的神学表述并非完全一致；祆教至今仍有信众，不能仅当作已经消失的神话体系。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 在琐罗亚斯德相关传统中，阿胡拉马兹达向先知启示善思、善言与善行的重要性，要求人对真理和谎言作出选择。中古波斯《本达希申》又叙述他以奥尔马兹德之名安排有限的宇宙时间，面对恶灵入侵，最终通过世界更新克服死亡与污染。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 火与光可象征洁净和真理，但祆教徒并非将普通火焰当作造物主。阿契美尼德翼盘人物是否直接代表阿胡拉马兹达仍有学术争论，不应把所有翼盘都作确定神像。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 伊朗与印度帕西社群持续保存祈祷、祭仪和节庆，彼此传统也有差异。介绍此神应区分古代王室铭文、经典神学及当代实践，并尊重信徒对宗教名称和神圣形象的使用。

en.name: Ahura Mazda
en.title: Wise Lord at the heart of living Zoroastrian faith

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Ahura Mazda means Wise Lord and stands at the centre of Zoroastrian faith, associated with creation, truth, and asha, righteous order. The Gathas, later Avestan texts, and Middle Persian works articulate theology differently. Zoroastrianism remains a living religion, not merely an extinct collection of myths.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Traditions concerning Zarathustra present Ahura Mazda as revealing the importance of good thoughts, words, and deeds and responsible choice between truth and deceit. The Middle Persian Bundahishn describes Ohrmazd arranging a limited cosmic span against the destructive spirit’s intrusion. Ultimately, renovation overcomes death and pollution, fulfilling creation’s intended good condition rather than abandoning the material world.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Fire and light express purity and truth, but worshippers do not simply identify ordinary flames with the creator. Scholars debate whether Achaemenid winged figures directly portray Ahura Mazda; every winged disk should not be labelled his image.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Iranian and Indian Parsi communities maintain prayers, rituals, and festivals with internal diversity. Ancient royal inscriptions, scriptural theology, and contemporary practice require distinction. Religious names, sacred images, and believers’ own understandings should be treated with care and respect.

figures.name: 安格拉·曼纽
figures.title: 祆教传统中毁灭与谎言的恶灵

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 安格拉曼纽意为敌对或毁灭的灵，中古波斯语常称阿赫里曼，在祆教传统中关联谎言、污染和破坏。早期经典与后期宇宙论对其地位的说明存在差异，不能一概说成与阿胡拉马兹达永远势均力敌的第二位神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《维迪夫达特》以善地及恶性反制的结构描述破坏力量，对创造带来寒冷、疾病等灾害。中古波斯宇宙论又叙述恶灵侵入受造世界，使死亡和污染进入生命，但它的行动受有限时间约束，最终在世界更新时失效，受造物得以脱离混杂的状态。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 黑暗、腐败和有害生物属于相关的象征语言，而非一套统一的恶灵肖像。近代带角、蝠翼的魔王造型多受其他文化影响，不能作为阿维斯塔时代的可靠识别标记。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 祆教内部对恶的本体地位与早期经文的解释并不单一，古典外部记述也常带偏见。应将宗教伦理、仪式洁净和后期神学区分，避免把活态信仰简化为崇拜善恶两神。

en.name: Angra Mainyu
en.title: Destructive spirit of deceit and corruption

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Angra Mainyu means Hostile or Destructive Spirit, later called Ahriman in Middle Persian. Associated with deceit, pollution, and damage, this figure receives differing explanations in early scripture and later cosmology. It is misleading to describe him universally as an eternally equal second god beside Ahura Mazda.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: The Vendidad describes good lands followed by destructive countermeasures, including cold and disease. Middle Persian cosmology recounts the spirit’s invasion of creation, introducing mortality and corruption into a previously good world.
