Yet its activity is confined within a limited cosmic history; final renovation defeats destructive influence and releases creation from its present mixed condition.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Darkness, decay, and harmful creatures belong to associated symbolic language, not a standardised portrait. Horns and bat wings in modern demon imagery often derive from other traditions and are not secure attributes from the Avestan period.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Zoroastrian interpretations of evil’s status and early scriptural passages are not uniform, while outside ancient descriptions can be prejudiced. Ethical choice, ritual purity, and later theological systems need distinction. Living Zoroastrianism should not be reduced to worship of two opposed gods.

figures.name: 密特拉
figures.title: 祆教契约、守望与公正的神圣存在

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 密特拉是伊朗宗教中与契约、承诺和守望相关的神圣存在，在祆教中属于值得敬奉的亚扎塔，而非与阿胡拉马兹达相争的造物主。他的名字与古印度密多罗同源，光明关联也不能直接等于单一太阳神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《密特拉颂》描写他拥有千耳万眼，驾车巡察广阔土地，识破背约者，不因对方属于本国或敌国便宽容欺骗。他在日出之前照察山岭，保护守信者及其牲畜与家园；后期祆教传统又让他与斯劳沙、拉什努共同参与灵魂的审判过程。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 广阔视野、战车、武器和光明属于经文中的主要意象，表现对誓言的警戒。罗马密特拉斯屠牛图不能直接当作伊朗密特拉的标准图像，二者之间的历史关系仍需区分。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 密赫尔甘节保留了与密赫尔相关的纪念传统，祆教祈祷也持续提及他。罗马军队及城镇流行的密特拉斯秘仪另有考古与制度背景，不能将两套宗教实践完全合并。

en.name: Mithra
en.title: Zoroastrian guardian of covenants and vigilant justice

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Mithra is an Iranian sacred being associated with covenants, commitments, and watchfulness. In Zoroastrianism he is a yazata, worthy of reverence, not a competing creator. His name is cognate with Vedic Mitra, while his luminous associations do not make him simply identical with the sun.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: The Mihr Yasht describes Mithra with a thousand ears and ten thousand eyes, surveying broad lands from his chariot and exposing broken agreements. Neither national loyalty nor hostility excuses deceit. He watches mountains before sunrise and protects faithful households and cattle. Later traditions associate him with Sraosha and Rashnu in the judgement of souls.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Wide vision, a chariot, weapons, and brightness express his scriptural vigilance over commitments. The Roman bull slaying scene should not automatically serve as Iranian Mithra’s standard image, since the relationship between these traditions requires historical differentiation.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The Mehrgan festival preserves traditions connected with Mihr, and Zoroastrian prayers continue to honour him. Roman Mithraic mysteries had distinct archaeological settings and institutional practices. Shared names and possible contacts do not justify treating Iranian worship and Roman initiation as one identical religion.

figures.name: 阿娜希塔
figures.title: 祆教纯净水源与生命丰饶的守护者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 阿娜希塔常指阿尔德维苏拉阿娜希塔，名号包含强健与无染的意义，是祆教传统中与广大水域、生命繁衍和净化相联的亚扎塔。其经典形象、王室崇奉与地方女神传统相互交织，不能简单等同某位希腊女神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《阿邦颂》将她描写为从高处奔流、滋养大地的神圣水源，同时以华美而强健的女子形象出现。英雄和君王向她献祭，请求胜利、权力或生育，她接受正当祈愿而拒绝某些破坏者。她的马车由四匹马牵引，分别关联风、雨、云和雨夹雪。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 奔流的河水、华服、冠饰和四马战车来自经典描述，表达净化与生命供给。萨珊浮雕中女性授环者的身份仍需具体判断，不能把所有持水器女性都确定为阿娜希塔。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 阿契美尼德王室铭文及后期传统显示对她的敬奉，伊朗水源祭仪至今具有宗教意义。所谓阿娜希塔神庙的建筑认定有时存在争议，应区分古代奉献证据与现代遗址命名。

en.name: Anahita
en.title: Guardian of pure waters and life sustaining abundance

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Anahita commonly denotes Aredvi Sura Anahita, whose titles convey might and freedom from defilement. A Zoroastrian yazata of abundant waters, fertility, and purification, she combines scriptural imagery with royal patronage and local traditions. She should not simply be identified with a single Greek goddess.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: The Aban Yasht depicts her as a mighty sacred watercourse nourishing the earth and as a richly dressed, powerful woman. Heroes and rulers offer sacrifices seeking victory, authority, or offspring. She grants suitable petitions and rejects some destructive claimants. Her chariot is drawn by four horses associated with wind, rain, cloud, and sleet.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Flowing water, elaborate clothing, a crown, and the four horse chariot derive from scriptural descriptions. Female figures offering royal rings in Sasanian reliefs require contextual identification; not every woman holding a vessel can securely be called Anahita.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Achaemenid inscriptions and later sources attest her reverence, while water related observances retain importance in living Iranian religion. Identifying particular ruins as her temples can be disputed. Ancient dedicatory evidence should therefore be distinguished from modern archaeological labels and popular site names.

figures.name: 贾姆希德
figures.title: 伊朗史诗中黄金时代与失去荣光的君王

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 贾姆希德是伊朗传说中的早期君王，在《列王纪》中属于皮什达德王朝，其名字与《阿维斯塔》的伊玛相关。两者跨越不同语言与时代，既有连续性也有改写；他不是祆教造物主，也不能把史诗经历等同经典教义。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《列王纪》写贾姆希德发展手工业、社会分工与航行，开创繁荣，并在新年受到欢庆。但他后来把成就归于自身，失去神圣荣光，最终遭扎哈克推翻并杀害。《维迪夫达特》的伊玛则奉命建造围护空间，保存人、动物与植物，以躲过毁灭性的严冬。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 王座、王冠、诺鲁孜庆典与神圣荣光可提示其君王形象，保存生命的围护空间属于伊玛传统。传说中洞察世界的宝杯与他相关，但具体归属随波斯文学发展而变化。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 菲尔多西的波斯语《列王纪》在伊斯兰时代重述古代伊朗王统，不能直接当作祆教礼仪手册。诺鲁孜今天跨越宗教与国界流传，贾姆希德只是其多层文化记忆的一部分。

en.name: Jamshid
en.title: Epic king of a golden age and lost royal glory

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Jamshid is an early Iranian legendary king placed within the Pishdadian dynasty in the Shahnameh. His name connects with Avestan Yima, but continuity crosses major linguistic and historical changes. He is not a Zoroastrian creator, and his epic biography should not be treated as identical with scriptural teaching.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: The Shahnameh credits Jamshid with crafts, social organisation, navigation, and flourishing prosperity celebrated at the new year. Pride leads him to claim excessive personal credit, lose royal glory, and fall to Zahhak. In the Vendidad, Yima instead receives instructions to build an enclosure preserving selected humans, animals, and plants against a devastating winter.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Throne, crown, Nowruz celebration, and royal glory evoke Jamshid’s kingship. The life preserving enclosure belongs specifically to Yima’s scriptural story. A world revealing cup also becomes associated with him, though its ownership shifts within Persian literary traditions.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Ferdowsi’s Persian Shahnameh retells ancient Iranian kingship within an Islamic era literary setting; it is not a Zoroastrian ritual handbook. Nowruz now crosses religious and national boundaries, and Jamshid forms only one layer within its rich and changing cultural memory.

figures.name: 鲁斯塔姆
figures.title: 《列王纪》中锡斯坦的悲剧英雄

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 鲁斯塔姆是波斯史诗《列王纪》的核心英雄，出自锡斯坦，父亲为扎尔，母亲为鲁达贝。神鸟西摩格曾指导他的艰难出生；他长年保护伊朗王国，却不是祆教中接受礼仪敬奉的亚扎塔，英雄身份与宗教神格应当区分。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 鲁斯塔姆骑名马拉赫什完成七项艰险任务，击败白魔，拯救凯卡乌斯。最著名的悲剧中，他与未曾相认的儿子苏赫拉布交战，致命一击之后才凭信物发现真相。他后来又被迫与伊斯凡迪亚尔决斗，最终自己遭沙加德设计的陷坑伏杀，临死仍射杀仇人。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 名马拉赫什、虎皮衣、重型武器与强壮武士形象最易辨识鲁斯塔姆，儿子的臂环或信物则指向认亲悲剧。波斯细密画常以鲜明服饰和反复出现的坐骑维持其身份连续。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 菲尔多西整理了长期流传的伊朗英雄材料，鲁斯塔姆又在说书、戏剧和细密画中持续重生。他的故事讨论忠诚、王权压力与亲属伤害，不宜归类为所有伊朗人共同实践的宗教教义。

en.name: Rostam
en.title: Tragic champion of Sistan in the Shahnameh

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Rostam is the Shahnameh’s great champion from Sistan, son of Zal and Rudabeh. The supernatural bird Simurgh assists his difficult birth through instructions given to Zal. A defender of Iran’s kings, he is an epic hero, not a Zoroastrian yazata receiving the same category of ritual reverence.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: With his horse Rakhsh, Rostam survives seven ordeals, defeats the White Div, and rescues Kay Kavus. His greatest tragedy comes when he mortally wounds his unrecognised son Sohrab and identifies him only through a token. He later fights Esfandiyar under political pressure, then dies in Shaghad’s concealed pit, killing the betrayer before his own death.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Rakhsh, tiger skin clothing, heavy weapons, and formidable physical strength identify Rostam. A token or armband signals the recognition of Sohrab. Persian miniature painters maintain his identity through distinctive costume and the recurrent appearance of his horse.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Ferdowsi shaped older Iranian heroic materials, while storytelling, theatre, and miniature painting continue to renew Rostam’s career. His narratives explore loyalty, royal coercion, and harm within families. They should not be classified as doctrines religiously practised by all Iranian people.

figures.name: 得墨忒耳
figures.title: 谷物与农耕女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 得墨忒耳是克洛诺斯与瑞亚之女，宙斯的姐妹，也是珀耳塞福涅的母亲。她主管谷物生长和人类农耕，并与土地丰产、婚姻秩序及厄琉息斯的祭仪传统密切相连。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《荷马颂歌·致得墨忒耳》记述哈得斯掳走珀耳塞福涅，母亲寻女并使谷物停长。在厄琉息斯，她化身老妇照料得摩丰，试图以火使他不死，却被其母打断。最终女儿每年三分之一时间留在地下，其余时间回归母亲。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 麦穗、火炬和丰收作物是她常见的辨识物：麦穗指向食粮，火炬呼应寻女。古代造像多呈庄严的成年女性，有时与女儿并列，而非仅以田园丰收为主题。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 厄琉息斯秘仪以她和女儿为核心，但具体仪式因守秘而难以复原。妇女参与的忒斯摩福里亚节也敬奉她；这些传统兼及农业、群体秩序及死后希望，不能简化为四季寓言。

en.name: Demeter
en.title: Goddess of Grain and Agriculture

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Demeter is a daughter of Cronus and Rhea, a sister of Zeus, and the mother of Persephone. Greek worship connected her with grain, cultivated land, and agricultural prosperity, while particular festivals also linked her authority to marriage and community order.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: In the Homeric Hymn to Demeter, she searches for Persephone after Hades abducts her and withholds the harvest. At Eleusis she attempts to immortalize Demophon through fire. The settlement gives Persephone one third of each year below and the remainder with her mother.

sections.title: Symbols and Identification
sections.text: Ears of grain and burning torches frequently identify Demeter in ancient art. Grain expresses her responsibility for food, while torches recall her search. She generally appears as a dignified adult woman, sometimes beside Persephone rather than in an isolated harvest scene.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: The Eleusinian Mysteries centered on Demeter and Persephone, but secrecy limits reconstruction of their ceremonies. The Thesmophoria also honored Demeter through gatherings of women. These cults addressed fertility, social continuity, and hopes concerning death, not simply a universal explanation of seasons.

figures.name: 赫尔墨斯
figures.title: 使者、旅途与边界之神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 赫尔墨斯是宙斯与迈亚之子，传说出生于阿卡迪亚的库勒涅山。他既是诸神使者，也护佑道路、交易和越界行动；其狡黠与口才使他同时关联盗窃、协商及机敏的发明。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《荷马颂歌·致赫尔墨斯》写他出生当天便以龟甲制琴，又盗走阿波罗的牛群，并设法隐匿踪迹。争端最终在宙斯面前解决，他以琴换得阿波罗的友谊。在《奥德赛》中，他送给奥德修斯抵御喀耳刻法术的神草。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 双蛇缠绕的使者杖、旅行帽和翼鞋是常见标识，但各时代形制不同。路旁赫尔墨斯柱则标记边界与通道；他的双蛇杖不应混同阿斯克勒庇俄斯的单蛇医杖。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 赫尔墨斯在史诗中跨越神界、人间与冥界，并引导亡魂。希腊化时期，他与埃及托特发生融合，形成赫尔墨斯·特里斯墨吉斯托斯传统；这属于后起会通，不是早期希腊神话的原貌。

en.name: Hermes
en.title: Messenger and God of Crossings

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Hermes is the son of Zeus and Maia, associated with Mount Cyllene in Arcadia. His responsibilities include divine messages, roads, exchange, and movement across boundaries. Intelligence and persuasive speech connect him with negotiation and invention as well as theft and deception.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: The Homeric Hymn to Hermes describes the newborn god making a lyre from a tortoise shell and stealing the cattle of Apollo. Their dispute ends in reconciliation and an exchange involving the lyre. In the Odyssey, Hermes supplies Odysseus with protective moly against Circe.

sections.title: Symbols and Identification
sections.text: His heraldic staff, traveling hat, and winged footwear provide familiar identifiers, although their forms vary across periods. Herm pillars marked routes and boundaries. The staff with two snakes should not be confused with the single serpent rod associated with the healing god Asclepius.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Epic presents Hermes moving between divine, human, and underworld settings, including service as a guide of souls. In Hellenistic Egypt he became associated with Thoth. The resulting Hermes Trismegistus tradition belongs to later religious and intellectual synthesis, not an unchanged early Greek identity.

figures.name: 赫尔
figures.title: 死者国度的统治者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 赫尔在斯诺里《散文埃达》中是洛基与女巨人安格尔博达之女，与芬里尔狼、世界蛇同胞。奥丁把她安置在尼福尔海姆，令其收容因疾病或衰老而死者；她并非所有亡者的唯一主宰。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 巴德尔死后，赫尔莫德骑马赴冥界请求放人。赫尔答应，若世间万物都为巴德尔哭泣，他便可归来。万物响应，唯有名叫索克的女巨人拒绝，于是巴德尔仍须留下。斯诺里称人们认为索克就是洛基所变，这一解释应归于该文本。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 斯诺里形容她身体一半青黑、一半呈肤色，神情阴沉；她的居所及器物多有饥饿、疾病之名。现代常见的半边骷髅形象是再创作，并非原文对骨骼的明确描写。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 古诺尔斯语中的赫尔也可指死者居处，须按上下文区分地点与人格化角色。现存系统叙述多经基督教时代作者保存，不能把她径直等同惩罚罪人的撒旦或基督教地狱。

en.name: Hel
en.title: Ruler of a Realm of the Dead

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: In the Prose Edda of Snorri Sturluson, Hel is the daughter of Loki and Angrboda, and sister of Fenrir and the world serpent. Odin assigns her a realm in Niflheim, receiving those who die from illness or age, rather than every deceased person.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: After Baldr dies, Hermod rides to her realm to request his release. Hel requires every being to weep for him. All comply except the giantess Thokk, so Baldr remains below. Snorri adds that people believed Thokk was Loki in disguise, an interpretation belonging to that account.

sections.title: Symbols and Identification
sections.text: Snorri describes Hel as half dark or blue black and half flesh colored, with a grim appearance. Her household carries names evoking hunger and sickness. Popular images giving her an exposed skeletal half are later visual interpretations, not an explicit anatomical description in his text.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: The Old Norse word hel can designate a dwelling of the dead as well as a personified ruler. Context determines the meaning. Surviving systematic accounts were recorded by Christian authors, but Hel should not simply be equated with Satan or a Christian place of punishment.

figures.name: 弗丽嘉
figures.title: 阿斯加德的王后与巴德尔之母

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 弗丽嘉是奥丁之妻、巴德尔之母，在埃达传统中居于女神的重要位置。她的居所名为芬萨利尔，常被解释为沼泽之厅。文本称她知晓命运而不轻易言说，但没有把她写成能够随意改写命运的全能者。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 在斯诺里的巴德尔故事中，弗丽嘉向万物取得不伤害儿子的誓言，却略过被认为过于幼小的槲寄生。洛基探得这一缺口，利用盲眼的霍德尔投出槲寄生，导致巴德尔死亡。母亲周密的保护未能解除预兆，成为故事的悲剧核心。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 弗丽嘉的辨识主要依靠王后身份、芬萨利尔及与巴德尔的亲属关系。后世艺术常加上纺锤、纺车或王冠，但不宜将这些道具都视为埃达中明确规定的固定属性。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 弗丽嘉与芙蕾雅在现存叙事中是不同角色，二者是否源自更早的共同形象仍有争论。英语星期五的名称关联她的日耳曼同源神名，不能仅据词源便抹平不同地区、时期的信仰差异。

en.name: Frigg
en.title: Queen of Asgard and Mother of Baldr

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Frigg is the wife of Odin and mother of Baldr, holding a prominent position among the goddesses of Eddic tradition. Her dwelling is Fensalir, often interpreted as marsh halls. Knowledge of fate is attributed to her, but not unlimited power to alter it.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: In the account by Snorri, Frigg obtains promises that things will not harm Baldr, overlooking mistletoe because it seems too young. Loki discovers the omission and helps the blind Hodr use mistletoe against him. Her extensive precautions therefore become the framework of a tragic failure.

sections.title: Symbols and Identification
sections.text: Her status as queen, the dwelling Fensalir, and her relationship to Baldr provide stronger textual identifiers than any single object. Later art often supplies a spindle, spinning wheel, or crown. These accessories should not all be treated as attributes explicitly prescribed by Eddic sources.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Frigg and Freyja are separate figures in surviving narratives, although scholars debate possible connections in their earlier development. The English weekday Friday derives from a related Germanic divine name. Such linguistic relationships do not erase differences between regional traditions or demonstrate identical medieval mythological roles.

figures.name: 萨图尔努斯
figures.title: 播种之神与黄金时代的旧王

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 萨图尔努斯是罗马古老神祇，传统上关联播种、农业与富足。他后来与希腊克洛诺斯相认同，因而承接被儿子取代的旧神王谱系；这些希腊化叙述不能直接当作早期意大利祭祀的完整起源。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 罗马文学记述他被朱庇特逐出天界后来到拉丁姆，受到雅努斯接纳，教当地人耕作并带来黄金时代。维吉尔《埃涅阿斯纪》让厄万德追述这位旧王治理的太平岁月；诗中的理想过去也用来反衬后来战争与财产争夺。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 镰刀或弯刃工具标示他的农业职能，也承接克洛诺斯的图像传统。神像有双足以羊毛束缚的记载，农神节期间解开；这些祭仪比现代星球图像更有古代依据。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 十二月的农神节以宴饮、赠礼及暂时放宽社会礼法著称，部分场合容许奴隶与主人角色倒置。罗马广场的萨图尔努斯神庙还曾保存国库，显示其崇拜并不限于乡村农业。

en.name: Saturn
en.title: God of Sowing and King of the Golden Age

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Saturn, or Saturnus, is an ancient Roman deity traditionally connected with sowing and agricultural abundance. His identification with the Greek Cronus supplied a genealogy involving an overthrown divine ruler. That literary assimilation should not be mistaken for a complete account of early Italian worship.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: Roman literature tells how Saturn reached Latium after Jupiter expelled him, received hospitality from Janus, and taught agriculture. In the Aeneid, Evander recalls the peaceful golden age under his rule. This idealized past also contrasts with subsequent warfare and the pursuit of private wealth.

sections.title: Symbols and Identification
sections.text: A sickle or curved agricultural blade identifies Saturn, while also reflecting imagery shared with Cronus. Ancient accounts describe the feet of his Roman statue bound with wool and released during Saturnalia. Such ritual details are more historically specific than modern associations with the planet.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Celebrated in December, Saturnalia involved feasting, gifts, and temporary relaxation of social conventions, with some contexts permitting reversals between masters and slaves. The Temple of Saturn in the Roman Forum also housed the public treasury, connecting his cult with civic institutions as well as agriculture.

figures.name: 伏尔甘
figures.title: 火焰与锻冶之神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 伏尔甘是罗马的火神，其意大利崇拜关注火焰的威力及失控危险。与希腊赫淮斯托斯相认同后，他更鲜明地成为神匠；文学中的家庭关系和锻造故事，不宜全部倒推为早期罗马信仰原有的内容。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《埃涅阿斯纪》中，维纳斯请求伏尔甘为埃涅阿斯制造武器，他召集独眼巨人在火山炉坊锻造盾甲，盾面展示罗马未来历史。奥维德则转述他用细密罗网捕住维纳斯与玛尔斯的偷情故事，改写自希腊神匠的叙事传统。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 锤、钳、铁砧和工匠帽常用于辨认伏尔甘，炉火表现其生产力量。火山锻坊属于文学和图像中的重要场景，但他在罗马祭祀中也关乎防止城市与储粮遭受火灾。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 八月二十三日的伏尔甘节位于炎热且火险较高的时节。古代作者记有向火中投献小鱼的仪式，并解释为替人命献祭；这是特定祭仪解释，不应泛化成所有火神崇拜的共同规则。

en.name: Vulcan
en.title: God of Fire and the Forge

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Vulcan, or Vulcanus, is the Roman god of fire, including its dangerous and destructive potential. Identification with the Greek Hephaestus emphasized his role as a divine craftsman. Literary family relationships and workshop adventures should not automatically be projected back into the earliest Italian cult.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: In the Aeneid, Venus persuades Vulcan to provide armor for Aeneas. He directs the Cyclopes at their volcanic forge, producing a shield that depicts future Roman history. Ovid also retells his trapping of Venus and Mars in a delicate net, adapting a Greek divine adultery narrative.

sections.title: Symbols and Identification
sections.text: Hammer, tongs, anvil, and a craftsman cap commonly identify Vulcan. Furnace imagery conveys the productive force of fire, while volcanic workshops belong prominently to literature and art. Roman worship also addressed the danger that uncontrolled flames posed to settlements and stored agricultural produce.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: The Volcanalia fell on August 23, during a hot season with considerable fire risk. Ancient writers describe offerings of small fish thrown into fire and interpret them as substitutes for human lives. That explanation concerns a particular practice, not a universal rule of fire worship.

figures.name: 马纳南
figures.title: 爱尔兰海上异界的主人

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 马纳南·麦克·李尔是爱尔兰叙事中的海上异界人物，名字表明他是李尔之子。他常与达努神族及跨海通向的彼界联系，也与马恩岛传统相连；不宜把这些材料合并成全体凯尔特人共有的统一神谱。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《布兰航海记》中，布兰见马纳南驾车越海，对方眼中的鲜花平原正是航海者眼中的海面。在科尔马克历险故事里，他以神奇银枝引王进入异界，又赠予能辨别真假的杯子；故事借款待与考验，揭示凡人判断所见世界的局限。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 海面上的车驾、隐蔽异界的迷雾及带金苹果的银枝，都可联系他的不同故事。它们不是一套固定制服：银枝尤其属于科尔马克叙事，辨识时应兼顾具体文本。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 有关马纳南的材料保存在中世纪爱尔兰手稿及更晚的民间传统中，版本间身份与道具会变化。马恩岛也有独立发展的地方传说；现代海神形象不能替代这些各有年代的文本。

en.name: Manannan mac Lir
en.title: Lord of the Irish Otherworld across the Sea

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Manannan mac Lir is a supernatural figure of Irish tradition whose patronymic identifies him as the son of Ler. Associated with the sea, the Tuatha De Danann, and otherworldly domains, he also appears in Manx tradition, without representing a uniform deity of every Celtic people.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: In the Voyage of Bran, Manannan travels by chariot over what Bran sees as the sea but he experiences as a flowering plain. In the adventures of Cormac, a magical silver branch leads toward his otherworldly hospitality, and a marvelous cup distinguishes falsehood from truth.

sections.title: Symbols and Identification
sections.text: His chariot crossing the sea, concealing mist, and the silver branch bearing golden apples connect with different narratives. They are not a standardized costume shared by every source. The branch is particularly relevant to the Cormac story, so identification should remain attentive to textual context.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Medieval Irish manuscripts and later folklore preserve differing accounts of Manannan, with changes in roles and magical possessions. The Isle of Man also developed local traditions about him. Modern presentations as a generic sea god should not replace the distinct histories of these sources.

figures.name: 博安
figures.title: 爱尔兰博因河的神话女性

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 博安是爱尔兰博因河的人格化女性，见于解释地名来历的中世纪诗文。不同叙述把她与奈赫坦、达格达及安格斯联系起来；她首先属于爱尔兰具体河流与地方谱系，而非泛凯尔特的抽象水元素女神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 一组《地名传说》叙述她走近奈赫坦的禁忌水井，并逆向绕井而行，井水骤然涌出追赶她，造成重创，最终形成通海的博因河。另一些故事写她与达格达生下安格斯，借延长一个白昼掩藏孕育过程；两类材料不必拼成唯一传记。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 博因河、水井、奔涌的水流及沿途地名，是辨认博安的可靠线索。她与诗歌、知识的联系应结合特定水井传统说明，不宜直接套用所有智慧之泉或鲑鱼的故事。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 《地名传说》把河道、死亡与地方记忆编织在一起，保存的并非可直接测绘的地理史。博因河谷的史前遗址早于现存手稿许多世纪，不能仅据后世故事认定其最初建造者信仰。

en.name: Boann
en.title: Mythic Woman of the River Boyne

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Boann personifies the River Boyne in Irish tradition and appears in medieval accounts explaining the origins of places. Narratives connect her with Nechtan, the Dagda, and Aengus. Her setting is a particular Irish landscape and genealogy, rather than an abstract water goddess shared everywhere.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: Accounts in the Dindshenchas describe Boann approaching the forbidden well of Nechtan and circling it against the customary direction. Water erupts, pursues and wounds her, forming the Boyne. Other narratives concern her union with the Dagda and the prolonged day concealing the conception and birth of Aengus.

sections.title: Symbols and Identification
sections.text: The Boyne, a well, rushing water, and named places along the river provide the clearest identifiers. Connections with poetic knowledge require attention to particular well traditions. They do not justify assigning every Irish story about a wisdom spring or a salmon directly to Boann.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: The Dindshenchas weaves landscape, death, and local memory into explanatory narratives rather than straightforward geographical history. Prehistoric monuments of the Boyne valley considerably predate surviving manuscripts. Later stories cannot, by themselves, establish the original religious beliefs or intentions of the people who built those monuments.

figures.name: 托特
figures.title: 书写、计量与月亮之神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 托特是埃及与书写、计算、智慧及月亮相关的神，重要崇拜中心为赫蒙城，即希腊人所称赫尔摩波利斯。他在神界担任记录者、调解者等职能，不同地方神学对其起源和创世作用有不同安排。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 在亡者审判图像中，托特记录称心的结果，而不是亲自吞食有罪者。较晚的普鲁塔克叙述他与月亮博戏，赢得光亮凑成五个额外日子，使努特得以在原有三百六十日之外生育；这一希腊语记载不能概括全部埃及创世传统。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 鹮首人身与狒狒是托特的主要形象，书写用具和月盘也能提示其身份。鹮喙的弧度可让人联想到月形，但具体图像仍须结合题铭，不能仅凭鸟头便确定为托特。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 托特深受书吏尊崇，既参与日常书写观念，也见于宗教和丧葬文本。希腊化及罗马时期，他与赫尔墨斯发生会通，成为赫尔墨斯主义的重要渊源，但两者并非从一开始就完全相同。

en.name: Thoth
en.title: God of Writing, Measurement, and the Moon

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Thoth is an Egyptian deity associated with writing, calculation, wisdom, and the moon. A major center of worship was Khmun, known to Greeks as Hermopolis. He serves as recorder and mediator among gods, while local theological traditions offer differing accounts of his origins and creative activity.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: In judgment scenes Thoth records the result of weighing the heart; he does not devour the condemned. A much later account by Plutarch describes him winning moonlight through gaming to create five additional days for Nut to give birth outside the original year of 360 days.

sections.title: Symbols and Identification
sections.text: An ibis headed human figure and a baboon are principal forms of Thoth. Writing equipment and lunar imagery can reinforce identification. The curved ibis bill may suggest the moon, but inscriptions and the surrounding scene remain important: a bird head alone does not establish his identity.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Scribes particularly honored Thoth, whose presence extends through practical ideas about writing, religious compositions, and funerary literature. In Hellenistic and Roman settings he was associated with Hermes, contributing to Hermetic traditions. This historical synthesis does not mean the two gods were originally identical.

figures.name: 哈托尔
figures.title: 天空、欢悦与护佑之女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 哈托尔是埃及重要女神，涉及天空、母性、爱情、音乐及死者护佑。她的名字常释为荷鲁斯之宫；不同地方传统让她成为荷鲁斯的母亲或配偶，不能把这些关系当作同一神谱中毫无变化的设定。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《天牛之书》讲述人类反叛年老的拉，拉遣自己的眼惩罚人类，哈托尔参与这一毁灭性行动。为止住杀戮，拉使大量啤酒染成血色，女神饮下后沉醉。相关传统把拉之眼的狂烈面貌也联系塞赫迈特，二者关系需按版本说明。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 母牛、牛耳及夹日盘的牛角是她常见标识，叉铃与梅纳特珠饰关联音乐祭仪。丹德拉的哈托尔柱头有牛耳；牛角日盘后来也用于伊西斯，不能据此独断身份。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 丹德拉是哈托尔的重要崇拜中心，其节庆与埃德富的荷鲁斯崇拜相联系。她也作为西方之女主人迎接亡者；这些丧葬角色与欢悦、舞乐并存，说明她并非只有爱情职能的单一女神。

en.name: Hathor
en.title: Goddess of Sky, Joy, and Protection

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Hathor is a major Egyptian goddess connected with the sky, maternity, love, music, and protection of the dead. Her name is commonly interpreted as House of Horus. Different local traditions make her his mother or consort, relationships that should not be flattened into one genealogy.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: The Book of the Heavenly Cow recounts human rebellion against the aging Ra and the dispatch of his Eye to punish humanity, involving Hathor. Ra halts slaughter with beer colored like blood, which intoxicates the goddess. Related traditions also connect the destructive Eye with Sekhmet.

sections.title: Symbols and Identification
sections.text: Cow form, bovine ears, and horns enclosing a solar disk commonly mark Hathor. The sistrum and menat ornament connect her with ritual music. Hathoric capitals at Dendera display distinctive cow ears. Horns and a sun disk also appear with Isis, so context remains essential.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Dendera was a major center of Hathor worship, with festivals linking her to Horus at Edfu. As Mistress of the West she also welcomed the dead. Funerary responsibilities coexisted with celebration and music, resisting any reduction of her identity to a goddess of romantic love.

figures.name: 埃列什基伽勒
figures.title: 美索不达米亚冥界女王

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 埃列什基伽勒是美索不达米亚冥界的女主人，其苏美尔语名字常释为大地之主母，语境中指向地下国度。在伊南娜下冥界的叙事中，她是伊南娜的姐姐；其他文本又发展出她与涅尔伽勒的配偶关系。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 苏美尔语《伊南娜下冥界》写来访女神经过七道门，逐一被除去服饰与权能标志，最终遭判决成为悬挂的尸体。恩基创造的使者回应埃列什基伽勒的痛苦，取得遗体并使伊南娜复生；离开冥界仍须提供替身，死亡秩序并未就此废除。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 冥界宫殿、门禁和王座比单一动物更能提示她的身份。常被称作夜之女王的古代浮雕究竟表现她、伊什塔尔或其他角色，学界仍有分歧，不应当作已证实肖像。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 苏美尔语与阿卡德语冥界故事的情节和人物配置并不完全一致。埃列什基伽勒统治死者之域，却不是基督教意义的魔鬼；相关叙事强调死亡边界、礼法和权力，而非简单的善恶报应。

en.name: Ereshkigal
en.title: Queen of the Mesopotamian Underworld

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Ereshkigal rules the Mesopotamian realm of the dead. Her Sumerian name is commonly understood as Lady of the Great Earth, referring here to the underworld. Narratives of the descent of Inanna identify her as an elder sister; other compositions develop her relationship with Nergal.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: In the Sumerian descent narrative, Inanna passes seven gates, losing garments and emblems of power before being killed and hung as a corpse. Beings fashioned by Enki respond sympathetically to the suffering of Ereshkigal and obtain the body. Revival still requires a substitute for departure.

sections.title: Symbols and Identification
sections.text: The underworld palace, controlled gateways, and royal authority provide firmer narrative identifiers than a particular animal. The ancient relief popularly called the Queen of the Night has been attributed to Ereshkigal, Ishtar, and other figures. Its identity remains debated, not a securely established portrait.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Sumerian and Akkadian underworld compositions differ in plot and the arrangement of divine roles. Ereshkigal governs the dead but is not a devil in the Christian sense. These narratives explore mortal limits, protocol, and authority rather than simply distributing rewards and punishments for moral conduct.

figures.name: 杜穆兹
figures.title: 牧者、伊南娜的伴侣与哀悼对象

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 杜穆兹是苏美尔传统中的牧者神，与伊南娜的爱情、婚配诗歌及死亡哀歌密切相连，后世亦以塔木兹之名流传。同名者也见于王表，但不能不加辨析便把神话角色和各位同名君王当作同一历史人物。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 在《伊南娜下冥界》中，伊南娜返回后见杜穆兹盛装安坐，没有为她哀悼，便把他交给追索替身的恶魔。相关文本又写他逃亡、求助和被捕，妹妹格什提南娜与他分担地下岁月。不同作品对死亡缘由及轮替安排的叙述并不完全相同。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 羊群、牧者身份及乳制品意象，常见于杜穆兹的爱情和丰产诗歌；哀哭提示他的死亡传统。他没有跨越所有时代的唯一造型，不能仅凭牧羊人物就认定身份。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 对杜穆兹的哀悼传播到更广阔的近东，《以西结书》也提及为塔木兹哭泣的妇女。月份名称保存其名，但把全部材料化约成每年春死秋生的植物神公式，会掩盖地方历法及文本差异。

en.name: Dumuzi
en.title: Shepherd, Consort, and Mourned God

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Dumuzi is a shepherd deity of Sumerian tradition, prominent in love poetry involving Inanna and in laments for his death. He also became known as Tammuz in later traditions. Namesakes also occur in king lists, but the divine figure and every similarly named ruler should not automatically be identified.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: In the descent of Inanna, the returning goddess finds Dumuzi splendidly seated rather than mourning and hands him to demons seeking her substitute. Related compositions recount flight, appeals for help, and capture. His sister Geshtinanna shares time below, although arrangements and explanations differ across texts.

sections.title: Symbols and Identification
sections.text: Flocks, pastoral identity, and imagery of milk products belong to poems concerning Dumuzi, love, and abundance. Lamentation evokes the traditions of his death. There is no single visual formula valid for every period, so a shepherd figure alone cannot securely establish his presence in an image.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Mourning for Dumuzi spread beyond Sumer; the biblical Book of Ezekiel mentions women weeping for Tammuz. Calendar terminology also preserved his name. Reducing all evidence to a vegetation god who dies and returns on one fixed seasonal schedule obscures differences between local calendars and compositions.

figures.name: 扎尔
figures.title: 《列王纪》中的白发英雄

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 扎尔是菲尔多西《列王纪》中的英雄，萨姆之子、鲁斯塔姆之父。他出生便有白发，父亲因恐惧异相将他遗弃山中，由神鸟西摩格养大；他是伊朗史诗中的人类人物，不能直接归类为祆教神祇。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 萨姆后来悔悟，寻回儿子；西摩格让扎尔带走羽毛，遇险可焚羽求援。扎尔与喀布尔公主鲁达芭相爱，双方家族顾虑其血统与政治后果，终获婚姻认可。鲁达芭难产时，他召来西摩格，依其指点通过切开腹部接生鲁斯塔姆。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 与青年面貌反差鲜明的白发，以及联系西摩格的羽毛，是扎尔的重要标志。波斯细密画常将山巢中的婴儿、神鸟和前来寻子的萨姆同绘，须按情节辨识。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 扎尔连接萨姆与鲁斯塔姆的英雄世系，故事涉及身体差异、父子和解及跨家族婚姻。《列王纪》保存早期伊朗传说，但成书于伊斯兰时代，人物伦理不能直接等同宗教的神学教义。

en.name: Zal
en.title: White Haired Hero of the Shahnameh

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Zal is a human hero in the Shahnameh of Ferdowsi, the son of Sam and father of Rostam. Born with white hair, he is abandoned because his father fears his unusual appearance. The Simurgh raises him; he is not simply a deity of Zoroastrian religion.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: Sam eventually recovers his son, and the Simurgh provides a feather for summoning aid. Zal loves Rudabeh, a princess of Kabul, overcoming dynastic and political objections to their marriage. When childbirth threatens her life, he summons the bird, whose instructions enable the surgical delivery of Rostam.

sections.title: Symbols and Identification
sections.text: White hair contrasting with a youthful face is a key identifier, alongside the feather linking Zal to the Simurgh. Persian manuscript paintings may show the infant in a mountain nest with the bird and the approaching Sam. Narrative context distinguishes the father, child, and later adult hero.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Zal connects the heroic generations of Sam and Rostam through stories of bodily difference, paternal reconciliation, and marriage across political boundaries. The Shahnameh preserves earlier Iranian traditions but was composed in the Islamic period. Its characterization and ethics cannot be equated directly with one religious theology.

figures.name: 西摩格
figures.title: 《列王纪》中育养英雄的神鸟

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 西摩格是伊朗传统中的神鸟，在《列王纪》中栖居高山，养育被遗弃的扎尔，并向英雄传授救难知识。其名称与更早伊朗鸟类神话存在联系，但史诗形象不能一概视为祆教神祇或某种单一教义的化身。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 西摩格把扎尔抚养成人，分别时赠羽以备召唤，后来指导鲁斯塔姆的接生。鲁斯塔姆与伊斯凡迪亚尔交战受创后，神鸟又治疗他和战马，并指出敌手眼部的弱点，指导制作柽柳箭，同时警告杀死这位王子将招致沉重后果。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 巨鸟、山巢与可焚烧求援的羽毛，是辨认《列王纪》西摩格的线索。细密画中的羽色和形体随画家而异；不能仅因古代纹样具有翅膀，便断定都是同一神鸟。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 阿塔尔《百鸟朝凤》让西摩格成为苏菲灵性追寻的终点，并利用三十只鸟的波斯语谐音展开寓意。这与《列王纪》的养育者、医治者角色属于不同文学语境，不能倒置为史诗原意。

en.name: Simurgh
en.title: The Nurturing Bird of the Shahnameh

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: The Simurgh is a marvelous bird of Iranian tradition, dwelling on a mountain in the Shahnameh and raising the abandoned Zal. Its name has connections with earlier Iranian bird traditions. This epic portrayal should not automatically be classified as a Zoroastrian deity or a single doctrinal symbol.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: The Simurgh gives Zal a summoning feather and later guides the birth of Rostam. After Rostam battles Esfandiyar, the bird heals him and his horse, reveals the vulnerability of his opponent at the eyes, and advises a tamarisk arrow while warning of grave consequences for killing him.

sections.title: Symbols and Identification
sections.text: A great bird, a mountain nest, and feathers burned to summon assistance are useful Shahnameh identifiers. Plumage and bodily form vary across manuscript paintings. An ancient winged motif cannot be labeled the Simurgh merely because it has wings; context and the history of interpretation matter.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: In the Conference of the Birds, Attar makes the Simurgh the goal of a Sufi spiritual quest and develops wordplay involving thirty birds in Persian. This literary setting differs from the nurturing and healing bird of the Shahnameh and should not be read backward as its original meaning.

figures.name: 普罗米修斯
figures.title: 盗火的提坦神与人类的恩主

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 赫西俄德《神谱》称他是提坦伊阿珀托斯之子，与阿特拉斯、厄庇米修斯为兄弟，母亲或作克吕墨涅或作亚细亚。他属于前奥林匹斯的一代，却在宙斯夺权之战中站在宙斯一边，因此仍留在新的神界秩序之内，而非被投入塔耳塔罗斯。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《神谱》与《工作与时日》记他在墨科涅分牛时以油脂裹骨头欺骗宙斯，宙斯藏起火种，他又用茴香杆把火盗回人间，宙斯遂命造潘多拉为罚。埃斯库罗斯《被缚的普罗米修斯》则改写为反抗暴政的殉道者，另加高加索缚身与鹰啄肝脏的情节。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 茴香杆火炬是最稳定的标识，后世又添指环与鹰。雅典陶瓶绘有盗火与受罚场面，雕像多表现裸身受难的躯体；“以泥土造人”的母题主要见于晚期作家与罗马艺术，并不属于荷马。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 赫西俄德笔下他是狡黠的欺骗者，受罚理所应当；埃斯库罗斯却把他抬为文明的赐予者与专制的受害者，两种古代评价彼此冲突。歌德、雪莱与马克思各有取用，普罗米修斯因而成为技术、反抗与启蒙的复合象征，而非某一城邦的祭祀对象。

en.name: Prometheus
en.title: The Titan who stole fire for mortals

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: In Hesiod the Theogony Prometheus is a Titan, son of Iapetos and brother of Atlas and Epimetheus, born before the Olympian order and so older than Zeus. He nevertheless sided with Zeus in the war against the Titans, which left him inside the new divine order rather than outside it.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Hesiod tells how Prometheus tricked Zeus at Mekone, hiding meat under an unappetising hide and bones under fat, and how he later stole fire in a fennel stalk after Zeus hid it. Zeus answered with Pandora. The Prometheus Bound of Aeschylus recasts him as a tortured martyr chained in the Caucasus.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Prometheus carries a fennel-stalk torch, and later art adds the ring and the eagle. Attic vase painting shows the theft of fire and the punishment, while statues favour a naked, suffering body. The creator-of-mankind motif, modelling humans from clay, belongs mostly to later writers and Roman art rather than to Homer.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: For Hesiod, Prometheus is a clever deceiver whose punishment is deserved. Aeschylus turns him into the benefactor of civilisation and a victim of tyranny, and the two ancient verdicts contradict each other. Goethe, Shelley and Marx each reused him, which is why he now stands for technology, revolt and enlightenment.

figures.name: 珀耳塞福涅
figures.title: 冥后与四季轮转的女儿

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 宙斯与得墨忒耳之女，少女时代称科瑞（Kore），意为“少女”。荷马体《得墨忒耳颂歌》记她在倪萨草地采花时被哈得斯劫走；赫西俄德《神谱》只简短提到她成为冥府王后，未展开被劫的细节。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 得墨忒耳悲怒之下令大地荒芜，宙斯只好命哈得斯放人；因她在冥界吃了石榴籽，每年须留住数月，归返时大地回春。奥维德《变形记》又加入她与阿佛洛狄忒争夺阿多尼斯，以及忒修斯与庇里托俄斯闯入冥府的情节。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 石榴、麦穗、火炬与蛇是主要标志；作科瑞时手持花篮或谷穗，作冥后时执权杖、戴冠。希腊瓶画中她常与哈得斯并坐，或出现在厄琉西斯祭祀场景，头戴谷穗冠的形象多与得墨忒耳成对。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 厄琉西斯秘仪以她与得墨忒耳为核心，是古代希腊最重要的秘祭，入教者守密。现代解释常把故事简化为四季寓言，但古代文本本身更关注母女分离、冥界权能与谷物的丰产；她既是可怖的冥府女主，也是被迎回的少女。

en.name: Persephone
en.title: Queen of the underworld and daughter of the harvest

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Persephone is the daughter of Zeus and Demeter, called Kore, the maiden, before her marriage. The Homeric Hymn to Demeter describes her seizure by Hades while gathering flowers at Nysa. Hesiod mentions her only briefly as queen of the dead, without narrating the abduction itself.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Demeter withdraws and the earth starves until Zeus orders her daughter returned. Because Persephone has eaten pomegranate seeds, she must spend part of each year below, and the earth blooms at her return. Ovid adds her quarrel with Aphrodite over Adonis and the failed descent of Theseus and Peirithoos.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Pomegranate, wheat ears, torches and snakes mark her. As Kore she holds flowers or grain; as queen she carries a sceptre and wears a crown, often seated beside Hades. Attic vases place her in Eleusinian scenes, and she is regularly paired with Demeter in cult images.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The Eleusinian Mysteries centred on mother and daughter and were the most important secret cult of the Greek world. Modern readers reduce the story to a seasonal allegory, but ancient texts stress separation, reunion and power over the dead. She is both a terrifying queen and a recovered girl.

figures.name: 赫拉克勒斯
figures.title: 十二功业的英雄与凡人升神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 宙斯与阿尔克墨涅之子，名义上的父亲是安菲特律翁，故属忒拜一支；因赫拉的敌意，他从婴儿时便受迫害。希腊语作 Herakles，意为“赫拉的荣耀”，罗马人音译为 Hercules 并纳入自己的宗教与政治象征体系。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 主要叙事见阿波罗多洛斯《书库》、狄奥多罗斯与欧里庇得斯的悲剧：完成十二功业（涅墨亚狮、九头蛇、刻耳柏洛斯等），受役于欧律斯透斯，远征四方；晚年误穿马人涅索斯的毒血衣，于俄塔山自焚，火葬后升神并娶赫柏。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 狮皮头盔与披风、橄榄木棒、弓与箭袋是稳定标识，雕像强调肌肉、短须与矮壮体格。他常在瓶画中与赫拉、雅典娜同场；“赫拉克勒斯之结”与直布罗陀的“赫拉克勒斯之柱”也由他得名。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 斯多亚派把他视为忍苦成德的典范，罗马则奉他为国家与胜利的保护者，在阿文提诺山与博阿里乌姆广场设祭。文艺复兴以后他成为“力量战胜野蛮”的图像，现代流行文化的大力士形象已失去古代原型中暴怒、受难与庇护并存的多面性。

en.name: Hercules (Herakles)
en.title: The hero of twelve labours who became a god

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Herakles is the son of Zeus and Alkmene, his mortal father being Amphitryon, and so belongs to Theban legend. Hera persecutes him from infancy. The Greek name means glory of Hera; the Romans transliterated it as Hercules and absorbed him into their own religious and political symbolism.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: The main narrative survives in Apollodorus, Diodorus and several tragedies: the twelve labours, including the Nemean lion, the Hydra and Cerberus, service under Eurystheus, and far-flung campaigns. He dies from the poisoned blood of the centaur Nessos, burns on Mount Oeta, and is received among the gods.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Lion scalp, olive club, bow and quiver identify him, and statues stress a short, muscular, bearded physique. Vase painting often sets him against Hera or beside Athena. The Herakles knot and the Pillars of Hercules, at the strait of Gibraltar, both take his name.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Stoics read him as endurance turned into virtue, while Rome honoured him as a guardian of state and victory, with shrines at the Aventine and the Forum Boarium. Since the Renaissance he images strength defeating savagery; modern popular culture keeps the muscle but loses the anger, suffering and protection of the ancient figure.

figures.name: 忒修斯
figures.title: 雅典的王与迷宫屠牛者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 雅典王埃勾斯之子，一说其父为海神波塞冬；母亲是特洛曾公主埃特拉，故他在特洛曾外祖父家中长大。成年后取道陆路赴雅典，沿途除掉多名强盗。普鲁塔克《忒修斯传》把他与罗慕路斯并列作传，辨析传说中的史实成分。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 核心故事为入克里特迷宫杀死牛首人身的弥诺陶洛斯，靠阿里阿德涅给的线团脱身，随后弃她于纳克索斯岛；另有与庇里托俄斯的结义、劫走海伦、下冥府受困等情节。归航时忘换白帆，埃勾斯投海而死，爱琴海因此得名。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 短剑、线团、凉鞋与棒槌是常见标志；雅典红绘瓶多绘他制服弥诺陶洛斯或擒拿强盗。作为建城英雄，他出现在帕特农神庙与赫菲斯托斯神庙的浮雕中，与雅典娜、赫拉克勒斯并列。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 雅典借他的形象宣示对爱奥尼亚的宗主地位，把“统一阿提卡”说成他的政绩，属政治神话。普鲁塔克对他与罗慕路斯皆有存疑，修昔底德则把他视为传说中的王。现代研究把迷宫母题联系到克诺索斯考古与弥诺斯文明的记忆。

en.name: Theseus
en.title: The Athenian king who killed the Minotaur

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Theseus is son of Aegeus of Athens, or in other versions of Poseidon, and of Aethra of Troizen, where he was raised. Coming of age, he travelled to Athens by land and cleared the road of robbers. Plutarch pairs his life with Romulus and weighs the historical against the legendary.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: His central deed is entering the Cretan labyrinth, killing the bull-headed Minotaur and escaping with Ariadne thread, whom he then abandons on Naxos. Other episodes include his oath-friendship with Peirithoos, the abduction of Helen and a failed descent to Hades. Forgetting to change the sails, he causes his father to leap to death.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Short sword, thread, sandals and club identify him, and red-figure vases show him mastering the Minotaur or seizing bandits. As a founding hero he appears on the Parthenon and the Hephaisteion, set beside Athena and Herakles as a model of Athenian courage.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Athens used Theseus to claim leadership of the Ionian world, crediting him with the unification of Attica, a political myth rather than a record. Plutarch doubts details and Thucydides treats him as a legendary king. Modern scholarship links the labyrinth to Knossos and memories of Minoan Crete.

figures.name: 俄耳甫斯
figures.title: 琴声动冥府的色雷斯歌者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 传说为色雷斯人，缪斯卡利俄珀与色雷斯王俄阿格罗斯之子，也有更古老的谱系说法。古典文献中他既是随阿耳戈号远航的歌者，又是“俄耳甫斯诗”这一神秘诗篇传统的托名作者，两者不可混为一谈。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 妻子欧律狄刻被蛇咬死后，他携琴入冥府，以歌声打动哈得斯与珀耳塞福涅，获准带妻返回，条件是途中不得回头；将近地面时他回头一望，妻子遂永留冥界。维吉尔《农事诗》与奥维德《变形记》各有一版，细节与情绪侧重不同。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 里拉琴、色雷斯软帽与长袍是稳定标志；瓶画中他常坐在岩石上弹琴，周围聚集走兽与树木，表现音乐驯服自然。后期图像演变为头颅被撕下后仍在歌唱，随水漂流至列斯堡岛。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 其死因古说不一：或被酒神女祭司撕裂，或因轻蔑妇女而被杀，也有被宙斯雷击之说。俄耳甫斯教与毕达哥拉斯派借其名传播灵魂不朽与轮回的观念；蒙特威尔第《奥菲欧》以来，歌剧与诗歌反复重写这段回头之痛。

en.name: Orpheus
en.title: The Thracian singer who moved the underworld

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Orpheus is a Thracian, son of the Muse Calliope and of Oiagros, though older genealogies exist. Classical sources know him both as the singer who sailed with the Argonauts and as the borrowed name behind the Orphic poems, two things that should not be conflated.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: When his wife Eurydice dies of a snakebite, Orpheus enters Hades, wins over its rulers with song and is allowed to lead her out on condition that he not look back. He turns, and she is lost. Virgil in the Georgics and Ovid in the Metamorphoses tell the story with different emphases.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The lyre, the Thracian cap and long robe identify him. Vases show him seated on a rock, singing, surrounded by animals and trees, music taming nature. Later images have his severed head still singing as it floats to Lesbos, a motif that reshapes the whole story.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Ancient accounts of his death disagree: Maenads tear him apart, or he is killed for scorning women, or Zeus strikes him with lightning. Orphic and Pythagorean circles used his name for teachings on the soul and rebirth. Since Monteverdi, opera and poetry keep returning to that backward glance.

figures.name: 阿喀琉斯
figures.title: 伊利昂城下的捷足英雄

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 佩琉斯与海中女神忒提斯之子，统治色萨利弗提亚的密耳弥多涅人。荷马《伊利亚特》开篇即点明“女神的儿子阿喀琉斯的愤怒”为主题；史诗并未提到母亲以冥河之水浸体使他刀枪不入，那是后世的补充。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《伊利亚特》只写战争第十年的数十日：因与阿伽门农争夺女俘而罢战，好友帕特罗克洛斯借其铠甲出战被杀，他复出杀死赫克托耳并凌辱尸体，最终应普里阿摩斯之求归还遗体。史诗以赫克托耳的葬礼收束，未写他自己的死亡。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 赫菲斯托斯所铸的大盾（刻有宇宙与城邦图景）、长枪、铠甲与神马是主要标志，瓶画中他多赤身持盾。所谓“阿喀琉斯之踵”不见于荷马，而见于斯塔提乌斯《阿喀琉斯纪》等后世文本与图像传统。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 荷马之后的《埃塞俄比斯》等史诗写他死于帕里斯之箭。悲剧与哲学常以他代表“短命而光荣”的抉择，《奥德赛》中他的亡魂却宁可在人间为雇农；这一反差是古代接受史的关键。今日通用的“阿喀琉斯之踵”并非荷马原文。

en.name: Achilles
en.title: The swift-footed hero before the walls of Troy

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Achilles is the son of Peleus and the sea goddess Thetis and rules the Myrmidons of Phthia in Thessaly. The Iliad opens by naming the wrath of Achilles as its subject. The epic never mentions a mother dipping him in the Styx to make him invulnerable; that belongs to later tradition.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: The Iliad covers only some weeks of the tenth year: his quarrel with Agamemnon over a captive, his withdrawal, the death of Patroclus in his armour, his return, the killing of Hector and the maltreatment of the corpse, ended by pity for Priam. It closes with the funeral of Hector, not with his own death.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The shield forged by Hephaestus, with its cosmos and cities, his spear, armour and immortal horses mark him, and vase painters show him naked behind the shield. The heel is absent from Homer and appears in later texts such as the Achilleid of Statius and in Roman imagery.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Post-Homeric epics such as the Aethiopis have him killed by an arrow from Paris. Tragedy and philosophy make him the choice of a short glorious life, yet in the Odyssey his ghost says he would rather be a hired labourer among the living. The modern Achilles heel is not Homeric.

figures.name: 伊卡洛斯
figures.title: 蜡翼少年与父亲的坠落

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 工匠代达罗斯之子，母亲据说是弥诺斯家的女奴瑙克拉忒。父子因代达罗斯为帕西淮造木牛、又为阿里阿德涅造迷宫而失宠，被弥诺斯囚禁于克里特。伊卡洛斯本人在故事中始终是少年，没有独立的功业。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 完整文本主要来自奥维德《变形记》卷八：代达罗斯用羽毛与蜡粘成双翼，叮嘱儿子不要飞得太低以免海水浸湿，也不要太高以免日光融化；伊卡洛斯得意忘形越飞越高，蜡融羽散，坠海而死，父亲在空中呼唤其名，附近的海与岛遂以他命名。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 蜡翼、散落的羽毛、伸向海面的手臂是稳定标志；古代图像多表现他裸身张开双臂下坠，代达罗斯在上方呼喊。文艺复兴版画与布鲁盖尔《伊卡洛斯的坠落》构成了最有名的近代图像传统。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 阿波罗多洛斯《书库》与希腊化文献也提到此事，细节略有出入。奥维德的版本关注父子关系与技术之限，后世多以“僭越”读之，也有人读作技术乐观与少年鲁莽的寓言；这两种读法都属接受史，而非古典文本的原意。

en.name: Icarus
en.title: The boy on wax wings and his fall

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Icarus is the son of the craftsman Daedalus, his mother said to be Naucrate, a slave in the household of Minos. Father and son are imprisoned in Crete after Daedalus builds the wooden cow for Pasiphae and the labyrinth for Ariadne. Icarus himself has no separate career in the story.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: The fullest account is Ovid, Metamorphoses book eight. Daedalus joins feathers with wax and warns his son to fly neither low enough for the sea to soak the wings nor high enough for the sun to melt them. Icarus climbs in delight, the wax runs, and he falls; sea and island take his name.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Wax wings, falling feathers and an arm stretched towards the water identify him. Ancient images show a naked youth with outspread arms dropping while Daedalus calls from above. Renaissance prints and Bruegels Landscape with the Fall of Icarus created the best known modern version of the scene.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Apollodorus and Hellenistic writers mention the story with small variations. Ovid is interested in the father, the son and the limits of craft; later ages read the tale as hubris, or as a parable of technical confidence and youthful recklessness. Both readings belong to reception, not to the ancient text.

figures.name: 芬里尔
figures.title: 被缚的巨狼与诸神黄昏

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 洛基与女巨人安格尔波达之子，与耶梦加得、海拉为同胞兄妹。斯诺里《散文埃达·吉尔法基宁》记诸神因预言得知他将带来灾祸，把他带到阿斯加德抚养，后因其迅速暴长、形貌可怖而不敢再留。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 前两条锁链雷锭与德罗米都被他轻易挣断；第三次诸神改用侏儒以猫步、山根、鸟唾等六物制成的格莱普尼尔，他疑心有诈，要求有人把手放入口中作保，提尔伸出右手而失之。他被缚于林格维岛，口中撑剑，涎水成河。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 巨狼、张开的巨口、断裂的锁链与撑口的剑是主要标志。冰岛手稿插图与瑞典教堂浮雕常表现他咬断锁链，或与吞日的狼并置；末日图像的核心是“吞下奥丁的狼”，这一母题在中世纪北欧艺术中反复出现。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 《诗体埃达·女巫的预言》与《散文埃达》都写他在诸神黄昏挣脱，吞下奥丁，随后被维达杀死。学界把他联系到狼人、亡命者与被束缚的恶魔母题；中世纪的基督教写手也乐于把他读作恶魔的对应物，但文本本身仍属异教神话的遗产。

en.name: Fenrir
en.title: The bound wolf that devours Odin

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Fenrir is the son of Loki and the giantess Angrboda, brother of Jormungandr and Hel. Snorri in Gylfaginning says the gods, warned by prophecy that he will bring disaster, raise him in Asgard until his monstrous growth and appearance make them afraid to keep him.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: He snaps the first two fetters, Leyding and Dromi. The third, Gleipnir, is made by dwarves from six impossible things, including the tread of a cat and the spit of a bird. Suspicious, Fenrir demands a hand in his mouth as pledge; Tyr gives his right hand and loses it. He is bound on Lyngvi.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The wolf, the gaping jaw, the broken fetter and the sword propping his mouth open are the standard markers. Icelandic manuscript drawings and Swedish church carvings show him snapping chains or paired with the wolf that swallows the sun. The wolf that devours Odin dominates eschatological imagery.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Voluspa and Snorri agree that he breaks free at Ragnarok, swallows Odin and is then killed by Vidar. Scholars link him to werewolf, outlaw and bound-demon motifs. Medieval Christian writers readily read him as a figure of the devil, but the material remains a pagan mythological inheritance.

figures.name: 耶梦加得
figures.title: 环绕中庭的尘世巨蛇与雷神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 洛基与安格尔波达之子，与芬里尔、海拉同胞。斯诺里称他为“尘世巨蛇”（Miðgarðsormr）；奥丁把他抛入环绕中庭的大海，他在海中长到能自衔其尾、环抱整个大地，因而与索尔结下宿怨；《女巫的预言》与《散文埃达》都把他列为诸神黄昏的关键角色。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 他与索尔有三次交锋：在巨人乌特加德-洛基处，索尔所举的“猫”其实是他；在巨人希米尔船上，索尔以牛头为饵把他钓起，举锤欲击时巨人割断钓线；诸神黄昏时两人在维格利德原野互杀，索尔走出九步后中毒倒地。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 衔尾蛇形态、毒牙与翻涌的海浪是主要标志。符文石与手稿插图常把“索尔钓蛇”与诸神黄昏并置：索尔站在船上，脚穿破船底，牛头作饵。这一母题在英格兰、瑞典与哥特兰的画像石上都有发现。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 《许米尔之歌》与《散文埃达》都写钓蛇，细节不同：前者近于一次失败的狩猎，后者强调巨人见到蛇头时的惊恐并割断钓线。世界巨蛇母题可与印度阿难陀等相比，但结构相似不等于同源传播，需谨慎。

en.name: Jormungandr
en.title: The world serpent encircling Midgard

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Jormungandr is a child of Loki and Angrboda, sibling of Fenrir and Hel. Snorri calls him the world serpent. Odin throws him into the ocean surrounding Midgard, where he grows until he can bite his own tail and encircle the earth, which sets up his lasting feud with Thor.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: They meet three times. In the hall of Utgard-Loki the cat Thor tries to lift is the serpent. On the giant Hymir boat Thor hauls him up using an ox head as bait until Hymir cuts the line. At Ragnarok they kill each other on the field of Vigrid, Thor walking nine steps before the poison takes him.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The tail-biting ring, venomous fangs and heaving sea mark him. Runestones and manuscript pictures pair the serpent with Ragnarok, showing Thor in a boat with an ox head and his foot through the hull. The motif appears on stones in England, Sweden and Gotland.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Hymiskvida and Snorri both tell of the fishing but differ: the poem is closer to a failed hunt, while Snorri stresses the giant terror at the serpent head and his cutting of the line. The world serpent invites comparison with Indian Ananta, though shared structure is not evidence of transmission.

figures.name: 尤弥尔
figures.title: 被分尸造世的原初巨人

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 《女巫的预言》把他列为巨人一族，斯诺里《散文埃达》则记他由冰与火交汇处埃利瓦加尔河的毒水滴凝成，是霜巨人的始祖；他沉睡时从腋下与双脚生出后代，与母牛奥德姆布拉同以冰霜为食。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 奥丁与维利、维三兄弟杀死尤弥尔，伤口涌出的血水成洪，淹死大部分霜巨人，只有贝尔格尔米尔乘船逃生，成为新巨人族的祖先。诸神把他的肉造成大地、骨造成山、血造成海、颅骨造成天穹、脑造成云，眉毛围成中庭，蛆虫化为侏儒。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 以身体部位命名地貌是北欧创世叙事的特征：巨人躯体与大地结构一一对应、洪血与颅骨天穹是主要意象。中世纪冰岛抄本中有“人形—世界”的图示，但直接标注尤弥尔者多为近代学者的重构，不能当作中世纪原图使用，文本本身并未留下对应的图绘。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 此神话只见于《诗体埃达》与斯诺里，无法确证为更早的共同日耳曼信仰，也可能是冰岛基督教时期文人整理的成果。“以原人之身造世界”与印度普鲁沙、中国盘古结构相似，学界多视为类型学平行，而非传播证据。

en.name: Ymir
en.title: The primeval giant dismembered to make the world

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Voluspa counts Ymir among the giants, and Snorri describes him as formed from venomous drops in the river Elivagar where ice and fire meet, the ancestor of all frost giants. While he sleeps, descendants grow from his armpits and feet, and he feeds on the milk of the cow Audhumla.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Odin, Vili and Ve kill Ymir, and the blood from his wounds floods the world, drowning all the frost giants except Bergelmir, who escapes by boat and founds a new line. The gods make earth from his flesh, mountains from bones, sea from blood and sky from his skull; his brows wall in Midgard.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The correspondence between giant body and world structure, the flood of blood and the skull as sky are his defining images. Some Icelandic manuscripts contain man-and-cosmos diagrams, but the ones explicitly labelled Ymir are mostly modern scholarly reconstructions rather than medieval drawings.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The myth survives only in the Poetic Edda and in Snorri, so it cannot be shown to reflect an older common Germanic belief and may be the work of Christian-era Icelandic compilers. Creating the world from a primal body resembles Indian Purusha and Chinese Pangu, usually read as typological parallels, not evidence of diffusion.

figures.name: 伊登
figures.title: 掌管青春苹果的阿萨女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 斯诺里《散文埃达》称她是诗人布拉吉之妻，属阿萨神族，其名可能与“更新、回春”之义相关。她保管能让诸神保持青春的苹果，装在一只梣木匣中；诸神衰老时便向她索取，她因此是诸神得以不老的条件之一。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 最完整的故事见《散文埃达·布拉吉的谈话》：巨人夏基化鹰诱捕洛基，洛基以伊登为赎，把她骗出阿斯加德；她一去，诸神迅速衰老，遂逼洛基以隼形把她变回，夏基追至阿斯加德被火堆烧死。另《哈巴尔之歌》保存她与神秘问话者的对话残片。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 苹果、梣木匣与四季更新是主要标志。古代图像材料极少，多依文本想象为持果的少女；她的苹果常被与希腊的金苹果、凯尔特阿瓦隆的苹果混同，其实三者属于彼此独立的神话体系。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 该神话以“诸神也会衰老”为前提，说明青春苹果是宇宙秩序得以延续的条件，此点常被忽略。19世纪民族主义与瓦格纳式改写把她浪漫化，当代流行文化中的“青春女神”用法更远离中世纪文本，多属现代再创造。

en.name: Idun
en.title: The goddess who keeps the apples of youth

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Snorri makes Idun the wife of the poet Bragi and one of the Aesir; her name probably relates to renewal or rejuvenation. She keeps the apples that preserve the gods from old age in a box of ash wood, and the gods come to her when they feel age coming on.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: The fullest story is in Skaldskaparmal: the giant Thjazi, in eagle form, traps Loki, who buys his freedom by luring Idun out of Asgard. With her gone the gods age at once and force Loki to bring her back in falcon shape; Thjazi pursues them and is burned on the walls of Asgard.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Apples, the ash-wood box and the renewal of the seasons define her. Ancient images are almost nonexistent, so she is usually imagined from texts as a girl holding fruit. Her apples are often confused with the Greek golden apples or the apples of Avalon, which belong to separate traditions.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The myth assumes that gods can grow old, making the apples a condition for the continued order of the cosmos, a point often overlooked. Nineteenth-century nationalism and Wagnerian rewriting sentimentalised her, and the modern youth goddess of popular culture is a further reinvention rather than a medieval figure.

figures.name: 布伦希尔德
figures.title: 瓦尔斯伦加萨迦中的女英雄

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 主要见于《诗体埃达》英雄诗与十三世纪冰岛散文体《瓦尔斯伦加萨迦》（本于更早诗歌），她是匈人王布德利之女、阿提拉之妹，与《尼伯龙根之歌》的布伦希尔德相对应。她属英雄传说人物，不是《散文埃达》神名录中的瓦尔基里。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 她与西格德互誓婚约，西格德却因饮下忘情之酒而化形代贡纳尔求婚，越过火墙三日；婚后她发现真相，指认背誓，促成西格德被杀，自己亦在火葬中殉身。萨迦以家族血仇与誓言破裂推动结局，细节与《尼伯龙根之歌》颇有出入。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 火墙、盾与铠甲、安德瓦拉纳乌特金戒指是主要标志。图像多来自中世纪北欧教堂门板与木刻，表现她坐于火中或与西格德相会；闪亮的带翼头盔与甲胄则多为19世纪舞台与插画的加工。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 她是文学萨迦（fornaldarsaga）中的英雄，而非宗教崇拜对象；文本成于基督教时期的冰岛，保存了异教英雄世界的记忆。瓦格纳《尼伯龙根的指环》把她与女武神合并，是现代重构，不应回读为中世纪原貌。

en.name: Brynhild
en.title: The Volsunga heroine behind the ring of fire

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Brynhild belongs to the heroic poems of the Poetic Edda and to Völsunga saga, a thirteenth-century Icelandic prose compilation drawing on older verse. She is daughter of Budli and sister of Attila, and corresponds to Brunhild in the Nibelungenlied. She is a legendary heroine, not one of the valkyries listed by Snorri.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: She and Sigurd swear an oath, but Sigurd, made forgetful by a drink, takes his shape to woo her for Gunnar and rides her fire wall for three nights. Learning of the deception, she demands and obtains the death of Sigurd, and dies on his pyre. Family feud and broken oath drive the saga to its end.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The wall of flame, shield and mail, and the ring Andvaranaut mark her. Images come mainly from medieval Scandinavian church doors and carvings showing her seated in fire or meeting Sigurd. The winged helmet and shining armour are nineteenth-century stage and illustration work.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: She is a figure of legendary saga rather than an object of cult, recorded in Christian-era Iceland that preserved memories of a pagan heroic world. Wagner in the Ring cycle merges her with the valkyries, a modern construction that should not be read back into the medieval sources.

figures.name: 埃涅阿斯
figures.title: 从特洛伊到拉丁姆的建城先祖

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 特洛伊王子安喀塞斯与女神阿佛洛狄忒（罗马称维纳斯）之子，属特洛伊王族的旁支。荷马《伊利亚特》中他是特洛伊一方的重要战将，屡次在危急时被神救走；罗马传统则把他推为阿尔巴隆加之祖与尤利乌斯家族的祖先，两者层次不同。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 维吉尔《埃涅阿斯纪》写他背负父亲、携幼子阿斯卡尼乌斯逃离火城，历海上漂泊、迦太基女王狄多之恋与其自杀、下冥府见亡父、抵拉丁姆与图尔努斯决战。这是公元前一世纪的文人史诗，属建城起源叙事，并非同代史料记录。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 背负老父、手牵幼子、携家庭神像的“三重形象”是核心标志，钱币与浮雕以此表现虔敬（pietas）。维吉尔笔下他的盾由伏尔甘所铸，刻着未来罗马的史事，明显与《伊利亚特》中阿喀琉斯之盾形成互文。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 奥古斯都时代借埃涅阿斯为朱利乌斯家族与罗马统治立传说谱系，李维、狄奥尼修斯等史家也记录多种异文。中世纪把他读作朝圣者的寓言，近代则视之为帝国意识形态与文学想象的结合；其“历史性”始终是传说谱系，而非编年记录。

en.name: Aeneas
en.title: The Trojan ancestor of Rome

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Aeneas is a Trojan prince, son of Anchises and the goddess Aphrodite, whom the Romans called Venus, and a junior member of the royal house. In the Iliad he is a prominent Trojan fighter repeatedly rescued by gods. Roman tradition made him ancestor of the kings of Alba Longa and of the Julian family.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: The Aeneid of Virgil, written in the first century BC, has him carry his father from burning Troy and lead his son Ascanius and the household gods westward. He loves and abandons Dido at Carthage, visits the ghost of Anchises below, and fights Turnus in Latium. It is literature, not record.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The triple image of a man carrying his aged father, leading the child and bearing the household gods expresses pietas, and coins and reliefs use it. In Virgil his shield, made by Vulcan, carries scenes of future Roman history, deliberately echoing the shield of Achilles in the Iliad.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Augustan writers used Aeneas to give the Julian family and Roman rule a legendary genealogy, while Livy and Dionysius preserved several competing versions. Medieval readers allegorised him as a pilgrim soul; modern criticism treats him as a meeting point of imperial ideology and literary imagination rather than a datable figure.

figures.name: 罗慕路斯
figures.title: 罗马的建城者与首任王

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 传说为战神玛尔斯与维斯塔贞女瑞亚·西尔维亚之子，与孪生兄弟雷穆斯同被弃于台伯河，由母狼哺育、牧人浮斯图卢斯抚养。普鲁塔克《罗慕路斯传》与李维《建城以来史》各有记载，细节、年代与怀疑程度互有出入。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 兄弟长大后推翻阿尔巴王阿穆利乌斯，却因在何处建城、以何种占卜为凭而争执；雷穆斯跃过罗慕路斯所挖的城壕（一说城墙）被杀，罗慕路斯遂以自己的名字命名罗马。为补充人口，他设计劫掠萨宾妇女，后又与萨宾人共治。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 母狼、双婴、犁沟与城墙是核心标志。建城时以犁划出城界（pomerium），象征神圣边界；著名的卡比托利欧母狼像年代有争议，双婴通常被认为是后来添加的。罗马钱币与浮雕反复使用母狼哺乳的图案。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 建城年被后世定为公元前753年，属推算而非当时记录；王政时期的史事多由共和国与帝国文人重构。帕拉蒂尼山已发现早期聚落与城墙痕迹，却无法证实孪生兄弟其人；雷穆斯之死的不同版本也反映了家族与政治立场的差异。

en.name: Romulus
en.title: Founder and first king of Rome

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Romulus is said to be son of Mars and the Vestal Rhea Silvia, twin of Remus. The babies are exposed on the Tiber, suckled by a she-wolf and raised by the herdsman Faustulus. Plutarch and Livy tell the story with different details, dates and degrees of scepticism, and both record variant versions.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: The brothers overthrow Amulius of Alba Longa, then quarrel over the site and the auspices for their city. Remus jumps over the trench, or in some versions the wall, that Romulus has drawn, and is killed; Romulus names Rome after himself. He then seizes the Sabine women to populate the settlement.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The she-wolf, the twins, the plough furrow and the wall are the standard markers. Founding involved tracing the boundary, the pomerium, with a plough, marking a sacred limit. The famous Capitoline wolf is of disputed date, and the twins are usually thought to be later additions.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The founding date of 753 BC is a later calculation, not a contemporary record, and the regal period was reconstructed by Republican and Imperial writers. Excavation on the Palatine has revealed early huts and fortifications, but no trace of the twins, whose legend served competing political claims.

figures.name: 丘比特
figures.title: 罗马的爱欲之神与箭矢

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 罗马的 Cupido 意为“欲望”，本是拉丁宗教中神性力量的人格化，后与希腊的厄洛斯（Eros）认同，成为维纳斯之子，通常以少年或孩童形象出现。他在早期罗马的国家祭祀中没有独立大神的位置，更多见于文学与私人宗教。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 阿普列乌斯《金驴记》中的“丘比特与普绪刻”是最完整的拉丁叙事：丘比特夜访普绪刻，约定不得窥其容貌；普绪刻持灯偷看，致其离去，历多项试炼后获朱庇特准许成婚并升为神。希腊化诗歌中的厄洛斯则多为顽劣孩童。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 弓与箭、火炬、双翼是主要标志，蒙眼则是后期寓意艺术所加。文艺复兴与巴洛克绘画中的胖童形象（putto）由古代小爱神演化而来，但古典时期并无固定定式，他也常被表现为一群小爱神中的一个。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 罗马文学把爱欲视为需要驯服或戏拟的力量，奥维德《爱经》把他写成军营中的士兵；中世纪寓意诗把丘比特之箭释为贪欲或神圣之爱。现代情人节的天使形象与古代宗教意涵相去甚远，主要属近代印刷与商业文化的产物。

en.name: Cupid
en.title: The Roman god of desire and his arrows

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Cupido, desire, was a Latin personification of a divine force before being identified with Greek Eros, son of Venus and usually shown as a youth or child. He holds no place among the great state gods of early Rome and appears mainly in literature, private cult and later art.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: The fullest Latin narrative is Cupid and Psyche in Apuleius, where the god visits Psyche only at night and forbids her to see him. She looks by lamplight, loses him, and after trials wins the consent of Jupiter to marriage and immortality. Hellenistic poetry prefers a mischievous child.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Bow, arrows, torch and wings identify him; the blindfold is an addition of later allegorical art. Renaissance and Baroque painters developed the chubby putto from ancient minor loves, but classical art had no single fixed type, and he often appears as one of a plurality of little gods.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Roman poets treat erotic desire as a force to be disciplined or mocked; Ovid in the Art of Love makes Cupid a soldier in his camp. Medieval allegory read his arrows as lust or as divine love. The cherub of modern Valentines belongs to commercial print culture, not to ancient religion.

figures.name: 芬恩
figures.title: 费尼安传奇的首领与智者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 爱尔兰芬尼亚故事循环（Fenian cycle）的首领，名 Fionn mac Cumhaill，父亲库马尔在一次私斗中被杀，他少年时为父复仇。主要文本见于十二世纪《伦斯特之书》所收故事、后世民谣与口传，成文时间晚于以库呼兰为中心的阿尔斯特循环。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 最著名者为“知识的鲑鱼”：他随诗人菲内卡斯学艺，烤鱼时烫伤拇指，吮指而获得智慧；另有追逐迪尔穆德与格兰妮的私奔、猎野猪、与海外来敌交锋等。晚年他与费尼安武士团渐次失势，结局有多种异文，或说老死于床榻。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 智慧之拇指、矛与盾、猎犬与鹿是主要标志；苏格兰与北爱尔兰的“巨人堤道”传说也归在他名下。他是自由武士团（fianna）的首领，而非国王；其子莪相与孙奥斯卡同属这一循环，构成父子孙三代武士的谱系。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 芬尼亚循环与阿尔斯特循环并列，但成文较晚，多经口传与抄写者整理。麦弗逊在1760年代以其子莪相之名发表《莪相集》，实为改写与仿作，曾引起真伪之争，也深刻影响了欧洲浪漫主义对“北方吟游诗人”的想象。

en.name: Finn mac Cumhaill
en.title: Leader and seer of the Fenian cycle

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Fionn mac Cumhaill leads the fianna, the roving warrior bands of Irish tradition, in the Fenian cycle. His father Cumhall is killed in a private feud and the boy avenges him. The tales survive in twelfth-century manuscripts such as the Book of Leinster, in later ballads and in oral storytelling.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: His best known story is the salmon of knowledge: while cooking the fish for the poet Finnegas, Fionn burns his thumb, sucks it and gains wisdom. Other tales follow his pursuit of Diarmuid and Grainne, his hunts and clashes with overseas raiders. Accounts of his old age vary considerably.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The thumb of knowledge, spear and shield, hounds and deer mark him. Scottish and Ulster legends attach the Giants Causeway to him. He leads a free warrior band rather than a kingdom, and his son Oisin and grandson Oscar belong to the same cycle of three generations.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The Fenian cycle stands beside the Ulster cycle of Cu Chulainn but was written down later, shaped by oral performance and scribal editing. James Macpherson published Ossian in the 1760s as a translation from Oisin, though it was largely his own composition, and the quarrel shaped European romantic ideas of the bard.

figures.name: 布兰
figures.title: 威尔士的巨人与不列颠之王

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 威尔士《马比诺吉昂》四分支之一《布兰文》中的“受祝福的布兰”（Bendigeidfran），为不列颠之王、利尔（Llŷr）之子。他属威尔士本土传统，与爱尔兰海神马纳南·麦克·利尔并非同一人物，二者常被现代读物混为一谈。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 妹妹布兰文嫁爱尔兰王马索尔威奇后受辱，布兰率军征讨；因海水太浅无法行船，他以身横卧海峡作桥，让军队踏背而过。战事中他被毒矛伤脚，命部下斩下其头带回；头颅在哈莱赫宴饮数十年，据说其埋葬有抵御入侵之力。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 巨人之躯、涉海为桥、语鸟与长年是主要标志；“布兰之头”埋于伦敦白丘的传说与王权护佑相关。威尔士文本赋予他王、巨人与渡海者三重身份，与一般的战士英雄明显不同；其名 Bendigeidfran 意为“受祝福的布兰”，也见于威尔士三题诗。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 见于《马比诺吉昂》的白书与红书两件手稿，属十二至十三世纪编定的威尔士散文故事，也保存了更早的口头记忆。学者注意他与爱尔兰“渡海远征”母题的互动，但布兰与马纳南分属不同传统，不应混同。

en.name: Bran the Blessed
en.title: The Welsh giant king of Britain

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Bendigeidfran, Bran the Blessed, is king of Britain and son of Llyr in Branwen, one of the Four Branches of the Mabinogi. He belongs to Welsh tradition and is not the Irish sea god Manannan mac Lir, although modern retellings often merge the two figures into one.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: When his sister Branwen is humiliated by Matholwch of Ireland, Bran invades. Finding the sea too shallow for ships, he lies across the strait and his men walk over his body. Wounded in the foot by a poisoned spear, he orders his head cut off and carried home, where it feasts for years.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: His giant body, the sea crossing, the speaking birds and the long feast mark him. The head, buried on the White Mount in London, was said to protect Britain from invasion. Welsh texts give him three roles at once: king, giant and bridge across water.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The tale survives in the White Book and Red Book manuscripts of the Mabinogion, prose compiled in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries from older oral material. Scholars note links with Irish voyage and invasion tales, but Bran and Manannan belong to different traditions and should not be conflated.

figures.name: 安格斯
figures.title: 博因河畔的青春与爱之神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 爱尔兰神话中的 Aengus Óg（“年轻的安格斯”），达格达与博因河女神博安之子，属图阿萨·德·达南一族。传说他于一日之内受孕与出生，由米迪尔抚养，故又称“青春之子”（Mac Óc），与青春、爱欲和诗歌相关。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 核心故事为《艾莲的求婚》：他在梦中爱上少女艾莲，寻访经年，与养父米迪尔争夺，最终以天鹅之形相认相随。另一故事讲他如何从父亲达格达手中求得博因河畔的宫殿（Brú na Bóinne），以“昼与夜”的文字游戏取胜。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 天鹅、环绕其头的四鸟（吻旁有三鸟歌唱）、博因河湾与史前墓丘是主要标志。纽格莱奇通道墓在后世传说中被当作他的居所，考古上属新石器时代建筑，与神话并无直接对应关系，不宜当作同一证据。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 文本见于《伦斯特之书》与《黛尔吉的牛劫》等中古爱尔兰抄本，属文人整理的神话与传奇材料。他与青春、爱欲和诗歌相关，并非主管生育的职能神；叶芝等近代作家把他浪漫化为“青春与美”的象征，与中古贵族叙事语境有别。

en.name: Aengus Og
en.title: God of youth and love by the Boyne

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Aengus Og, Aengus the Young, is son of the Dagda and the river goddess Boann and belongs to the Tuatha De Danann. Conceived and born within a single day, he is fostered by Midir and called Mac Oc, son of youth, and is associated with youth, love and poetry.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In The Wooing of Etain he falls in love with a girl seen in a dream, searches for her for years, contends with his fosterfather Midir and finally recognises her in swan form. Another tale tells how he wins the Bru na Boinne, the bend of the Boyne, from the Dagda by a trick of words.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Swans, the four birds around his head, the Boyne bend and the great prehistoric mounds mark him. Newgrange, a Neolithic passage tomb, was later said to be his dwelling, though archaeology and myth are separate orders of evidence and should not be conflated.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: His stories appear in medieval Irish manuscripts including the Book of Leinster and the Cattle Raid of Cooley, edited by literate clerics from older material. He concerns youth, desire and poetry rather than fertility as a function. Yeats made him a symbol of beauty in modern verse.

figures.name: 塞赫美特
figures.title: 狮首的瘟疫与治疗女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 孟菲斯神学中的女战神，普塔之妻、奈费尔图姆之母，名意为“强有力的”。她与哈托尔、穆特、巴斯特等女神在职能上常有重叠，被视为“拉之眼”的凶猛形态。相关神学文本见于沙巴卡石碑，该碑是公元前八世纪抄录的古老文本。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 最著名者为“拉之眼”的毁灭：人类密谋反叛拉，拉遣其眼（此处作哈托尔—塞赫美特）下界杀戮，血流成河；拉以红赭石染酒倾于地面，女神饮醉而止，杀戮遂停。另有大量咒语把她与瘟疫之箭及治疗并置，二者是同一位女神的两面。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 狮首女身、日盘与圣蛇、纸草权杖、生命之符是主要标志，常着红色亚麻衣。她的祭司在孟菲斯兼行医术与咒术，被称为“塞赫美特祭司”的医师，是古代埃及少见的兼具神职与医疗身份者。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 她既降瘟疫也解瘟疫，故医生与咒语皆求她；每年“醉宴”以饮酒纪念杀戮的终止，可能与她的祭祀有关。现代读物常把她简化为战争女神，忽略了医疗、王权庇护与“拉之眼”功能的复杂性。

en.name: Sekhmet
en.title: The lion-headed goddess of plague and healing

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Sekhmet is the Memphite goddess of war and pestilence, wife of Ptah and mother of Nefertem; her name means the powerful one. She overlaps with Hathor, Mut and Bastet and is a fierce form of the Eye of Re. The Memphite theology is known from the Shabaka Stone, an eighth-century copy of an older text.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Her best known myth is the slaughter wrought by the Eye of Re. When humanity plots against Re, he sends his eye, here Hathor or Sekhmet, to destroy them. Re dyes beer with red ochre and pours it out; the goddess drinks, becomes drunk and stops. Spells call her arrows of pestilence and her cures alike.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A lioness head on a human body, sun disk with uraeus, papyrus sceptre and ankh identify her, and she often wears red linen. Her priests at Memphis combined healing with incantation, so the priests of Sekhmet worked as physicians as well as ritual specialists, an unusual double role.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: She both sends and cures plague, so doctors and spells appeal to her. The Festival of Drunkenness, commemorating the end of the slaughter, may belong to her cult. Modern summaries flatten her into a war goddess and lose the medical, royal-protective dimensions of the Eye of Re.

figures.name: 普塔
figures.title: 孟菲斯的造物之神与匠神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 孟菲斯的主神，与塞赫美特、奈费尔图姆构成三联神。其名或与“开启”、雕刻家相关；在孟菲斯神学中，他不靠生育或战斗，而凭心（思想）与舌（言语）创造万物，因而常被形容为以语言造世的匠神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 主要材料是沙巴卡石碑所载的孟菲斯神学：普塔以心构想、以舌命名，诸神与万物由此而生，文本又把传统的九柱神系统纳入普塔名下，宣称孟菲斯为创世之地。这套叙述带有明显的一神论式倾向，与赫利奥波利斯神学形成竞争。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 木乃伊状的紧身衣、蓝色颅帽、直杖与安卡是主要标志，有时立于台座上，形如工匠之作。希腊人把他与赫菲斯托斯认同，故孟菲斯在希腊文献中有“火神之城”的称呼；阿匹斯圣牛也与他相关。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 他是工匠、建筑者与匠人的保护神，孟菲斯为其重要祭司中心，阿匹斯圣牛养于附近。沙巴卡石碑本身是公元前八世纪沙巴卡王命人抄录的古老文本，为研究埃及创世论的关键材料，其原件的年代至今仍有争论。

en.name: Ptah
en.title: The Memphite creator and patron of craftsmen

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Ptah is the chief god of Memphis, forming a triad with Sekhmet and Nefertem. His name may relate to opening or to the sculptor. In Memphite theology he creates by heart and tongue, thought and speech, rather than by generation or combat, and is therefore described as a craftsman god who creates through language.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: The main source is the Memphite theology on the Shabaka Stone. Ptah conceives in his heart and names with his tongue, and gods and creatures come into being; the text also absorbs the Heliopolitan Ennead into Ptah, claiming Memphis as the site of creation. Its tone is strikingly monolatrous.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Mummiform tight garment, blue skullcap, straight staff and ankh mark him, and he sometimes stands on a pedestal like a crafted object. Greeks identified him with Hephaestus, so Memphis is a city of the fire god in Greek sources. The Apis bull is also connected with him.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: He protects craftsmen and builders, and Memphis was his great priestly centre, with the Apis bulls kept nearby. The Shabaka Stone itself is an eighth-century BC copy of an older text, a key document for Egyptian creation thought, though the date of the original remains debated.

figures.name: 努特
figures.title: 以身躯覆盖大地的天穹女神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 赫利奥波利斯九柱神之一，空气神舒与湿气神特夫努特之女，地神盖布之妻，奥西里斯、伊西斯、赛特、奈芙蒂斯之母。其名常直接写作“天空”，在文本中她既是神格，也是天穹本身。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 她与盖布被父亲舒强行分开，天与地由此分离；因拉的诅咒，她与盖布的子女无法在一年之内出生，托特以骰子赢来五个附日，五神遂得降生。太阳神每夜穿行其体内，晨间自其下体再生，构成埃及的日的循环。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 女身弓覆大地、身布星辰是核心图像；棺椁内壁常绘努特像，死者进入她体内以求再生。她也可作母牛或母猪，出现吞下太阳再将其生出的图像，与“天母”的宇宙功能一致；她的手指与脚趾触地之处，被说成撑起天穹的四角。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 《金字塔文本》《棺椁文本》与《亡灵书》反复使用努特意象，使“进入天母之身”成为丧葬神学的核心结构。帝王谷陵墓的天文穹顶绘有她的星体图像，用以标示时间与再生，而非现代意义上的占星预测。

en.name: Nut
en.title: The sky goddess arching over the earth

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Nut is one of the Heliopolitan Ennead, daughter of Shu and Tefnut, wife of Geb and mother of Osiris, Isis, Seth and Nephthys. Her name is written as the sky itself, so she is both a goddess and the vault of heaven arched above the earth.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Shu separates her from Geb, and sky and earth are divided. Cursed by Re, she cannot give birth on any day of the year, until Thoth wins five extra days at dice and her five children are born. Each night the sun passes through her body and is reborn from her at dawn.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: A female body arched over the earth, spangled with stars, is the core image. Coffin lids carry her figure so that the dead may enter her body for rebirth. She can also appear as a cow or a sow, and images of her swallowing and giving birth to the sun state the same cosmic function.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Pyramid Texts, Coffin Texts and the Book of the Dead return constantly to Nut, making entry into the sky mother a central structure of funerary theology. Astronomical ceilings in the Valley of the Kings show her starry body as a map of time and rebirth, not as astrology in the modern sense.

figures.name: 提亚马特
figures.title: 《埃努玛·埃利什》中的咸海之母

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 巴比伦创世史诗《埃努玛·埃利什》（约公元前二千年后半）中的原初咸水之神，与淡水之神阿普苏结为配偶，生出一代代神祇。她是宇宙生成之前的原初水体，而不是一般意义上的“混沌怪兽”，这一区别常被现代读物抹去。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 阿普苏欲灭诸神而被埃阿所杀；提亚马特在诸神压力下（或说为夫复仇）生出魔怪与十一战将，以金固为统帅。马尔杜克以网、四方之风与洪水迎战，趁她张口时吹风灌入、射箭裂身，以其尸造天地，双眼化为两河之源。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
