sections.text: 海水、咸味、龙形与多首怪兽是常见描述；带角、鳞、翼的“提亚马特龙”多为十九世纪以后的想象，古代圆柱印章上的怪兽图像来源不一，不能直接对号入座。她首先与水体相关，而非固定的画像类型。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 史诗在巴比伦新年节（Akitu）诵读，确立马尔杜克为众神之王与巴比伦的秩序中心，提亚马特因而是“被秩序征服的原初”，并非被简单否定的恶。学界也反对把她读成女性或自然的单一寓言，那属于现代投射。

en.name: Tiamat
en.title: The primeval sea mother of Enuma Elish

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Tiamat is the primeval salt-water deity of Enuma Elish, the Babylonian creation epic of the later second millennium BC. She is paired with Apsu, the fresh water, and together they generate successive generations of gods. She is the primordial water of cosmogony, not a generic chaos monster.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: Apsu is killed by Ea while planning to destroy the gods. Tiamat, pressed by the gods or avenging her husband, produces monsters and eleven champions under Kingu. Marduk meets her with a net, the four winds and a flood, drives the winds into her open mouth, splits her body and makes heaven and earth from it.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Sea, salt water and dragon or multi-headed forms are conventional descriptions. The horned, scaled, winged Tiamat of modern illustration is largely a nineteenth-century invention; monster figures on cylinder seals have various referents and cannot simply be labelled her. Water is her primary identity.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The epic was recited at the Babylonian New Year, establishing Marduk as king of the gods and Babylon as the centre of order. Tiamat is therefore the primordial defeated by order, not simply evil. Scholars also resist reading her as a single allegory of woman or of nature.

figures.name: 阿达帕
figures.title: 拒饮永生之水的埃利都智者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 埃利都的智者与祭司，属 apkallu（七智者）之一，智慧神埃阿之子，职责是为诸神供应面包与鱼。故事见于阿马尔奈文书中的阿卡德语残片及后世抄本，属“智者传说”序列，而非独立的神话史诗。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 他因折断南风之翼而被召至天界；埃阿嘱他勿食勿饮天上所赐之物，因恐那是死亡之食。阿努赐他永生之水与食，他却依嘱拒绝，阿努大笑而遣返；文本在结尾附近残缺，抄本不存结局，故不应代其补写。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 南风之翼、天界之门、面包与鱼是主要标志；他常被列入七智者，与咒术、驱邪和神庙仪式传统相关。图像材料稀少，主要靠文本辨识，也未见明确的独立祭祀或神庙；埃及与亚述的抄本都有发现，说明流传范围颇广。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 该传说与《吉尔伽美什》的永生失落主题相呼应，也常被与《圣经》亚当叙事比较，但二者并无直接承袭证据。因结尾残缺，学界只讨论其“永生失落”的结构与文化功能，不臆测具体结局。

en.name: Adapa
en.title: The sage of Eridu who refused the water of life

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Adapa is a sage and priest of Eridu, one of the apkallu, son of the god Ea, and his duty is to supply bread and fish to the gods. The story survives in Amarna tablets and later copies. It belongs to the sage traditions rather than to a standalone epic.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: He breaks the wing of the south wind and is summoned to heaven. Ea warns him to refuse food and drink offered there, fearing bread and water of death. Anu offers the water and food of life, Adapa refuses as instructed, and Anu laughs and sends him back. The text is fragmentary near the end.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The wing of the south wind, the gate of heaven, bread and fish identify him. He is counted among the seven sages and belongs to the traditions of incantation, exorcism and temple ritual. Images are scarce, so he is identified mainly from texts rather than from cult statues.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The tale echoes the failed quest for immortality in Gilgamesh and is often compared with the Adam story, though no direct dependence can be shown. Because the ending is lost, scholarship discusses the structure of lost immortality without inventing a conclusion. He had no evident independent cult.

figures.name: 苏赫拉布
figures.title: 《列王纪》中被父所杀的少年

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 菲尔多西《列王纪》（约十世纪末至十一世纪初）中的英雄，鲁斯塔姆与突朗公主塔赫米娜之子。母亲在突朗将他抚养成人，鲁斯塔姆只留下一枚护符为凭。他属史诗文学人物，并非琐罗亚斯德教的神祇。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 成年后他率突朗军寻找父亲，与鲁斯塔姆对阵三日；前两日被摔倒后，鲁斯塔姆以“英雄不杀无名之辈”为由放走，第三日凭护符认出对方时已将其刺伤，苏赫拉布死于父亲怀中，鲁斯塔姆痛悔欲绝。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 护符（臂环）、战马与铠甲是主要标志；波斯细密画与史诗插图反复描绘父子角力与垂死相认的场面。其悲剧结构与《列王纪》中其他父子相残的故事并置，共同构成史诗的宿命主题。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 该故事见于《列王纪》较后的增补部分，部分学者归于后人之手，但它早已成为伊朗民族史诗中最著名的悲剧之一。它与“陌生人决斗”母题（如爱尔兰库呼兰与亲子康拉）在类型上相似，却不宜视为同源传播的证据。

en.name: Suhrab
en.title: The young hero killed by his own father

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Suhrab is a hero of the Shahnameh of Firdawsi, composed around the end of the tenth century, son of Rostam and the Turanian princess Tahmina. His mother raises him in Turan with only an armband left by his father as token. He is an epic literary figure, not a Zoroastrian deity.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: As a young commander he seeks his unknown father and meets him in single combat over three days. Twice Rostam throws him and lets him go as a nameless youth; on the third day he recognises the armband only after fatally wounding him. Suhrab dies in the arms of his father.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The armband, horse and armour identify him. Persian miniature painting and epic illustration return repeatedly to the wrestling match and the deathbed recognition. The tragic structure belongs with other father-and-son combats in the Shahnameh, forming its theme of inescapable fate.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The episode belongs to a later, perhaps added portion of the Shahnameh, and some scholars assign it to a continuator, yet it has long been among the most famous tragedies of the Iranian national epic. It resembles stranger-combat motifs elsewhere without implying transmission.

figures.name: 扎哈克
figures.title: 蛇肩暴君与铁匠卡维的起义

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 《列王纪》中的暴君，阿拉伯—伊朗传说中的蛇肩之王，其原型可溯至阿维斯陀中的恶龙阿兹·达哈卡。史诗里他是被恶魔蛊惑的王子，双肩生出黑蛇，须以人脑喂食；他属史诗与传说人物，而非琐罗亚斯德教的神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 他杀父夺位，统治千年，每日以两名青年的脑喂蛇；铁匠卡维以皮围裙为旗聚众反抗，法里东最终以牛头棒将他击败，锁于达马万德山。史诗以“恶的长期统治与终被制服”结构这一段落，并把它写成王朝循环的转折。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 双肩黑蛇、王冠与牛头棒是主要标志；细密画常绘蛇自肩头生出、铁匠皮旗（Derafsh-e Kāviān）飘扬的场面。蛇肩是其最鲜明的辨识特征，也解释了“蛇王”这一通行称呼的由来；蛇每日重新长出，须不断喂食，象征暴政无法满足的胃口。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 故事融合了阿维斯陀的恶龙、波斯与阿拉伯的传说以及菲尔多西时代的政治隐喻，被视为暴政的典型形象。史诗以他为“外来暴君”的代表，后世伊朗民族叙事常引用铁匠卡维的起义；但他本身仍属文学人物，不是被崇拜的神。

en.name: Zahhak
en.title: The snake-shouldered tyrant of the Shahnameh

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Zahhak is the tyrant of the Shahnameh, the snake-shouldered king of Iranian and Arab legend whose ancestry reaches the Avestan dragon Azi Dahaka. In the epic he is a prince corrupted by a demon, with two black snakes growing from his shoulders that must be fed on human brains.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: He kills his father and rules for a thousand years, feeding the snakes with the brains of two young men each day. The blacksmith Kaveh raises a revolt behind his leather apron banner, and Fereydun defeats Zahhak with a bull-headed mace and imprisons him on Mount Damavand.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The twin black snakes, the crown and the bull-headed mace identify him. Miniatures show the snakes sprouting from his shoulders while the leather banner of Kaveh flies above the crowd. The snake shoulders are his unmistakable marker and explain the usual title of snake king.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: The story fuses the Avestan dragon, Persian and Arab legend and the politics of the time of Firdawsi, and became the standing image of tyranny. Later Iranian national narrative often cites Kaveh and his banner. Zahhak is a literary figure, not an object of worship.

figures.name: 胡纳赫普
figures.title: 基切史诗中的猎人与冥界胜者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 胡纳赫普是基切玛雅《波波尔·乌》中的英雄双子之一，与伊什巴兰克为兄弟，母亲是伊什基克。父亲胡恩·胡纳赫普遭冥界诸主杀害后，头颅悬在树上；母亲因这颗头颅的唾液受孕，双子的身世因此连结生死两界。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 双子因打球惊扰西巴尔巴的统治者，循父辈足迹进入冥界，却先派蚊虫探出诸主姓名，识破假座位等圈套。胡纳赫普在蝙蝠屋伸头察看天色而被斩首，兄弟以葫芦暂代头颅，再夺回真头。二人后来主动赴死、变形复生，以表演诱使冥界诸主接受无法逆转的杀戮。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 他的核心标志是吹箭筒、球戏与和兄弟协作的机智，而非单纯武力。古典玛雅图像中的某些青年猎手常被拿来与他比较，但不能把所有斑点青年形象都直接认定为同一人物。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 主要叙事见于殖民早期以拉丁字母记录的基切语《波波尔·乌》，不能视为全体玛雅人的统一教典。结尾双子升天，分别关联日月；基切人的讲述与当代阅读仍不断赋予故事新的意义。

en.name: Hunahpu
en.title: Kʼicheʼ hunter and victor over the underworld

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Hunahpu is one of the Hero Twins in the Kʼicheʼ Maya Popol Wuj, brother of Xbalanque and son of Xquic. Their father, Hun Hunahpu, was killed by the underworld lords. His severed head, hanging in a tree, impregnated Xquic through spittle, linking the twins to an interrupted paternal history.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: Summoned to Xibalba because of their noisy ballplaying, the twins expose traps through reconnaissance and deception. A bat decapitates Hunahpu when he looks outside the Bat House. Xbalanque temporarily replaces his head with a squash and retrieves the original. Later, their staged deaths and resurrection performances persuade the underworld rulers to request a fatal demonstration.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: Blowguns, ballplaying, hunting, and cooperation distinguish Hunahpu more reliably than any single emblem. Scholars compare him with certain youthful hunters in Classic Maya imagery, but the identification is interpretive. A spotted young figure on an ancient vessel should not automatically be treated as a literal portrait of the later Kʼicheʼ character.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: The fullest account survives in the Popol Wuj, written in alphabetic Kʼicheʼ during the early colonial period. Its concluding ascent associates the twins with the sun and moon. This particular narrative is not a universal Maya creed: Kʼicheʼ communities, storytellers, scholars, and contemporary readers maintain distinct relationships with its continuing cultural life.

figures.name: 伊什巴兰克
figures.title: 以计谋破解西巴尔巴的英雄双子

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 伊什巴兰克是基切玛雅《波波尔·乌》中胡纳赫普的兄弟，同为伊什基克所生。兄弟幼年受同父异母的哥哥胡恩·巴茨与胡恩·乔文排挤，后来反用计谋使他们变为猴子；这段家族冲突也解释了猴子与乐师艺人的联系。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 胡纳赫普在蝙蝠屋失去头颅后，伊什巴兰克召集动物取材，以葫芦充作替代，争取夺回真头的机会。双子死后重返世间，化作贫穷艺人，表演焚屋复原与杀生复活。他先杀死再救活兄弟，诱使冥界诸主要求同样待遇，最终拒绝让这些统治者复生，挫败其威权。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 他体现临场应变、变形与对死亡规则的反转，常与胡纳赫普成对讨论。名字的词源及其与古典玛雅人物的对应仍有争议，不宜仅凭现代译名把他固定成统一的豹神或月神。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 《波波尔·乌》在双子故事后讲述人类创造及基切家族历史，英雄冒险因此嵌入群体记忆。双子升天的结尾并不等于整个玛雅地区共享一套日月神谱，地方传统与不同时代的材料需要分别理解。

en.name: Xbalanque
en.title: The Hero Twin who outwits Xibalba

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Xbalanque is Hunahpu’s brother and Xquic’s son in the Kʼicheʼ Maya Popol Wuj. Their older half brothers, Hun Batz and Hun Chouen, mistreat the younger pair. The twins eventually turn these rivals into monkeys, connecting a family dispute with the narrative origins of monkey figures associated with musicians and other artists.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: After Hunahpu loses his head in the Bat House, Xbalanque organizes an animal-assisted substitution that enables its recovery. Following their own deaths, the brothers return as humble performers. Xbalanque kills and revives Hunahpu before the underworld lords, who demand the same treatment. The twins kill those rulers but refuse to restore them to life.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: Xbalanque represents strategic adaptability, transformation, and the overturning of apparently final death. He is best understood alongside his brother rather than through a solitary emblem. His name’s etymology and proposed connections with Classic Maya figures remain debated; modern translations do not establish a universal jaguar deity or a straightforward lunar identity.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: The Popol Wuj places the twins’ adventures before human creation and accounts of Kʼicheʼ ancestral lineages. Their deeds therefore belong to a larger framework of collective history. The final celestial ascent should not be converted into a single solar and lunar theology for every Maya community, ancient or living.

figures.name: 伊什基克
figures.title: 穿越冥界与人间的双子之母

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 伊什基克是基切玛雅《波波尔·乌》中的冥界少女，父亲库丘马基克属于西巴尔巴诸主。她听闻禁树上的奇事，走近胡恩·胡纳赫普的头颅；头颅向她伸出的手掌吐出唾液，使她怀上后来战胜冥界的英雄双子。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 父亲发现她怀孕，命使者取回她的心作为惩罚。伊什基克说服携刀的猫头鹰使者，以树脂制成的假心交差，自己逃到人间。祖母伊什穆卡内起初不肯承认她，要求她从仅有一株玉米的田里收满一网玉米。她祈求帮助，凭玉米须获得丰收，终于证明身份并得到接纳。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 她的故事以手掌、树上头颅、树脂假心和玉米收获为辨识线索。她既是主动拒绝处决的人物，也是父系血脉得以延续的关键，不能仅凭名字与血有关便称作统一的血液女神。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 伊什基克的具体经历属于基切史诗文本，不宜与低地玛雅月亮女神或伊希切尔直接合并。她的逃亡、受试与获得承认，使女性行动和亲属关系成为叙事核心，当代解读也常关注这些层面。

en.name: Xquic
en.title: Mother of the twins between underworld and earth

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Xquic, also written Ixquic, is an underworld maiden in the Kʼicheʼ Maya Popol Wuj. Her father, Cuchumaquic, belongs to Xibalba’s ruling circle. Approaching the forbidden tree, she encounters Hun Hunahpu’s severed head. Its spittle lands in her outstretched hand and causes the conception of the future Hero Twins.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: When her pregnancy is discovered, Xquic’s father orders messengers to bring back her heart. She persuades the owl messengers to substitute a resin heart and escapes. On earth, Xmucane doubts her claim to kinship. Challenged to gather a netful of maize from one plant, Xquic invokes assistance and achieves the abundance required for acceptance.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: The outstretched hand, speaking skull, substitute resin heart, and miraculous maize harvest distinguish her narrative. Xquic acts to avoid execution and secure recognition rather than simply serving as a passive mother. Although her name evokes blood, that association alone does not establish a general Maya goddess governing all blood.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Xquic’s particular biography belongs to the Kʼicheʼ epic and should not be merged automatically with lowland Maya moon goddesses or Ix Chel. Her escape and successful household trial foreground women’s agency, kinship, and contested belonging. These themes continue to inspire contemporary interpretations without exhausting what the narrative means within living Kʼicheʼ communities.

figures.name: 玉米神
figures.title: 低地玛雅王权与生命再生的玉米形象

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 玉米神是研究者对低地玛雅艺术中一组玉米神圣形象的概称，尤其常见于古典时期陶器、石刻与王室装饰。著名类型额头修长、头顶似剃发，表现成熟玉米的形态；其古代姓名、不同形态及与后世故事的关系仍需谨慎辨析。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 一些古典陶器绘有年轻玉米神自龟壳裂口升起，旁有青年神祇协助，常被解释为玉米从大地萌出或死后再生。另一些图像表现他在水域中旅行、更衣或起舞。现代解释常借基切史诗中被杀父亲与双子的故事比较这些场景，但图像并非一部已完整解读的同名传记。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 修长头形、玉米叶饰、珠玉腰带与舞姿是重要线索，龟壳与水域则常构成再生场景。王者也会扮作玉米神，借身体与丰收的联系展现统治正当性，但并非每位舞者都必然代表他。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 玉米在许多玛雅社群中既是食物，也是人与土地关系的根基，但各地礼俗并不相同。古典低地图像与殖民时代基切文本相隔时空，不能直接把玉米神等同胡恩·胡纳赫普，更不能据此替代今日社群自身的解释。

en.name: Maize God
en.title: Lowland Maya maize imagery of kingship and renewal

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Maize God is a scholarly label for related divine maize figures in lowland Maya art, especially Classic-period ceramics, sculpture, and royal imagery. A prominent youthful form has an elongated head and apparently shaven crown resembling a maize ear. Ancient names, distinctions among forms, and relationships with later narratives require careful interpretation rather than automatic equivalence.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: Some painted vessels show a youthful maize deity emerging through a split turtle shell with other young supernatural figures nearby. Scholars often interpret this as germination or resurrection. Other scenes involve watery journeys, dressing, or dancing. Comparisons with the Popol Wuj illuminate possibilities, but the images do not constitute a completely deciphered biography of its slain father.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: An elongated head, maize foliage, jade ornaments, and dance postures provide important visual clues. Turtle shells and watery settings frequently frame scenes of emergence. Rulers could impersonate maize divinity, associating their bodies with agricultural abundance and legitimate authority, although not every elongated head or dancing royal figure depicts the same deity.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Maize remains fundamental to food, personhood, and relationships with land in many Maya communities, whose practices differ considerably. Classic lowland imagery and colonial Kʼicheʼ literature come from different places and periods. Identifying every maize deity with Hun Hunahpu erases those distinctions, as does replacing living communities’ interpretations with a single archaeological reconstruction.

figures.name: 伊察姆纳
figures.title: 尤卡坦传统中的古老创造与知识之神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 伊察姆纳主要见于尤卡坦玛雅殖民时期记载，被描述为古老而尊贵的神，与创造、知识、治病及祭司技艺相联系。研究者也将他与古典和后古典图像中的老年神联系起来，但文字名称和图像身份的对应并非处处确定。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 殖民时期记录者兰达转述，伊察姆纳被认为创立文字与学习传统，祭司在相关仪式中祈求学识和疗愈能力。其他尤卡坦材料把他置于世界起源与神圣祖先的框架中。与英雄双子不同，他没有一部细节连贯、各地一致的冒险史诗；其事迹分散在殖民记述、地方文献及图像研究之中。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 玛雅抄本中的老年神常有大眼、突出鼻梁与少齿面容，学术上常称神Ｄ，并常与伊察姆纳关联。天界鸟类形象也被纳入讨论，但不同年代的鸟神与老神不应一概合并。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 殖民材料经过传教士分类和翻译，其所谓最高神等说法需要结合作者立场阅读。尤卡坦玛雅宗教并非静止神谱，地方祭仪、基督宗教影响和当代文化复兴长期交织，不能把历史描述当作今日共同信条。

en.name: Itzamna
en.title: Ancient creator and patron of knowledge in Yucatan

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Itzamna appears prominently in colonial accounts of Yucatec Maya religion as an ancient, esteemed deity associated with creation, knowledge, healing, and priestly expertise. Scholars connect him with elderly supernatural figures in Classic and Postclassic imagery. Such connections are useful hypotheses, but names and visual identities do not align with equal certainty across every period.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: Diego de Landa’s colonial account credits Itzamna with the invention of writing and learning and describes priestly observances seeking knowledge and healing. Other Yucatec materials situate him among origins and sacred ancestors. Unlike the Hero Twins, he lacks a single continuous adventure cycle: evidence comes from scattered colonial descriptions, local texts, and interpretations of imagery.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: The elderly manuscript figure conventionally called God D often has large eyes, a prominent nose, and a tooth-poor mouth; scholars commonly associate him with Itzamna. Celestial bird forms also enter discussions of his identity. Neither resemblance nor broad association, however, makes every ancient bird deity or elderly god an interchangeable representation.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Missionary classification and translation shaped colonial descriptions, including claims about supreme divinity. These sources need to be read with attention to their authors’ agendas. Yucatec Maya religious life has continued through local ceremonies, Christian encounters, and cultural renewal; a historical account cannot stand as a fixed creed shared by all present-day Maya people.

figures.name: 恰克
figures.title: 执斧降雨的玛雅雷雨之神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 恰克是尤卡坦玛雅雨神的常用名称，相关雷雨神在古典低地文字与图像中也有悠久历史。他既可作为单一神祇出现，也可体现为分掌方位的多位雨神；地域、时代与仪式语境决定其不同称呼和组合方式。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 古典图像常让雷雨神挥动斧具，表现闪电劈击与降水的力量，一些场景涉及打开山石、释放被封藏的玉米。尤卡坦求雨仪式则向雨神献上食物和饮品，并可能由参与者模仿蛙鸣，召唤雨季到来。这些材料呈现农业与降雨的紧密关系，却不能拼成各地共有的单一生平故事。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 长而卷曲的鼻部、突出的獠牙、斧与水流是常见标志，雨神面具常装饰建筑立面。四方雨神可与方位颜色相联，但具体配色和名称随来源变化，不宜套用一张永远固定的表。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 尤卡坦部分社区至今举行恰恰克等求雨礼，其组织方式与神圣称谓由当地传统决定。考古学上的雨神面具与活态仪式互有研究价值，却不意味着今日参与者只是重复古典王室宗教，社区仍有自主变化。

en.name: Chaac
en.title: Maya rain and thunder deity with the lightning axe

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Chaac is the familiar Yucatec name for a rain deity whose related storm forms have a long history in lowland Maya writing and imagery. He may appear individually or as multiple rain beings associated with directions. Names and groupings depend on region, period, and ritual setting rather than a permanently standardized pantheon.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: Classic storm imagery frequently shows an axe-wielding deity expressing lightning and rainfall; some scenes concern opening stone or mountains associated with concealed maize. Yucatec rain petitions offer food and drink, sometimes including participants imitating frogs. Such evidence reveals agricultural relationships with rain, but does not produce one continuous biography shared by every Maya tradition.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: A long curling nose, prominent fangs, axes, and flowing water are common identifying features. Rain-deity masks also appear on architectural facades. Directional rain beings may be associated with particular colors, but their precise names and arrangements vary between sources; a modern fixed chart can conceal differences important to individual communities.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Some Yucatec communities continue rain ceremonies often called chaʼ chaak, with locally maintained responsibilities, offerings, and sacred names. Archaeological rain masks and living ceremonies can illuminate related questions without being identical phenomena. Present-day participants are not simply reenacting Classic royal religion: communities retain the authority to adapt and interpret their practices.

figures.name: 羽蛇神
figures.title: 纳瓦传统中联结风、知识与人类起源的神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 羽蛇神的纳瓦语名为魁札尔科阿特尔，意为珍羽之蛇，在墨西加及其他纳瓦传统中地位重要。他与风神埃埃卡特尔密切相连，也关联祭司知识与历法；古代中美洲羽蛇图像的分布更广，不能全部视作墨西加同一神祇。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《太阳传说》记载，羽蛇神下到米克特兰索取前代人类的骨头，完成吹响无孔海螺的考验，却又遭冥王设局，跌落陷坑并摔碎骨骸。他仍带着碎骨返回，由基拉斯特利磨碎，再以自己的血参与造人。另一些纳瓦材料讲述托兰君主祭司的出走，需与神祇的创造故事区分。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 覆有珍羽的蛇是基本标志；作为风神时，他常佩突出的喙形口罩与风之珠胸饰。金星和晨星也与其传统有关，但各形态并非处处相同，不能仅凭羽饰或蛇形就作确定识别。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 主要叙事来自殖民早期保存的纳瓦语及西班牙语材料，包含不同城市的记忆。把科尔特斯来临说成墨西加人普遍认定神明归返，是过度简化且有争议的说法；今日纳瓦社群也不只是古帝国的遗留。

en.name: Quetzalcoatl
en.title: Nahua deity of wind, knowledge, and human origins

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Quetzalcoatl, whose Nahuatl name means Precious-Feathered Serpent, holds an important place in Mexica and other Nahua traditions. Closely associated with the wind deity Ehecatl, he also concerns priestly knowledge and calendrical learning. Feathered-serpent imagery extends much further across Mesoamerica, however, and cannot all be assigned to an identical Mexica deity.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: In the Legend of the Suns, Quetzalcoatl seeks earlier humanity’s bones in Mictlan. He sounds a seemingly impossible conch trumpet, then falls into a trap that breaks the bones. Recovering them, he brings them to Quilaztli for grinding and contributes his blood to human creation. Accounts of Tollan’s departing priest-ruler form a related but distinct narrative strand.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: A serpent covered in precious feathers provides the central image. As Ehecatl, he commonly wears a projecting beak-like mouth mask and a wind-jewel pectoral. Venus and the morning star also belong to his wider associations, but these aspects are not interchangeable in every source, and feathers alone are insufficient identification.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Early colonial Nahuatl and Spanish sources preserve stories shaped by different cities and political memories. The claim that Mexica people universally welcomed Cortes as a returning Quetzalcoatl is contested and misleadingly simple. Living Nahua communities likewise cannot be reduced to survivals of an imperial religion or to colonial explanations of the conquest.

figures.name: 特斯卡特利波卡
figures.title: 以冒烟之镜显现的命运与统治之神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 特斯卡特利波卡的纳瓦语名意为冒烟之镜，是墨西加与其他纳瓦传统中掌握命运、冲突和统治权的重要神。他可赐予财富，也可突然撤回恩惠，关联夜色、巫术与美洲豹；某些创世材料又把他列入不同颜色的神圣兄弟。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 关于托兰的殖民时期叙事中，他以镜子使祭司君主魁札尔科阿特尔惊见自己的容貌，又借醉酒等事件促成其失序和离去。在五太阳传统的某些版本里，两神反复争夺世界秩序，一方推翻另一方。另有创世故事让他们合作制服原初大地怪物，显示对立与协作并存。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 冒烟黑曜石镜可出现在头部或代替一只脚，脸上的深色横带也是常见线索。他与美洲豹形态特佩约洛特尔有关；这些形象强调不可预测的临在，不宜将他简单归为纯粹邪神。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》等保存了向他祈祷的修辞和托什卡特尔节记载，包括代表神祇的青年被献祭。材料同时反映纳瓦知识者与殖民记录环境，理解其残酷仪式不能脱离当时的王权、义务与宇宙观。

en.name: Tezcatlipoca
en.title: Lord of the Smoking Mirror, sovereignty, and reversal

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Tezcatlipoca means Smoking Mirror in Nahuatl. Important in Mexica and other Nahua traditions, he governs uncertain fortune, conflict, and sovereign power. He can bestow prosperity and abruptly remove it, and is associated with night, sorcery, and jaguars. Some creation accounts also place him among a group of differently colored divine brothers.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: Colonial narratives concerning Tollan describe him using a mirror to disturb the priest-ruler Quetzalcoatl and helping precipitate drunkenness, disorder, and departure. In some Five Suns accounts, the two deities repeatedly overthrow one another’s cosmic regimes. Other creation traditions have them cooperate against a primordial earth monster, making their relationship more complex than permanent moral opposition.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: A smoking obsidian mirror may appear at his head or replace a missing foot. Dark horizontal facial bands offer another common clue. His associations include the jaguar figure Tepeyollotl. Such imagery expresses elusive, unpredictable power; interpreting him simply as an evil counterpart to a benevolent Quetzalcoatl imposes an inappropriate binary.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: The Florentine Codex and related sources preserve elaborate prayers and accounts of Toxcatl, when a young divine representative was sacrificed. These records reflect both Nahua expertise and colonial circumstances of documentation. Their violent rites require historical explanation through sovereignty, obligation, and cosmology, rather than sensationalism or assumptions about all present-day Nahua people.

figures.name: 维齐洛波奇特利
figures.title: 引领墨西加迁徙的蜂鸟战神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 维齐洛波奇特利的纳瓦语名通常译作左方或南方的蜂鸟，是墨西加人的重要守护神，与战争、太阳力量及族群迁徙相连。他在特诺奇蒂特兰大神庙与雨神特拉洛克各有神殿，体现征战扩张和农业供养在国家仪式中的并置。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 据《佛罗伦萨手抄本》的科阿特佩克故事，科阿特利库埃扫地时把羽球藏在胸前而怀孕，女儿科约尔绍基与众多兄长因而要杀她。维齐洛波奇特利出生即全副武装，挥动火蛇击败来敌，将姐姐斩首并使其躯体滚下山坡。迁徙叙事另记他通过神谕指导墨西加人寻找定居之地。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 蜂鸟羽饰、蓝色面部装饰及火蛇武器是常见线索，盾牌与投矛器强调战士身份。太阳联想十分重要，但他并非所有纳瓦材料中唯一的太阳神，不能因此抹去托纳蒂乌等神的区别。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 大神庙南侧的科约尔绍基巨石与相关祭仪，使出生神话和首都建筑相互呼应。征服后的记录保留不同版本，也带有殖民立场；现代墨西哥的国家象征、艺术再现与当代纳瓦实践应分别理解。

en.name: Huitzilopochtli
en.title: Hummingbird war patron of the Mexica migration

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Huitzilopochtli’s Nahuatl name is commonly rendered Hummingbird of the Left or South. A principal Mexica patron, he connects warfare, solar power, and collective migration. At Tenochtitlan’s Templo Mayor, his sanctuary stood beside Tlaloc’s, placing military expansion and agricultural sustenance together within the ceremonial architecture of the imperial capital and its political order.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: In the Florentine Codex account, Coatlicue conceives after gathering a feather ball while sweeping at Coatepec. Coyolxauhqui and her brothers plan to kill her. Huitzilopochtli emerges armed, defeats the attackers with a fire-serpent weapon, and dismembers his sister, whose body falls down the mountain. Separate migration narratives describe his oracular guidance toward a new Mexica homeland.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: Hummingbird feathers, blue facial decoration, shields, dart-throwers, and the fire serpent Xiuhcoatl help identify him. These features emphasize his martial character and solar associations. He should not therefore replace every Nahua sun deity: Tonatiuh and other solar figures maintain distinct identities and roles within the diverse surviving textual and visual sources.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: The Coyolxauhqui monument below the southern Templo Mayor stairway linked the birth narrative with architecture and ritual. Postconquest records preserve versions shaped by colonial circumstances. Modern Mexican national imagery, artistic reinterpretation, and living Nahua practices are related but distinct contexts; none provides a transparent substitute for the religious life of imperial Tenochtitlan.

figures.name: 特拉洛克
figures.title: 兼赐甘霖、冰雹与山中丰饶的雨神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 特拉洛克是墨西加及其他纳瓦群体的重要雨神，与山岳、水源、作物及危险天气相连。他身边有被称为特拉洛克众的雨水神灵，居所特拉洛坎被描述为丰饶之地。相似雨神形象早见于中部墨西哥，但名称与身份不能跨时代机械套用。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 纳瓦记述把特拉洛坎说成持续丰饶的所在，溺水者和遭某些水相关病症夺去生命的人可前往那里，而不是按一般亡者路径进入米克特兰。关于雨神诸灵的材料还描述不同容器中的雨，分别带来滋养、冰雹或损害。墨西加国家祭仪向山岳和水源献祭，力求获得适时雨水。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 环形眼部、卷曲上唇、獠牙与水罐是常见标志，闪电器具也可出现。山岳既蓄藏水又孕育作物，因此不是普通背景；相似的面具特征仍须结合出土年代和地点来判断。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 大神庙北侧神殿及墨西哥盆地山岳祭场提供考古背景，殖民文献还记有儿童祭献。今日部分纳瓦地区延续山水与求雨礼俗，但不能把所有安置十字架或登山的仪式都直接认作古代祭祀原样延续。

en.name: Tlaloc
en.title: Rain lord of mountains, abundance, and dangerous weather

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Tlaloc is an important rain deity among Mexica and other Nahua peoples, associated with mountains, water sources, crops, and destructive weather. Rain beings called Tlaloque accompany him, and Tlalocan is described as an abundant domain. Related imagery is older than the Mexica, but names and identities should not be projected unchanged across centuries.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: Nahua accounts describe Tlalocan as a perpetually productive destination for people who drown or die from certain water-associated conditions, rather than following the usual route to Mictlan. Accounts of rain beings describe containers holding nourishing or damaging rains, including hail. Mexica ceremonies addressed mountain and water powers to obtain rainfall at the necessary agricultural moments.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: Ringed eyes, a curled upper lip, fangs, water vessels, and sometimes lightning implements form a familiar visual vocabulary. Mountains contain water and agricultural abundance rather than merely providing scenery. Similar facial features on earlier monuments still require contextual identification through their archaeological date and location, not recognition by appearance alone.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: The northern Templo Mayor shrine and mountain offering sites in the Basin of Mexico provide archaeological contexts, while colonial sources describe ceremonies including child sacrifice. Some living Nahua traditions maintain mountain and rain relationships. Their Christian elements and local histories mean that present ceremonies cannot simply be labeled unchanged replicas of imperial practice.

figures.name: 科阿特利库埃
figures.title: 蛇裙母亲与大地生命循环的可怖形象

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 科阿特利库埃的纳瓦语名意为穿蛇裙者，在墨西加叙事中是维齐洛波奇特利、科约尔绍基及众多星辰兄弟的母亲。她与大地、死亡和生育联系密切，但相关母神名称及巨型雕像的身份并非始终明确，不能把所有大地神都归为她。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 她在科阿特佩克扫地时拾得一团羽毛，藏入胸前后羽球消失，自己却已怀孕。女儿科约尔绍基认为这是家族羞辱，召集兄弟准备杀母。腹中的维齐洛波奇特利不断安慰她，随后持火蛇武器出生并击败来敌。故事把看似脆弱的母体置于神圣战争的起点，而非让母亲亲自征服众子女。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 墨西哥城出土的著名巨像通常称为科阿特利库埃，具有交缠蛇裙、手心项链与双蛇组成的头部。形象把生育和吞噬并置，不过这座无铭文巨像的具体神名与礼仪身份仍有讨论。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 巨像于一七九〇年被重新发现，后来成为博物馆研究和墨西哥艺术的重要对象。殖民时期文字与石雕提供不同证据，现代女性主义及奇卡纳创作又有新解释；这些再诠释不应冒充古代一致的原始教义。

en.name: Coatlicue
en.title: Serpent-skirted mother of birth, earth, and death

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Coatlicue means She of the Serpent Skirt in Nahuatl. Mexica narratives identify her as mother of Huitzilopochtli, Coyolxauhqui, and numerous stellar brothers. She has strong associations with earth, birth, and death. Related mother figures and monumental sculptures do not always have securely established identities, however; all earth divinities should not be collapsed into her.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: While sweeping at Coatepec, Coatlicue gathers a ball of feathers and places it against her breast. The feathers disappear, and she becomes pregnant. Coyolxauhqui calls this disgraceful and rallies her brothers to kill their mother. Huitzilopochtli reassures Coatlicue from the womb, then emerges armed with a fire serpent and defeats the attackers before their plan succeeds.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: The monumental Mexico City sculpture conventionally called Coatlicue wears an intertwined serpent skirt and a necklace incorporating hands and hearts; two serpents form its head. Its imagery brings generation together with consumption and death. Because the monument carries no identifying name inscription, its precise divine and ceremonial identity remains a matter of scholarly discussion.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Rediscovered in 1790, the great sculpture became central to museum interpretation and Mexican art. Colonial narratives and stone monuments offer different kinds of evidence. Modern feminist and Chicana artists have developed further meanings around Coatlicue; these powerful reinterpretations should be acknowledged on their own terms rather than presented as an unchanged ancient doctrine.

figures.name: 米克特兰特库特利
figures.title: 统治亡者去处米克特兰的骸骨之主

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 米克特兰特库特利的纳瓦语名意为米克特兰之主，与女性伙伴米克特卡西瓦特尔共同关联亡者领域。墨西加材料中，许多自然死亡者须前往此处，另有死法通向其他归宿；它不是按照生前善恶判决而设立的基督宗教式地狱。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 《太阳传说》中，羽蛇神来到米克特兰索取前代人骨，冥王要求他吹响并绕行一支没有孔洞的海螺。来客借虫与蜂的帮助完成任务后，冥王仍反悔，让部属制造陷坑阻拦。羽蛇神跌落，骨头被惊鸟啄散，却仍收集碎骨离去；这一失败的阻挠成为现世人类起源故事的环节。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 骷髅面孔、外露骨骼、爪状手足及与尸体相关的装饰有助辨识。并非所有骸骨人物都是冥王本人；判断雕像或抄本角色，还需结合姿势、配偶、地点与周围图像的关系。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 纳瓦文献描述亡者经历漫长旅程，有些版本提及四年及多重险境，但次序和细节并不完全统一。今日亡灵节受原住民与天主教等多种传统塑造，不能简单说成这位冥王的古代节庆直接延续。

en.name: Mictlantecuhtli
en.title: Skeletal lord of the destination of the dead

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Mictlantecuhtli means Lord of Mictlan in Nahuatl. He is associated with the realm of the dead alongside a female counterpart, Mictecacihuatl. Mexica sources send many who die ordinary deaths there, while other deaths lead elsewhere. Mictlan is not a Christian-style hell assigned as punishment according to a person’s moral behavior.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: In the Legend of the Suns, Quetzalcoatl requests ancestral bones from Mictlan. Its lord demands that he sound a conch without holes and circle with it. Insects help complete the task, but Mictlantecuhtli reneges and orders a pit prepared. Quetzalcoatl falls, the bones break, and he nevertheless retrieves their fragments for the creation of humanity.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: A skull face, exposed bones, claw-like extremities, and bodily or funerary ornaments help identify the deity. These features alone are not conclusive, since many beings can appear skeletal. Reading a sculpture or manuscript image also requires attention to pose, accompanying figures, archaeological location, and the relationships established by the surrounding scene.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Nahua sources describe lengthy journeys of the dead, sometimes mentioning four years and successive dangers, but details and sequences vary. Today’s Day of the Dead reflects Indigenous, Catholic, and other historical developments. Presenting it simply as an unchanged festival of Mictlantecuhtli obscures living communities’ practices and the complexity of their histories.

figures.name: 因蒂
figures.title: 印加王朝宣称血统所出的太阳神

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 因蒂是克丘亚语中的太阳，也是印加国家祭祀的核心神圣存在。印加君主以太阳后裔的身份强化统治，库斯科科里坎查神殿保存重要太阳圣物与礼仪。帝国内各地同时敬奉山岳、祖先和地方圣地，太阳崇拜并未抹去所有其他传统。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 在加尔西拉索记下的一种王朝起源说中，太阳怜悯缺乏教化的人群，把曼科卡帕克与玛玛奥克略送到地上，命二人寻找建立中心之地。这个叙事将新秩序解释为太阳的恩赐。其他殖民记录还描述帕查库特克强化太阳祭祀与国家建筑，体现王朝祖先故事和帝国制度之间的互动。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 金色圆盘、太阳光芒和王朝礼器常被用来表现因蒂，黄金也在殖民材料中被比作太阳的汗。太阳图案未必都是神像；需要区分历史祭器、现代国徽以及为旅游节庆新制的装饰。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 殖民统治毁坏或改造太阳神殿，但太阳与农时的关系仍进入不同安第斯实践。库斯科今日大型太阳节自一九四四年起以现代形式重建，结合史料、表演和地方认同，并非从帝国时代未经中断的同一仪式。

en.name: Inti
en.title: Solar source of Inca dynastic descent

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Inti is the Quechua word for the sun and a central sacred presence in Inca state religion. Rulers claimed solar descent to support their authority, while Cusco’s Qorikancha housed important solar objects and ceremonies. Across the empire, communities also honored mountains, ancestors, and local sacred places; imperial sun worship never erased every other tradition.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: In an origin account recorded by Garcilaso de la Vega, the Sun pities people portrayed as lacking civilization and sends Manco Capac and Mama Ocllo to establish a center of ordered life. Other colonial accounts describe Pachacuti strengthening solar worship and state institutions. Together these materials connect dynastic ancestry with changing imperial political and ceremonial arrangements.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: Golden disks, radiating sunlight, and royal ceremonial objects commonly represent Inti. Colonial descriptions also compare gold with the sun’s sweat. Not every solar design is a divine portrait, however. Historical cult objects, modern national emblems, and newly made festival decorations belong to different contexts and should be identified rather than treated interchangeably.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Colonial rule destroyed or transformed solar sanctuaries, while relationships between sunlight, seasons, and farming continued in diverse Andean practices. Cusco’s large public Inti Raymi was reconstructed in its modern form beginning in 1944. It combines historical interpretation, performance, and local identity rather than constituting an entirely uninterrupted ceremony inherited unchanged from the empire.

figures.name: 维拉科查
figures.title: 殖民记录中的安第斯创造者与行旅者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 维拉科查在多种殖民时代安第斯记述中是创造者，名称也写作维拉科恰或维拉科察，其完整称号和身份因来源而异。他与世界整理、人群起源及巡行相关，但不能将其直接理解为所有安第斯社群自古一致信奉的唯一至高神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 部分记述说他先创造一代人，因其行为不当而以洪水毁灭，随后在的的喀喀湖一带重建秩序，使日月出现，并安排不同人群从各自的起源地点出世。他与助手沿安第斯行旅，教导或惩罚遇到的群体，最后走向海岸离去。创造次序、助手姓名及旅程在各作者笔下并不相同。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 行旅者、创造者与湖区起源是较可靠的叙事线索。蒂瓦纳库太阳门持杖中央像常被现代读物称作维拉科查，但遗址早于印加帝国，图像没有留下可证实这个名字的直接铭文。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 贝坦索斯、谢萨和莫利纳等记录者保存不同版本，也可能受基督宗教创造观和翻译选择影响。材料须与当地地景及社群历史对读，不能把殖民作者使用的创造者称谓视为各地原住民完全相同的神学。

en.name: Viracocha
en.title: Andean creator and traveler in colonial accounts

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Viracocha appears as a creator in several colonial accounts of the Andes. Spellings, expanded titles, and descriptions vary among sources. Associated with ordering the world, human origins, and journeys, this figure should not be treated automatically as the single supreme deity worshipped identically by all Andean communities since remote antiquity.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: Some accounts describe an initial humanity destroyed by a flood, followed by a reordering near Lake Titicaca. Viracocha brings forth celestial bodies and arranges for peoples to emerge from their particular places of origin. Traveling with assistants, he instructs or punishes communities before departing toward the coast. Authors differ concerning the sequence, companions, and details of departure.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: Creation, travel, and associations with the Titicaca region provide firmer narrative clues than any universal visual emblem. The central staff-bearing figure on Tiwanaku’s Gateway of the Sun is often called Viracocha in modern publications. Tiwanaku predates the Inca Empire, however, and no direct naming inscription confirms that identification for the monument.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Betanzos, Cieza de Leon, Molina, and other writers preserve divergent versions shaped partly by translation and Christian assumptions about creation. Their texts require comparison with landscapes and community histories. A colonial author’s use of a creator category does not demonstrate that Indigenous peoples everywhere held an identical theology or understood that category in the same way.

figures.name: 帕查玛玛
figures.title: 安第斯社群持续交往的大地母亲

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 帕查玛玛常译为大地母亲，其中帕查也包含世界、时空与所处秩序等意义。她属于印加历史与更广泛的克丘亚、艾马拉及其他安第斯实践，不能只算某位帝王创立的国家神；不同社群把她与土地、食物和地方关系相联系。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 她没有一部各地一致的生平史诗，相关讲述常围绕土地给予、索取与人如何回应展开。部分社群在八月向大地献食，把饮品的最初一份洒在地上，说明收成不是可以无偿占有的礼物。耕作、出行或采掘也可能伴随请求与致谢；若忽视关系，大地可被讲述为饥饿或具有危险力量。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 田土、农作物、食物与饮品的分享比固定人形神像更能提示她的关系网络。现代绘画常将她画成山形母亲，但这不是所有安第斯社群共享的古老标准像，更不能代替当地解释。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 当代献礼、家庭实践与地方节庆体现她的活态意义，也可能与圣母崇敬并存。她在环保话语和国家政治中又获得新位置，但把她只当作全球通用的生态女神，会掩盖社群土地权、历史和礼仪差异。

en.name: Pachamama
en.title: Earth Mother in continuing Andean relationships

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Pachamama is often translated as Earth Mother, although pacha also encompasses world, time, space, and situated order. Her relationships belong to Inca history and wider Quechua, Aymara, and other Andean practices. She is not simply a state deity invented by an emperor: communities understand her through particular lands, foods, obligations, and local histories.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: There is no universally shared biography. Stories and practices instead concern land giving, receiving, and requiring a response. Some communities offer food in August and pour an initial share of drink onto the ground. Farming, travel, or extraction may involve requests and thanks. Neglecting these relationships can be described as leaving the earth hungry or dangerously demanding.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: Cultivated soil, crops, and shared food or drink often communicate her relationships more effectively than a fixed anthropomorphic image. Modern paintings may depict a mountain-shaped mother, but that composition is not an ancient universal icon for every Andean community. Local explanations remain essential when interpreting offerings, images, or accounts of sacred landscapes.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Household offerings, community celebrations, and relationships with Marian devotion demonstrate continuing, changing religious life. Environmental activism and state politics have given Pachamama additional public roles. Reducing her to a globally interchangeable ecological goddess, however, can obscure community land rights, colonial histories, and differences in how particular people maintain obligations to the earth.

figures.name: 玛玛基利亚
figures.title: 印加礼仪中的月亮母亲与历法之光

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 玛玛基利亚的克丘亚语名常解释为月亮母亲，也写作玛玛基亚。在若干印加王朝记述中，她是太阳的配偶或女性对应者，与王室女性及月相历法有关；不同作者提供的神圣亲属关系不完全一致，不应据此构造固定不变的全安第斯家谱。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 殖民记述把月食呈现为月亮生病或遭到攻击的危险时刻，人们呼喊、击响器物，部分记载还说催促狗吠，希望它们的叫声帮助月亮恢复。人们担心月亮若死去会坠落并危及世界。相比具有完整冒险的英雄，她的叙事更多通过异常天象及人群的仪式性回应展现出来。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 月盘、月相与银是常见辨识线索，殖民文献把银比作月亮的泪，和太阳的黄金形成对照。但任何银器都不必然属于她，现代带女性面孔的月亮图也不能直接充当古代祭像证据。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 科里坎查相关记述把月亮祭祀置于库斯科王室空间，地方农时知识则有更广泛且多样的来源。今日安第斯人对月相的观察仍可影响生产与生活，但不能将所有月亮习俗都追溯成同一套帝国月神崇拜。

en.name: Mama Quilla
en.title: Mother Moon of Inca ceremony and calendrical light

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Mama Quilla, also written Mama Killa, is commonly understood as Mother Moon in Quechua. Several accounts of Inca dynastic religion describe her as the Sun’s spouse or female counterpart, connected with royal women and lunar reckoning. Authors differ over divine relationships, so their descriptions do not establish a fixed family tree shared throughout the Andes.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: Colonial accounts portray lunar eclipses as dangerous episodes in which the moon is sick or under attack. People shout and strike instruments; some descriptions include encouraging dogs to howl in hopes of helping her recover. They fear that a dying moon could fall and endanger the world. Narrative action therefore centers on celestial crisis and collective ritual response.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: The lunar disk, changing phases, and silver provide common associations. Colonial writers compare silver with the moon’s tears, contrasting it with solar gold. This does not make every silver object a cult possession of Mama Quilla, nor does a modern moon with a woman’s face supply direct evidence for an ancient statue.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Descriptions of the Qorikancha place lunar observances within Cusco’s royal ceremonial setting. Local agricultural knowledge has wider and more varied histories. Attention to moon phases continues to influence work and everyday life in some Andean communities, but these practices should not all be traced to one uniform system of imperial lunar worship.

figures.name: 曼科·卡帕克
figures.title: 库斯科王室祖源中的奠基者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 曼科·卡帕克是印加王室起源叙事中的奠基人物，常被称为首位统治者。他在不同殖民时期记录中的亲缘、同伴与出发地点并不相同。传统讲述为库斯科的政治中心赋予神圣来历，不能直接当作已经考证无误的个人传记。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 印卡·加西拉索保存的版本让太阳派曼科与玛玛·奥克略携金杖前行，在杖能沉入之处定居并教导人群生活。另一些材料则把曼科放进阿亚尔兄弟姐妹的迁行：祖先从帕卡里坦普相关起源地出发，经历冲突、变化和石化，最终确立库斯科。两组叙事不能简单拼成同一趟旅程。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 金杖、太阳祖源与库斯科是常见关联。后世图像中的王冠、耳饰和王权标志，需要联系殖民时代绘画和现代公共纪念的历史，而非全部视作远古人物的真实肖像。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 王室祖源既连接神圣地景，也关系到统治合法性与群体记忆。殖民作者、地方讲述者和现代国家叙事各有选择；当代安第斯社群并不只有一种印加身份，更不能被假定仍保留完全不变的帝国制度。

en.name: Manco Capac
en.title: Founding ancestor in traditions of Cusco

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Manco Capac is a founding figure in accounts of Inca royal ancestry, commonly presented as an earliest ruler. Colonial sources differ over his companions, family, and point of departure. These narratives give sacred authority to Cusco; they are not independently verified modern biographies.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In Inca Garcilaso’s account, the Sun sends Manco and Mama Ocllo with a golden staff that will sink at the place for settlement. Other sources place Manco among the Ayar siblings leaving a place of emergence, facing conflict and transformations before establishing Cusco. The two narrative groups should not be silently fused into one journey.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: The golden staff, solar ancestry, and Cusco commonly identify him. Crowns, ear ornaments, and royal insignia in later images belong to particular histories of colonial painting and modern commemoration, not a surviving photographic likeness of an ancient founder.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Royal ancestry joins sacred landscape with legitimacy and collective memory. Colonial writers, local narrators, and modern national accounts emphasize different elements. Contemporary Andean communities have varied identities and practices; they cannot be assumed to preserve one unchanged imperial social order.

figures.name: 玛玛·奥克略
figures.title: 起源叙事中的女性祖先与文化传授者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 玛玛·奥克略是印加祖源叙事的重要女性人物，常与曼科·卡帕克共同出现。在加西拉索保存的太阳后裔版本中，她参与确立库斯科并传授生活技艺。她在其他祖先迁行版本中的位置，须依具体文本辨认，不能假定所有同名或近名人物完全相同。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 在金杖寻地的故事里，玛玛与曼科离开起源地点，向人群传授耕作、纺织及组织家庭生活的知识。叙述常按性别划分教导职责，反映王室起源故事及记录者对于社会秩序的理解。它并不证明实际历史上的全部知识，都由一对祖先在某一日首次发明或传授。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 纺织、女性祖源与太阳关系是常见的阅读线索。布匹在安第斯社会中关乎身份、交换、礼仪与劳动，不能只视为衣服；后世绘画的服装也须放回创作年代解释。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 将她只当作男性建城者的陪衬，会忽略女性祖先在王室血统和文化记忆中的作用；把故事直接称为现代性别平等宣言，也会遮蔽其历史结构。比较不同编年史，可以看见女性行动、亲缘与统治权威如何被重新安排。

en.name: Mama Ocllo
en.title: Female ancestor and teacher in Inca origin narratives

sections.title: Identity and origins
sections.text: Mama Ocllo is an important female figure in Inca origin accounts, commonly paired with Manco Capac. In Garcilaso’s solar ancestry narrative she helps establish Cusco and teaches skills of life. Her position in other ancestral migrations requires attention to each particular text.

sections.title: Key narratives
sections.text: In the golden staff account, she and Manco travel from their place of origin and instruct people in cultivation, textile work, and household organization. Gendered teaching roles reflect a narrative vision of social order. They do not prove that all practical knowledge was historically invented or introduced by one ancestral couple on a single occasion.

sections.title: Symbols and attributes
sections.text: Textile work, female ancestry, and solar relationships are common interpretive clues. Andean cloth concerns status, exchange, ritual, and labor as well as dress. Costumes in later paintings also require interpretation within the period when those images were produced.

sections.title: Tradition and context
sections.text: Reducing Mama Ocllo to a male founder’s companion misses female ancestry within royal legitimacy and memory. Turning her story into a straightforward modern equality manifesto is equally anachronistic. Comparing chronicles reveals how women’s actions, kinship, and authority were differently arranged by narrators.

figures.name: 奥洛杜马雷
figures.title: 约鲁巴传统中的至高创造者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 奥洛杜马雷是约鲁巴宗教中居于最高位置的创造者，与奥洛伦等称谓的关系依地区和解释而异。他并非希腊式神王，通常不以鲜明的人形冒险出现，而被理解为生命、宇宙秩序与效力阿谢的根本来源。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 一些伊费创世版本说，奥洛杜马雷把建立陆地的任务交给奥巴塔拉；任务受阻后，奥杜杜瓦完成撒土等工作。另一些讲述则分配不同职责。塑造人的形体与赋予生命也常被区分：奥里沙负责塑形，最终生命来自至高者，不能把某一版本当成唯一经典。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 辨识重点不是固定武器或雕像，而是天空、创造和阿谢所指的实现力量。约鲁巴赞词与祈语比统一肖像更重要，不能套用其他文化中雷神或太阳神的外形。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 相关观念流传于尼日利亚西南部、贝宁及大西洋离散传统。日常宗教生活往往更直接面向奥里沙、祖先和占卜；至高者较少拥有专属形象，并不意味着其地位无关紧要。

en.name: Olodumare
en.title: Supreme creator in Yoruba traditions

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Olodumare occupies the highest position in Yoruba religious thought. Relationships between this name and titles such as Olorun vary across communities and interpretations. Rather than an adventurous king with a stable human appearance, Olodumare is understood as the ultimate source of life, order, and enabling power.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: In some Ile-Ife creation accounts, Olodumare commissions Obatala to establish dry land, while Oduduwa completes important tasks after an interruption. Other tellings distribute these responsibilities differently. Human shaping and animation may also be separated: an orisha forms bodies, but the supreme being supplies life itself.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: Recognition depends less on a standard statue or weapon than on references to the sky, creation, and ase, the power through which things become effective. Praise language and prayer matter more than a universal portrait. Imported thunder-god or solar imagery can therefore be misleading.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: These understandings circulate in southwestern Nigeria, Benin, and Atlantic diaspora traditions. Everyday religious practice often addresses orishas, ancestors, and divination more directly. The relative scarcity of dedicated images or shrines should not be mistaken for insignificance, nor should distinct diaspora interpretations be treated as identical.

figures.name: 奥巴塔拉
figures.title: 塑造人身的白衣奥里沙

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 奥巴塔拉是约鲁巴传统中与人身塑造、洁净和沉静权威相连的奥里沙，在伊费及其他地方拥有不同称号与地方形态。他常被表现为年长的白衣者，但其身份不能简单缩成所有地区完全一致的男性形象。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 广为传播的一类故事说，他受命用泥塑造人身，却因饮棕榈酒而失去专注，做出了身体各异的人。醒悟后，他承担保护这些人的责任，并拒绝再饮酒。故事有地方差异，表达的是神圣照护的义务，不应借此贬低残障者或把身体差异视为道德过错。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 白布、白色珠饰与清凉沉静的气质是常见标识，杖等物件则依地方而异。白色既关乎洁净也关乎克制，与尚戈的雷霆、奥贡的铁器形成鲜明叙事对照。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 奥巴塔拉崇敬见于约鲁巴地区，也在美洲发展出奥巴塔拉、奥沙拉等不同传统。地方名号、性别表现与禁忌并非处处相同，应由具体共同体的解释说明，不能把离散实践倒写成单一起源。

en.name: Obatala
en.title: White-robed orisha who shapes human bodies

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Obatala is associated with forming human bodies, purity, and composed authority in Yoruba traditions. Ile-Ife and other communities preserve different titles and local manifestations. Although often represented as an elderly figure dressed in white, Obatala should not be reduced to one universally male image everywhere.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: A widely circulated account describes Obatala shaping people from clay after drinking palm wine, producing bodies with varied characteristics. On recognizing what happened, Obatala accepts responsibility for their protection and renounces alcohol. Versions differ, and the narrative should not be used to stigmatize disability or assign moral blame.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: White cloth, white beads, and a cool, restrained bearing are familiar identifying features, while staffs and other objects vary locally. Whiteness conveys purity and composure rather than a modern racial category. This imagery contrasts narratively with Shango’s thunder and the force of Ogun’s iron.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Devotion to Obatala extends across Yoruba communities and into distinct American traditions, including those using the name Oxala. Local titles, gendered manifestations, and observances are not interchangeable. Explanations should remain grounded in particular communities rather than projecting one diaspora arrangement backward as a universal original.

figures.name: 奥贡
figures.title: 铁器、道路与危险技艺的奥里沙

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 奥贡是约鲁巴传统中掌管铁器、锻造、狩猎和战争的奥里沙，也与使用金属工具的劳动者相连。他的力量既能开辟道路、支持耕作，也能造成伤亡；这种创造与毁坏并存的关系，比单称战神更能说明其身份。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 一类故事描写众奥里沙被茂密灌木阻挡，奥贡用铁器劈开通路，因此确立开路者的地位。有关伊雷的另一类传说说，他归来时误解居民的仪式性沉默，暴怒伤人，随后悔恨并隐入地下。细节与结局有异，不能拼成一部统一生平。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 铁刀、锄、锤和其他金属工具是核心标识，兼指生产与暴力的同一物质基础。棕榈枝或犬的关联也见于特定传统，但不能据此推定所有社群具有同样做法。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 在约鲁巴地区，铁匠、猎人及现代使用机械的人都可能与奥贡建立宗教联系。海地奥古、巴西奥贡等离散形态各有历史；共同的铁与行动主题，不等于其仪式和人物性格完全相同。

en.name: Ogun
en.title: Orisha of iron, paths, and dangerous skills

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Ogun is the Yoruba orisha associated with iron, smithing, hunting, and warfare. His significance also reaches people whose livelihoods depend on metal tools. The same force that clears land and makes cultivation possible can inflict injury, so describing him simply as a war god misses important dimensions.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: One narrative makes Ogun the opener of a passage through vegetation that blocks the other orishas. A separate cycle associated with Ire describes his catastrophic misunderstanding of a community’s ritual silence, followed by remorse and withdrawal into the earth. These variable stories do not form a single fixed biography.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: Blades, hoes, hammers, and other iron implements identify Ogun through the shared material basis of production and violence. Palm fronds and associations with dogs occur in particular traditions. Such details require local context rather than assumptions that every community uses the same objects or practices.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Smiths, hunters, drivers, and other users of machinery may relate to Ogun in Yoruba settings. Atlantic traditions developed figures such as Haitian Ogou and Brazilian Ogum through their own histories. Shared iron imagery and themes of action do not make their ceremonies or personalities interchangeable.

figures.name: 尚戈
figures.title: 与奥约王权相连的雷霆奥里沙

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 尚戈是约鲁巴雷电奥里沙，与奥约王朝及一位被神化的阿拉芬君王紧密相连。口传常把他列为早期君主，但谱系与历史年代不能等同考古定论。其形象把王权的威严、雷暴力量与领导者承担的风险联结起来。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 一些奥约叙事讲述尚戈驾驭雷电，却因力量失控或政治危机离开王位；关于其死亡、消失与神化的说法并不一致。追随者宣告他并未真正死去，雷声成为其持续在场的证据。奥雅、奥舒恩与奥巴等伴侣的故事，也各有地方叙事脉络。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 双刃斧形舞杖奥谢尚戈是著名标识，红白配色及被解释为雷石的石器也常出现。斧刃象征雷霆威势，不宜把所有持斧雕像都未经语境核实地认作尚戈。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 尚戈崇敬连接奥约历史、专属祭司传统与表演艺术，并随大西洋迁徙传入美洲。巴西尚戈与加勒比昌戈的名称相近，但王权记忆、音乐和地方宗教结构各有重组，不能以一套习惯覆盖所有地区。

en.name: Shango
en.title: Thunder orisha associated with Oyo kingship

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Shango is the Yoruba thunder orisha closely associated with Oyo kingship and a deified ruler bearing the title Alaafin. Oral genealogies place him among early kings, but their chronology is not straightforward archaeological fact. His image joins royal authority, storm power, and the dangers of leadership.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: Oyo narratives variously describe Shango wielding lightning, losing control of destructive power, or leaving his throne amid political conflict. Accounts of death, disappearance, and deification disagree. Followers declare that he has not truly died, while stories involving Oya, Oshun, and Oba follow their own local narrative paths.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: The double-axe form of the ose Shango dance staff is especially recognizable. Red and white combinations and objects interpreted as thunderstones also occur. The axe evokes thunderous authority, but an axe-bearing sculpture cannot reliably be identified without its provenance and the community’s own explanation.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Shango devotion links Oyo history with priestly traditions and performance arts, and traveled across the Atlantic. Brazilian Xango and Caribbean Chango developed within different religious and political settings. Similar names do not imply identical music, royal memories, ritual organization, or relationships with other sacred figures.

figures.name: 奥舒恩
figures.title: 奥孙河与生命繁荣的奥里沙

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 奥舒恩是与尼日利亚奥孙河紧密相连的约鲁巴奥里沙，常关联淡水、生育、吸引力与物质繁荣。她并非仅供装饰的爱情女神；谈判能力、生命维系和女性权威同样重要，奥绍博的河流与圣林使其具有具体地理归属。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 一类广泛流传的故事说，奉命经营世界的十七位奥里沙中，其他成员排斥唯一的女性奥舒恩，结果工作失败，土地失去生机。至高者指出缺少她就不能成功；众人请她参与后，秩序才得恢复。不同讲述对人数与情节安排仍可能有所调整。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 流动淡水、扇、镜与黄铜饰物常用于辨识，黄色或金色在若干离散传统尤其醒目。蜂蜜的甜味可指吸引与调解，但颜色和供物并不是跨地区不变的清单。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 奥孙—奥绍博圣林及年度节庆体现河流、城市历史与宗教共同体的关系，而非抽象的自然崇拜。美洲奥舒恩传统另有地方发展；观看公开节庆不等于获准进入所有圣地或记录一切活动。

en.name: Oshun
en.title: Orisha of the Osun River and flourishing life

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Oshun is a Yoruba orisha closely connected with the Osun River in Nigeria, fresh water, fertility, attraction, and prosperity. She is not merely a decorative love goddess. Negotiation, sustaining life, and feminine authority are equally important, while Osogbo gives her traditions a specific geographical grounding.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: A widely told account describes seventeen orishas sent to organize the world. The others exclude Oshun, the only woman, and their undertaking fails as life withers. The supreme being explains that success requires her participation. Inviting her restores possibility, although numbers and details vary between tellings.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: Fresh water, fans, mirrors, and brass ornaments are frequent identifying features. Yellow and gold are especially prominent in some diaspora traditions. Honey’s sweetness can suggest attraction and mediation, but neither colors nor offerings constitute a universal checklist that applies unchanged to every community or historical setting.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: The Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove and annual festival connect a river, urban history, and a living religious community. They should not be reduced to generic nature worship. American traditions developed locally, and access to a public festival does not authorize entry into every sacred place or unrestricted recording.

figures.name: 埃舒
figures.title: 沟通、选择与歧义的奥里沙

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 埃舒是约鲁巴传统中与传递信息、交换、道路和出人意料的转折相连的奥里沙，在神人与占卜沟通中具有重要位置。他会制造麻烦，也揭露理解的局限；不能把这种复杂角色直接翻译成基督宗教的魔鬼或纯粹恶神。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 著名的双色帽故事说，埃舒从两个朋友之间走过，两人各见帽子的一种颜色，争论对方说谎，甚至破坏友谊。埃舒再揭示帽子的两面，显出双方都把有限观察当成全貌。帽子的具体配色和冲突程度因版本而异，重点是视角与判断。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 路口、门槛和传话的动作比单一外貌更能说明其位置，部分造像具有特别的发式或持杖。强调歧义并不等于说他毫无规范，而是提醒人们沟通需要谨慎。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 约鲁巴埃舒与丰人莱格巴、美洲埃莱瓜等存在历史联系，却不能未经说明就互作别名。殖民时代的魔鬼化翻译长期影响公众理解，介绍时应保留当地称呼以及各传统自己的角色区分。

en.name: Eshu
en.title: Orisha of communication, choice, and ambiguity

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Eshu is a Yoruba orisha associated with messages, exchange, roads, and unexpected turns. He occupies an important position in communication between humans and sacred powers, including divination. Creating trouble can expose failures of understanding; translating this complex role as the Christian devil seriously distorts its meaning.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: In the famous two-colored hat story, Eshu walks between two friends. Each sees a different side and insists that the other is lying, threatening their friendship. Revealing both sides exposes their incomplete perspectives. Colors and the severity of the quarrel differ, but limited judgment remains central.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: Crossroads, thresholds, and acts of carrying messages explain Eshu’s position better than a single standardized appearance. Particular sculptures feature distinctive hairstyles or staffs. Emphasizing ambiguity does not make him an embodiment of unrestricted chaos; it highlights how interpretation and communication require attention to context.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Yoruba Eshu has historical connections with Fon Legba and American figures such as Elegua, but these names are not automatically interchangeable. Colonial demonizing translations continue to shape popular misunderstandings. Introductions should retain local names and respect the distinctions maintained within each living religious tradition.

figures.name: 阿南西
figures.title: 阿坎故事中的蜘蛛智谋者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 阿南西在加纳等地的阿坎口述传统中以蜘蛛或兼具人形的智谋者出现，其名与蜘蛛有关。他有妻儿，会饥饿、贪心和出丑，不能一概称为至高神。阿南西故事以家庭、交易和权力为舞台，既赞赏机智，也嘲笑自作聪明。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 购买天空之神尼亚梅的故事时，阿南西须交出难以捕获的动物。他用比长短的争论把蟒蛇绑在木杆上，用假装避雨的办法把黄蜂诱入容器，又以陷阱对付豹子。完成条件后，故事获得阿南西之名；猎物清单与妻子的参与随讲述而变化。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 蜘蛛、多足形象、绳索和机巧的容器常让人想到阿南西，但他也会像普通人一样行动。判断关键是计谋及其反转，而不是把每一只蜘蛛都当成他的神圣化身。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 阿坎语中的阿南西故事属于活跃的讲述体裁，与听众回应及讲者发挥相连。大西洋奴隶贸易使其进入加勒比等地，形成阿南西、南希等新传统；这些版本不能抹去加纳阿坎社会的具体根基。

en.name: Anansi
en.title: Spider trickster of Akan storytelling

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Anansi appears in Akan oral traditions of Ghana and neighboring areas as a spider or a figure combining spider and human characteristics. He has a family, becomes hungry, cheats, and fails. Calling him simply a supreme deity obscures stories concerned with households, bargaining, status, and comic reversal.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: To buy the sky deity Nyame’s stories, Anansi must capture formidable creatures. He ties a python to a pole through a length comparison, lures hornets into a container by pretending to offer shelter, and traps a leopard. Required creatures and his wife’s contribution vary across performances.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: Spider forms, multiple legs, ropes, and cleverly used containers can suggest Anansi, although he often behaves like an ordinary person. His identifying feature is the ingenious scheme and its possible reversal. Not every spider image represents him, and not every story celebrates his behavior.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Akan Ananse storytelling is a living performance genre shaped by narrators and audience participation. The Atlantic slave trade carried related tales into Caribbean societies, where Anancy and Nancy traditions developed. Their creativity should be recognized without erasing the specific Akan settings from which these narrative histories emerged.

figures.name: 尼亚梅
figures.title: 阿坎传统中的天空与至高者

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 尼亚梅是阿坎传统中与天空及至高创造力量相连的名称，在不同语言地区与其他尊称的关系有所变化。他不是全西非共享的同一位天神。阿散蒂等阿坎社会的赞称、俗语和叙事，为理解其权威提供了具体文化背景。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 在阿南西购买故事的叙事里，故事最初属于尼亚梅。蜘蛛提出交易时，他要求难以捕获的蟒蛇、豹子和黄蜂等作为代价，并以此设置几乎不可能的考验。阿南西逐项交付后，他承认交易，让故事以蜘蛛之名流传；部分版本另加森林精灵。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 天空的高度和故事的最初所有权突显其权威。名为杰尼亚梅的阿丁克拉符号常被解释为唯有上帝，表达至高者的独一地位，并不是对神身体外貌的画像。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 阿坎语言和基督宗教翻译也使用尼亚梅相关称呼，使传统与近现代宗教语汇产生交叠。分析时应说明讨论的是哪种讲述或用法，不能把教会中的词义直接等同所有前殖民时期的观念。

en.name: Nyame
en.title: Sky and supreme being in Akan traditions

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Nyame is an Akan name associated with the sky and supreme creative power. Its relationship to other divine titles varies across language communities and contexts. Nyame is not a single sky god shared identically throughout West Africa; Asante praise expressions, proverbs, and narratives provide more specific cultural grounding.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: In the tale of Anansi purchasing stories, Nyame initially owns them. He sets an apparently impossible price involving creatures such as a python, leopard, and hornets. When Anansi delivers the required captives, Nyame acknowledges the transaction and releases the stories under the spider’s name; some versions add a forest spirit.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: The height of the sky and ownership of stories express Nyame’s authority. The adinkra design called Gye Nyame is commonly interpreted as except God or only God, affirming divine supremacy. It is a symbolic statement, not a portrait of the deity’s physical body or face.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Names related to Nyame also occur in Akan Christian translation and contemporary religious speech, creating historical overlaps in vocabulary. Interpretation should identify the particular narrative or usage involved. A meaning established in a church translation cannot simply be projected onto every earlier Akan religious understanding.

figures.name: 阿萨塞娅
figures.title: 阿散蒂阿坎传统的土地力量

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 阿萨塞娅是阿散蒂等阿坎传统中的大地神圣力量，名字中的娅对应星期四出生的女性名。她与土地的生产力、死者归土及人的道德责任相连。芳蒂等地可见阿萨塞埃富娅等称呼，关联星期五，不宜把日期统一。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 与阿南西不同，阿萨塞娅并不以一组固定冒险最为人熟知。公开记述更常描写人们在耕种前向大地致意、在郑重誓言中请土地见证，以及把埋葬理解为回归土地。她的叙事位置由播种、收获和死亡的往复显现，不应另编一场创造万物的战役。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 耕地、土壤与承载生命的地面是核心线索，而不是固定动物或统一神像。阿散蒂一些地方以星期四限制下田劳动，提示土地具有应受尊重的时间与边界。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 土地信仰与阿坎地方共同体的农业、祖先观念及土地责任相联。休耕日和称谓因地区而异，现代实践也会改变。她不是非洲所有大地母神的总称，更不能被当作各地习俗完全相同的证明。

en.name: Asase Yaa
en.title: Sacred earth in Asante Akan traditions

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Asase Yaa personifies sacred earth in Asante and other Akan settings. Yaa is a female Thursday day-name. Her associations include agricultural fertility, the dead returning to earth, and human obligations. Fante contexts may instead use Asase Efua, linked with Friday, so the weekday should not be universalized.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: Unlike Anansi, Asase Yaa is not chiefly known through a fixed cycle of adventures. Public accounts more often describe acknowledging earth before cultivation, invoking it in solemn oaths, and understanding burial as a return to the ground. Her narrative significance emerges through planting, harvest, death, and continuing responsibility.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: Cultivated ground, soil, and the surface sustaining life are more useful identifiers than a standard animal or statue. Some Asante communities restrict farm work on Thursday. Such observances mark earth’s respected times and limits, but should not be turned into instructions supposedly binding on all Akan people.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Earth traditions connect agriculture, ancestors, and responsibilities to land within particular Akan communities. Names and days of observance differ geographically, and contemporary practices change. Asase Yaa is not a collective label for every African earth mother, nor evidence that different societies share identical institutions or beliefs.

figures.name: 阿索
figures.title: 阿南西故事中的妻子与计谋伙伴

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 阿索是部分阿坎阿南西故事中蜘蛛的妻子，名字在转写中也作阿苏等形式。她首先是具有家庭身份的故事人物，并非固定神系中的女神。不同讲者赋予她的篇幅不等，有时她提供关键判断，有时只是家庭情节的参与者。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 在购买尼亚梅故事的一些版本里，阿南西把困难条件告诉阿索，她帮助把捕捉强敌改造成可操作的骗局。针对蟒蛇的办法，是假称夫妻正在争论蛇与木杆谁长，诱使蛇伸直，再把它绑住。各版本分配建议者角色不同，不能把每项计谋都归给她。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 阿索没有广为公认的神圣徽记，通常由妻子身份、家中商议和提出办法的对白辨识。木杆、绳索只是相关故事道具，并不是她在阿坎宗教中的专属法器。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 关注阿索能看见蜘蛛成功背后的协作，也能比较讲述如何分配家庭中的智慧与功劳。不能据一篇童书概括阿坎妇女地位；采录、翻译与儿童改写都可能增删她的台词和作用，需要区分文本版本。

en.name: Aso
en.title: Anansi’s wife and partner in planning

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Aso, also transcribed in other forms such as Asɔ, is Anansi’s wife in some Akan tales. She is primarily a character within a storytelling household, not an established goddess in a fixed pantheon. Narrators give her different degrees of agency, from decisive adviser to supporting family participant.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: In some versions of the purchase of Nyame’s stories, Anansi consults Aso about impossible demands. A python is tricked through a supposed marital disagreement over whether it is longer than a pole, then stretched out and bound. Attribution of this advice varies, so not every scheme should automatically be credited to her.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: Aso has no widely standardized sacred emblem. Her identity emerges through her relationship to Anansi, domestic discussion, and practical dialogue. The pole and ropes belong to particular narrative situations; they should not be presented as established personal ritual implements or evidence of a separate cult.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Attending to Aso reveals cooperation behind the spider’s apparent individual triumph and invites comparison of how tellers distribute intelligence and credit. A single children’s adaptation cannot establish Akan women’s social position. Collection, translation, and rewriting may expand or remove her dialogue and practical contribution.

figures.name: 恩蒂库马
figures.title: 看破智慧罐难题的阿南西之子

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 恩蒂库马是若干阿坎阿南西故事中蜘蛛的儿子，名字有多种拉丁字母转写。他不是掌管智慧的神，而是以孩子身份显露父亲盲点的人物。其作用依赖亲子关系：年长者自认掌握一切，却可能需要听取年轻人的朴素建议。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 阿南西想把天下智慧装进罐里，独占后藏到树顶。他把罐子挂在胸前，攀树时不断被挡住；树下的恩蒂库马建议把罐移到背后。蜘蛛发现自称拥有全部智慧仍会被孩子提醒，恼怒或震惊之下使罐子破裂，智慧散入人间，结尾细节随版本变化。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 胸前妨碍攀爬的罐子、树干与孩子的简单建议构成辨识场景。智慧不再由单一长者垄断是故事的反讽，而不是宣称恩蒂库马拥有一套固定的神圣权能。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 智慧罐故事在阿坎口传及世界各地改写中广为流通，儿子名字有时被省略。比较版本应注意罐如何破碎、智慧如何传播，以及孩子是否具名；这些变化影响道德重点，不能当成无关紧要的装饰。

en.name: Ntikuma
en.title: Anansi’s son who sees the wisdom-pot problem

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Ntikuma is a son of Anansi in a number of Akan tales, with several spellings in transcription. He is not a god governing wisdom. His narrative importance lies in the family relationship: a father claiming superior knowledge encounters an insight supplied by a younger and apparently less authoritative person.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: Anansi collects wisdom in a pot and tries to hide it high in a tree, but the pot strapped against his chest obstructs climbing. Ntikuma suggests moving it behind him. Discovering that complete wisdom still requires a child’s advice, Anansi loses the pot, releasing wisdom; the precise ending varies.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: The obstructing pot, tree trunk, and child’s practical suggestion form the recognizable scene. Its irony challenges any elder’s claim to monopolize understanding. These narrative objects should not be converted into divine attributes, and Ntikuma should not be assigned supernatural offices unsupported by the tale.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: The wisdom-pot tale circulates in Akan performance and international adaptations, sometimes without naming the son. Comparing versions requires attention to how the vessel breaks, how wisdom spreads, and whether the child receives credit. Such variations shape the lesson rather than merely decorating an otherwise identical story.

figures.name: 奥塞博
figures.title: 被阿南西智取的故事豹子

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 奥塞博是阿南西购买故事的一类阿坎叙事中具名的豹子，名字也与阿坎语豹子称呼相关。他是危险的动物对手，并非全西非崇拜的豹神。其强壮和利爪抬高任务难度，让弱小蜘蛛的计谋显得格外出人意料。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 尼亚梅索取的代价包括豹子时，阿南西在其经过的路上设置覆有枝叶的深坑。豹子落入后，蜘蛛假意营救，要它借助木棍或固定四肢以便拉起，乘机将它捆住带走。救助变成捕获是这段故事的核心，具体捆绑方法则随讲述有所变化。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 斑点皮毛、利爪、陷坑和假营救构成主要线索。豹子体现体力优势在特定局面中的失效，但不能因此声称阿坎文化始终轻视豹子，其他语境可赋予它威严。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 奥塞博主要应放在阿南西的交易故事中介绍，而不是添入并不存在的统一神族谱系。部分简写本只说豹子而不保留名字；把名字恢复出来有助于辨认具体传统，但不代表角色必有独立祭祀。

en.name: Osebo
en.title: The leopard outwitted in Anansi’s story bargain

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Osebo is the named leopard in a family of Akan accounts about Anansi purchasing stories. The name is related to the Akan word for leopard. He is a dangerous animal opponent, not a universal West African leopard deity; his strength makes the small spider’s challenge seem particularly formidable.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: When Nyame’s price includes a leopard, Anansi prepares a concealed pit along its route. After Osebo falls in, the spider pretends to help him escape, using sticks or instructions about securing his limbs to gain control. Rescue becomes capture, although the exact mechanics of binding differ between tellings.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: Spotted fur, claws, a concealed pit, and a deceptive rescue identify this episode. The leopard demonstrates how bodily advantage can fail under particular circumstances. This does not mean Akan societies always disparage leopards, since other contexts can associate the animal with authority and formidable dignity.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Osebo belongs within the narrative setting of Anansi’s bargain rather than an invented genealogy of gods. Some shortened retellings retain only an unnamed leopard. Preserving his name helps identify a specific story tradition, but a named character does not necessarily possess an independent cult or worship.

figures.name: 毛伊
figures.title: 奥特亚罗瓦毛利叙事中的钓岛英雄

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 毛伊是许多波利尼西亚传统中的英雄，本条聚焦奥特亚罗瓦新西兰的毛利版本。毛伊提基提基阿塔朗加的长名关联母亲塔朗加及发髻故事。他兼具神奇祖先与顽皮智谋者特征，不能把夏威夷等岛群的家世全部并入。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 毛利的一类钓岛故事说，兄长不愿带毛伊出海，他偷偷藏进船中，再用祖先穆里朗加费努阿的颚骨作钩钓起巨鱼。兄长们急于切割鱼身，使其形成崎岖地貌；北岛因此称毛伊之鱼。南岛与独木舟的关联另有讲述，不能把全部地理细节视为通说。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 颚骨鱼钩、独木舟和巨鱼是此版本的主要标识，套住太阳则属于另一著名故事。现代商业角色的纹身与造型是改编设计，不等于毛利各部族共享的形象。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 毛利部族与家族保有各自的谱系、地名解释和讲述权威。钓岛叙事连接祖先与土地，不只是供娱乐的冒险；与夏威夷或汤加毛伊比较时，应明确岛群、讲者背景及叙事之间的实际差别。

en.name: Maui
en.title: Fishing-up hero in Aotearoa Maori narratives

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Maui appears across Polynesian traditions, but this entry centers on Maori accounts from Aotearoa New Zealand. The name Maui-tikitiki-a-Taranga recalls his mother Taranga and a topknot narrative. He combines extraordinary ancestry with mischievous ingenuity; Hawaiian or other island genealogies should not be added indiscriminately to this version.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: In a Maori fishing account, Maui hides in his brothers’ canoe and uses the ancestral jawbone of Muri-ranga-whenua as a hook. He raises an immense fish, which his brothers cut prematurely, producing rough terrain. The North Island is called Te Ika-a-Maui; associated canoe geography varies among traditions.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: The jawbone hook, canoe, and immense fish distinguish this narrative. Snaring the sun belongs to another celebrated Maui episode. Tattoos, body shapes, and accessories in contemporary commercial adaptations are creative designs, not a reliable collective portrait authorized by all Maori iwi or other Polynesian communities.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Maori iwi and families maintain particular genealogies, place associations, and storytelling authority. Fishing-up narratives connect ancestors and land rather than functioning merely as entertainment. Comparisons with Hawaiian or Tongan Maui accounts should identify island setting, narrator background, and meaningful differences instead of constructing one seamless pan-Polynesian biography.

figures.name: 希娜
figures.title: 夏威夷月中制布者与相关女性名号

sections.title: 身份与来历
sections.text: 希娜是波利尼西亚多地女性人物使用的名字，本条只介绍夏威夷公开叙事中的月中希娜及毛伊母亲的相关版本。名字相同不证明所有人物原本是一人，也不能把塔希提、库克群岛或毛利希娜的家世直接拼接进来。

sections.title: 主要叙事
sections.text: 一些夏威夷讲述把月面明暗解释为希娜及其制布工具，呈现月中的树皮布制作者。另一类毛伊套太阳故事写母亲希娜制作的卡帕布来不及晒干，儿子于是约束飞快运行的太阳，使白昼延长。两组材料可以并读，但不必强行写成连续生平。

sections.title: 象征与辨识
sections.text: 月面、木槌、砧板与卡帕布是公开故事中可辨认的线索。卡帕是经过处理和捶打的树皮布，不是织机织出的棉布；劳动细节比笼统的月亮女神标签更具体。

sections.title: 流传与文化语境
sections.text: 夏威夷语中的希娜相关复合名可指不同人物，其关系应由具体文本说明。月亮、女性劳动与谱系在不同岛群有不同联系；旅游改写常合并同名人物，阅读时须保留夏威夷版本及其边界。

en.name: Hina
en.title: Hawaiian lunar kapa maker and related female names

sections.title: Identity and Origins
sections.text: Hina names female figures in many Polynesian societies. This entry concerns publicly circulated Hawaiian accounts of a lunar Hina and versions naming Maui’s mother Hina. A shared name does not prove a single original person, and genealogies from Tahiti, the Cook Islands, or Maori traditions should remain distinct.

sections.title: Principal Narratives
sections.text: Some Hawaiian accounts read the moon’s markings as Hina with her kapa-making equipment. In another narrative family, Maui’s mother cannot dry her kapa because daylight passes too quickly, prompting him to restrain the sun. These materials can be compared without forcing them into one continuous life story.

sections.title: Symbols and Recognition
sections.text: The moon, wooden beaters, an anvil, and kapa identify publicly told episodes. Kapa is barkcloth produced through processing and beating, not cotton cloth woven on a loom. Recognizing this labor gives more cultural substance than attaching only a generalized label such as moon goddess.

sections.title: Transmission and Cultural Context
sections.text: Hawaiian compound names containing Hina may identify different figures whose relationships require specific textual evidence. Lunar associations, women’s work, and genealogy intersect differently across island groups. Tourist retellings often merge namesakes, so a responsible account preserves its Hawaiian setting and acknowledges the limits of the selected version.

figures.name: 唐加罗瓦
figures.title: 毛利版本中的海洋与水族祖先

sections.title: 身份与来历
